Name: rittik bora
Title: Previledge
Content:
PRIVILEGE

A palace,
built behind fragile walls,
a crown passed down
upon stones we never laid.

We inherited
the path,
but not the eyes
to question it—
the crown,
not the spine to carry it.

Empty footsteps
wandering through its halls,
until the mirror asks:
who is walking?

Heirs of the past,
or architects of the future?

Let the mirror strip the mask,
until nothing borrowed remains.

A privilege we pass along—
a voice
for those who come next,
not a path to follow,
but a compass to guide,
a gate left open,
and the courage
to lay their own stones.

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Courage, resilience, defiance, rebellion, dionysus, following your own path, questioning people's judgements.
Title: Dionysus.
Content:
I'll change my career path a million times
I'll eat chicken and eggs if that's what I want
I'll transfer colleges and wear crop tops
I'll go alone to places if I have no one else
I'll eat alone every day if that's what it is
Your gaze, which used to imprint on my soul,
Even after you looked away, caused me unease
A hole burned into my being by your judgement
Now stare at me all you want, and I don't care

Dionysus took me with him to paradise
Have I drunk from the well, or have you?
I'll get intoxicated and dance in public if I want
Because we're on a floating rock in space
Were you there to wipe my tears when I cried?
Did you ask me to eat when I used to skip meals?
Did you hold my hand in the heat while I was alone?
And if not, don't ask me the 6 Ws, let me live
If I can live life my own way, turning to ash is okay

Your momentary, fleeting gaze full of judgement
Used to etch itself on my soul. But the truth is,
I'm the one who has stayed for it all, have you?
I'll stay loyal to the unending flame inside me
That kept it bright for my eyes even in the dark.
My resilience, which saved me over and over.
I'm no longer locked in the bars of your gaze.
So turn up the music, and let's get drunk tonight
Because I'm my own slave, and I do what I like.

Name: Naina Pandita
Title: The Rain and You
Content:
The Rain and You

I sat silently watching the rain,
As water trickled down the drain.
Sitting alone, sipping hot tea,
I looked up, and your face I did see.

The photograph of the scene
Was not something from a dream.
It remained imprinted on my mind,
A memory of you, forever well-defined.

Rain kept falling the next day,
Thinking of you made me sway.
Memories of a happy life—
Now I am no longer your wife.

Rain may come and go,
The wind may or may not blow.
I will always remember you
And all the times we went through.

We may not be together now,
A deep line fills my brow.
Every time I see the rain,
Missing you brings back the pain.

Name: Divya Iyer
Title: Letting them fly alone
Content:
You watched him pack his school bag, and every cell in your body wanted to intervene. No pencil box. Wrong notebook. A single sock ..one solitary sock, inexplicably, for a reason science may never determine .. placed gently on top like a garnish.
You stood there gripping your coffee like it was a stress ball, reciting the mantra of modern motherhood: let them fail young, while the stakes are pencil boxes and not resumes.
You had read the articles. You had saved the reels. "Natural consequences build resilience," said a woman on Instagram whose children appeared to own matching stationery. And also.. let's be honest..you were, frankly, exhausted. Some days your parenting philosophy is deeply researched child development theory. Some days it's I cannot fold one more thing.
So you said nothing. You let him walk out the door with his chaos fully intact, his bag zipped over what could only be described as a cry for help.
And then ..plot twist .. he came home thriving.
He announced, quite pleased with himself, that he had forgotten his tiffin and eaten his friend's extra roti instead. Told it like a triumph. Like he had hacked the system. Like he had discovered barter economy before fractions.
You waited for the lesson. The remorse. The promise to never forget again.
Instead he said, "Can we make extra roti tomorrow? In case someone forgets theirs. We could call it the emergency backup roti."
Sir, you are the emergency.
It's not a grand, cinematic moment where you release your child into the world with tearful wisdom. It's standing in the doorway at 7:40 AM, physically biting your tongue, watching a boy walk into the world armed with one sock and a dream.
And here's the real surprise.. it worked. Not because he suffered some great lesson. But because he handled it. No tears, no drama, no rescue mission from HQ. He forgot his tiffin, he found a roti, he came home taller somehow. Somewhere between the wrong notebook and the borrowed lunch, my baby learned to solve his own problems. Loudly, chaotically, and with zero remorse.. but on his own.
So no, I didn't fix the bag. I'm not going to fix tomorrow's either. Because the backpack isn't the thing being packed here. It's the person carrying it. Every forgotten pencil box is a small deposit into an account called "I'll figure it out" and trust me, that account pays better interest than anything I audit at work.
He will remember the tiffin tomorrow. Or he won't, and he will live on borrowed rotis a while longer. Either way, the boy came home happy, fed, and unbearably proud of himself. And I came home a slightly cooler, slightly calmer mom who let it happen.
Letting go isn't about trusting the bag. It's about trusting the boy. Turns out, he is more ready than I am.
Baby steps. For both of us.

Name: Dr Bolie Therattil
Title: In the Quiet, I Find Myself
Content:
In the Quiet, I Find Myself
It is not loneliness that I seek,
but the silence where I can finally hear my own soul.

When the noise of the world falls away,
when applause fades and expectations grow silent,
I begin to see my path with clearer eyes.
I no longer need to be understood by everyone,
nor validated by every voice around me.

I am learning that some journeys
are meant to be walked quietly.

I may be only one small voice
in this vast and restless world,
but this life is mine to shape.
Every step I take, every dream I carry,
every mistake that teaches me,
becomes a part of the person I am becoming.

I have learned not to wait for someone
to light the fire within me.
There is a silent strength that rises
when we choose to believe in ourselves—
when we stop looking outward
and begin listening inward.

In independence, I find clarity.
In silence, I find perspective.
In solitude, I find strength.

Perhaps peace was never meant
to be found in the loudest rooms
or in the approval of restless crowds.

Perhaps peace is something we build—
slowly, quietly, within ourselves.

And sometimes,
the most powerful thing we can do
is step away from the noise,
stand quietly in our own light,
and continue becoming
who we were meant to be.
Dr Bolie Therattil

Name: Nisha RG
Theme: Mother’s love for her son, loss
Title: PAVITRA ,The Mother
Content:
SHORT STORY -1 
PAVITRA, The Mother
Pavitra woke up to the sound of plates falling on the floor. She found it difficult to open her eyes as it was injured and for some time She had blurred vision. The backside of the head was throbbing with a sharp pain. Her husband  Sagar under the influence of alcohol hits her daily.  Pavitra walked towards the kitchen wobbling her feet. She saw her husband pouring dosa batter on the cast iron skillet. He saw her and smiled at her and said “ Pavitra go and take a bath. Breakfast is ready. I will be late in the evening. I have prepared the lunch also . You can take rest for the whole day.  He smiled at her again”. Pavitra was accustomed to his strange behaviour in the morning. He smiles, talks and behaves as if nothing happened on the previous night.  She sat on a stool and had some water from the pitcher. The cold water made her inside cool. But her busted and bruised lip gave a burning pain. It started raining outside. The pitter-patter of raindrops falling on the asbestos sheet was jarring.Pavitra felt all the more annoyed and frustrated. Sitting inside the hall She could see the climbers in the Serpent groove and the Indian Copal tree with its oblong-shaped fruits glazed with the rainwater. The priest Kurukkal walking with an umbrella and a bronze uruli or the round bowl to his home after closing the temple is a man who gave Anandu and Pavitra a refugee in their house whenever Sagar dismisses them from the house at midnight after the squabbles. The strong winds blowing through the coconut tree made the tree sway. Her mind was also raining inside with emotions that could not be fathomed with words. She looked inside and saw her ten-year-old son Anandu sleeping.She tried to remember what was the fight for. She had lost hearing ability in her left ear after a heavy blow from her husband. Pavitra finds it difficult to live with him. But she is devoid of choices. Her parents are dead, only brother is married and living happily with whatever they have. Many times Pavitra contemplated suicide but she could not bring herself to kill her son. Her son  Anandu is the only lifeline for whom she bears everything. Her husband Sagar is a doubting husband on top of that an alcoholic. Post-marriage first two months were problem-free. In the third month, they moved to a rental house, and from there onwards her nightmares started. It was a two-bedroom house with a false ceiling, dampness in the basement, broken water pipe, fragmented window panes, bedroom doors without latches, walls of the house with vertical cracks, and bathrooms without faucets. She cannot understand what made her husband move to this place. She had to complain constantly about water shortage. He made her draw up water from the well. He needs breakfast and a sumptuous lunch and not a simple lunch. He buys fish, poultry, provision and vegetables.But he never gives a single penny for her. She was forbidden to go out, to talk to people. If she violates any of his rules he will beat her up mercilessly. In between she became pregnant. But he in his drunken booze state kicked her stomach three times. Pavitra felt a sharp pain radiating from her stomach. She vomited. Her body was trembling inside out.She sensed the hotness of blood flowing inside her panties to her pyjamas. She screamed calling for help. Even then he smacked her thighs. Her neighbours came to her rescue. By the time they wiggled his iron hand from her hair, she was unconscious. She was taken to the hospital by her neighbours. She lost her baby. The doctor complained about the incident to the police. He was taken into custody for domestic violence and hurting a pregnant woman. Her parents were alive then. They took her with them.But her mother-in-law came to her and cried with folded hands to invalidate the complaint. She and her parents succumbed to her request. After three days came to her house, talked to her parents promised them he would not harm her but would love her and take good care of her. She reluctantly went with him. After two years She delivered Anandu in a government hospital while Sagar boozed in a local toddy parlour. Her parents paid the hospital bill and took her with her Son to their house. She was under postpartum care for three months. Post-pregnancy She had to face extreme challenges in her life. Sagar under the influence of alcohol many times tried to hit the baby, and broke all the glass plates and cups. She had to face his whacking, punching and pounding daily She was hospitalised several times. On complaining to the Police She met with another monster in the hands of a womanising Sub Inspector of Police. She had to complain to Panchayath President Rekha about his outrageous behaviour phone calls and chats that the Sub inspector whenever sees her on the road or market unexpectedly had to face his ruthlessness and brutality in public. But nobody dared to support her and go against him. She silently endured everything for her Son Anandu. For some time She went on a emotional roller coaster ride. She took a deep breath. Now at the moment, she stares at the floor thinking what to do about her life. How to get rid of her husband? Yesterday the fight was for a petty matter wherein she has no role. He bought fish from the stall and kept the satchel with fish outside Pavitra’s tailoring shop. She was busily stitching alongside her son doing his homework. The moment  Sagar came inside the shop to take a newspaper to wrap the bottle of brandy that he bought from the beverage shop, two street dogs had their time with the fish. When Sagar came out of the shop, he saw the dogs gobbling fish from the satchel. He took a stone to throw them. But those two dogs took the satchel and fish with them. He stormed inside her shop and gave a hit on the wall and said” How can you be irresponsible you shag? Don’t you see the dogs who took the fish ? “. Pavitra and her son were unaware of the happening outside the shop. Her son said, “Father what are you saying? We didn’t know you bought fish and you kept it outside the shop”. “What did you say ? You didn’t know? Your Son is questioning me,” said Sagar and went towards him to hit him. Pavitra pulled her Son to her side and said “Please don’t hit him. He didn’t question you. What he said is true. We were unaware of it. Now Sagar this is my tailoring shop. This is on rent. I should give these clothes stitched tomorrow. You please go home. If you want fish curry to eat. You have the previous day’s fish curry sufficient for you”. Please don’t create a scene here. People are watching. Please Sagar please”. Sagar left the shop immediately. After completing her stitching work for the day they both closed the shop and started walking towards their home. Yet on reaching home Pavitra and Son had to run for their life because he came running towards them with a sickle. Her neighbours came to their rescue again. But her husband started saying that she had slept with those men and this made them mad at Sagar. Pavitra was so shocked to hear those words. Her son was listening too. She cried with folded hands. One of the men said,” Sagar mind your language. If you say anything unwanted we will not stand here dumb. You will be whacked to death”. Sagar instantly spit on him. This led to a fight. Pavitra and her son start to scream. The women came and stopped the men somehow and led them back home. Sagar was writhing in pain. He was so angry that he broke the glass plates, tumblers and earthen pitcher. When they went inside the hall was full of broken pieces of plates, pots and a pool of water. He grabbed Pavitra by her hair and started hitting her with his hands forcefully. She could feel the pain of the hair pulling out from her scalp. He hit her head with his fist. Pavitra started to feel dizzy. He gave a hard slap on her face.Her lips were torn, and she spitted blood from her mouth. Her Son seeing all this started wailing loudly. She somehow got up. But her body was shaking. She went towards her son and hugged him. Sagar took the liquor bottle from the kitchen shelf and went outside. Pavitra took her son to bed and she passed out. Sitting on the stool she saw Sagar coming towards her smiling as if nothing happened. Her son woke up and went to the washroom. Pavitra stood up but she did not feel steady. Her phone started ringing from the bedroom which was intact inside her bag. She knew it would be one of her customers. She got up and somehow went towards her bag and took the phone but it stopped ringing. Pavitra called back to the number. A lady took the phone and said,” Pavitra are you alright? This is me Rekha. I need my blouse today. Is it possible to stitch my blouse and give it to me by evening Pavitra?”. “ Rekha Sister I am not feeling good. Sagar hit me yesterday. Can I give the blouse stitched by morning 10 am? “asked Pavitra. “All alright then tomorrow in the morning I want my blouse. At what time should I come to fetch it? asked Renuka “Maybe by 9:30,” said Pavitra. And the phone became dead at the other end. Her Son went to the kitchen came back sat on a chair and stared at the dirty floor. He was silent. Pavitra looked at him. She wants to ask him if he is alright. But she knew the question itself was ironical. After some moments of silence between them, her Son looked at her and asked,” Amma I feel so tired. Amma Can we escape this place? Can we escape from father? I am really scared of him Amma. I hate him. Please Amma please I beg you. Please take me from here. I am fed up with his drinking, taunting, beating “ he start to cry bitterly. Pavitra knew her Son was the most affected.Many times She thought of escaping. But Something was pulling her back. Now for the past few months, the feeling of freeing his clutches is very strong. Pavitra is altogether fed up with him, and her life but the only surviving factor is her Son. Now he is sick and tired of his father. The heaps of pain and abundance of torture had reached its fullest extent. “My dear Son I know what you feel right now. Yes, the time has come for us to take the decision. We can change this house to another. Let me talk to the Panchayat member Rekha. She will arrange a small rental house for us. Give me three days dear. I promise you we will move out of this hell”. said Pavitra with a strong conviction.” But Amma, will Father come there to torture us? What will we do then?” asked him. “ No dear he will not bother us once we are out of this house. Trust me. I will not allow him to come near to you. I will be on guard. I am aware of his activities. You are my life. My very existence. This time no looking back” said Pavitra firmly. She went towards the open well, took the trough and drew water. She splashed the cold water on her face. The coldness was soothing but her wounds gave her stabbing pain. She stood there clutching the pillar of the open well. Her neighbour Usha came towards her walking. “ Pavitra are you alright? You look in such bad shape. Rekha Akka called me and asked about you. Where is your Son? Do you want something to eat or drink ? “ asked Usha.” I want to move to a new house. I don’t want to live like this. Even my Son is fed up with him. It’s been 14 years I have been suffering under his iron clutches. This time no looking back. Usha akka Will you please help me?”. “ Sure I will. I will call Rekha Akka. There is an empty house available near the temple. A three-bedroom house. It is near your tailoring shop. We can bargain about the rent. The owner is a relative of Rekha Akka. What do you say?” said Usha . “Yes I want to move out. Can we go today and meet the owner? Can you call Rekha Akka for me? Usha akka if you don’t mind can you prepare two cups of black tea?” asked Pavitra.” Sure Pavitra. I will bring it now” and She walked towards her house. Anandu who was standing behind Pavitra heard everything. He felt so happy and relieved. He looked at his mother and smiled. Pavitra also smiled at him. After some time Usha Akka brought two cups of black tea and steamed tapioca with spicy chutney. Pavitra and Anandu were so worn out and hungry that seeing the food before them they started to drool. They instantly had the food. Pavitra found it difficult to eat because of her wounds. She saw the Panchayath member Rekha Akka with two other men coming towards them. They came inside the house and saw the condition with their own eyes and realised their pathetic condition. “ Pavitra what is your decision? Are you ready to move out? Do you want to live with Sagar ?” asked Rekha Akka. “No Akka. I don’t want to live with him. I want to move out Also I want to separate from him legally,” said a strong Pavitra. They unanimously supported her. After a brief discussion, they decided to talk to the owner of the house regarding the rent and deposit. Meanwhile outside a person was observing each and everything- Ratheesh, Sagar’s drinking companion who is known for his immoral activities. Pavitra saw him from a distance She instantly felt something bad was going to happen. Everybody dispersed. Pavitra and Anandu cleaned the house, they took a huge baseboard and started putting household items into it. Around 5 in the evening, a completely drunken Sagar came to the house along with Ratheesh. Sagar screamed Pavitra’s name. He was so angry about them shifting the house. Pavitra and Sagar had a heated argument. Sagar took a pickaxe from the store room to hit Pavitra.She escaped his hit but unfortunately, the pickaxe hammered off the neck of Anandu. Blood started rushing out and made a pool, Pavitra screamed her heart out. Ratheesh ran out of the scene and escaped. Sagar seeing his Son wriggling for breath dropped his pickaxe, started screaming, crying and beating his head with his own hands. “ Anandu Anandu my son my son … what have you done Sagar? What have you done? Oh my god..” said Pavitra. Her hands were shaking. Anandu had a seizure, his body started to tremble uncontrollably, then suddenly the trembling stopped and he remained motionless in the hands of Pavitra. She screamed, yelled. She fell unconscious. Sagar ran out of the house wailing. Seeing this people ran with him. Sagar reached the river which was overflowing due to the monsoon rains. He stopped and panted, cried out loudly, and called his Son’s name. “ Anandu Anandu My Son.. I killed you . I killed you with my own hands. Oh God!. “ Sagar Sagar stop there. Sagar Sagar.” People started calling out his name. Sagar took a deep breath and jumped into the running water to the shock of people who witnessed it. Because nobody can do anything. The river was in its wild fierce ferocious form. People stood there in disbelief for some seconds. Someone tried to inform the police. Meanwhile, Pavitra and her Son were taken to hospital by the neighbours. When Pavitra opened her eyes the next day She screamed and yelled and ran to the top of the hospital building to commit suicide but hospital staff took hold of her and sedated her. This went on for some days until  Pavitra lost her sanity. She was taken to a government mental hospital for treatment. There She slept, screamed, and self-injured and her delusions lasted for seven years then slowly She came back to normalcy. She was not accepted in society and her brother’s family due to the stigma associated with mental illness. Pavitra visited the ordinary grave of her son which cannot be recognised due to huge grasses and unwanted climbers. Their house was completely dilapidated and covered with unwanted weeds and climbers. Nobody talked to her. Some people seeing her moved away from her as if She was contaminated. The only person who was kind enough to give her some food and water was the Panchayath member  Rekha Akka. The social isolation made her suffocate. She left her house and the place where she came post-marriage, where her Son was born and died. She felt a blankness. She contemplated suicide and She walked and walked reached the railway station. She was ready to jump to the track but She felt a sudden dizziness and fell on the platform. She heard people calling out her name.She opened her eyes and saw her Son Anandu standing in front of her and smiling at her. She felt so happy that She hugged him “Amma I am with you amma . You don’t have to worry amma. I am always with you. Smile amma . Be happy amma. I love you amma. “ Pavitra opened her eyes and saw people looking at her anxiously. They gave her water to drink. She stood up and sat on the bench with the help of the kindly woman. An elderly woman clad in a white saree came towards her and said, “Daughter I know you are up to something. But think before you do anything foolish. Life will be tough on you but you don’t have to be tough on yourself. Killing yourself doesn’t change anything. You have more to do with your life dear. Look around you. You can see people who are in more serious pain. They are wriggling themselves in the hardships of life. If they all start to kill themselves then this world will be devoid of people dear daughter.I lost my entire family in a car accident, my youngest son was only two years old when he left this world. Even I thought of killing myself. I hated everything. But realised I have more to perform in this world. I have an organisation called  Swasthi. I take care of the needy, elderly and babies who are left to die in the streets. Here take this card. Whenever you feel like coming to us you are all welcome my dear. Keep this with you. Take care, my daughter”. The elderly woman walked towards the group of people who were cladded in white. Pavitra looked at them. She thought about her parents, brother, husband and her dear Son. She took a rewind of her life and took a deep breath.She sat there until She felt alright and boarded a train to nowhere. She struggled to find some space in the general compartment which was packed with people. She stood and at night slept by sitting on the floor of the train. The train stopped at a railway station by morning. She looked around the platform and saw people busy talking and walking with their pieces of baggage. Pavitra saw beggars seeking alms. The group of white-cladded people walked straight towards the station entrance. The hustle and bustle, rumbling sound of trains moving, announcements, potters running hither and thither, shoutings of train tea vendors, some passengers sleeping on the benches of the platform, people from different walks of life across the country were present there. For some time Pavitra sat on the platform floor feeling alienated. She read the name of the railway station from the yellow board- Rameshwaram.She stood up, walked towards the ladies' waiting room freshened herself and came to the tea vendor for tea and two dal fritters with white chutney. She paid from the money given to her by the sympathetic warm-hearted Panchayath President Rekha Akka and the compassionate elderly woman. She drank the tea, threw the cup in the dustbin washed the hands from the small washbasin kept near the Station master’s office outside and started walking towards the Ramanathaswamy temple. The quaint town and sea made her mind and body calm. She became in equilibrium with the ambience of the place. Here nobody knows her. She is just a pilgrim and not Pavitra the mad woman who had lost her Son and Husband. She slowly and happily walked towards the silent sea. Dipped herself in the holy agnitheertham emerged pure and went to the public toilet. She bathed, changed her clothes, came outside looked around and saw the board hanging with the words  “ Swasthi”. She walked towards the gate, talked to the old man sitting on a chair and reading a newspaper and he showed her the way inside. Half an hour inside the premises She saw the elderly woman happily looking at her and walking towards her. Pavitra smiled at her. With open hands, She said, “Hey you are here!! Come my daughter . Help yourself and the needy people here. And by the by you can call me Sarada or Didi . Alright” Instead of killing herself She decided to live and help the underprivileged as much as She can. She realised the presence of her Son with her. She believed it was he who made her reach this place. Pavitra explained everything to Didi. Didi said, “Forget your past. Live the moment dear.  Be part of this family. You have a lot to do here. Come let me introduce you to our family”. Pavitra smiled started to walk.  She turned back and saw her Son happily waving his hands to her from the trees against the sea.Pavitra realised where she is and what she should do with the rest of her life. She felt at peace.

Name: Velvet horizons
Title: आज, अपनी ही नज़रों में हार गई🥀
Content:
कितने ही तूफ़ानों को
पलकों के पीछे छुपाकर,
हर बार बिखरने से पहले
ख़ुद को समेट लिया था।
ज़ख़्म मिले तो ख़ामोशी ओढ़ ली,
आँखें भीगीं तो मुस्कुराना सीख लिया—
हर टूटन के बाद
एक नई हिम्मत जन्म लेती रही।

मगर आज…
न वक़्त ने हराया,
न हालात ने,
न किसी और के दिए हुए ज़ख़्म ने—
आज हार
अपने ही भीतर से हुई।

दुनिया को हँसी दिखाई दी,
उस हँसी के पीछे दबा शोर नहीं।
ख़ामोशी को सुकून समझा गया,
मुस्कान को बेफ़िक्री—
किसी ने यह नहीं जाना
कि ठीक दिखने की कोशिश में
कितना कुछ भीतर चुपचाप टूटता रहा।

दुनिया से हार जाना फिर भी आसान है,
वहाँ दोष किसी और का होता है;
सबसे कठिन वह क्षण है
जब आईना सामने हो
और आँखों में
ख़ुद के लिए कोई सम्मान बाकी न बचे।

आज किसी और से नहीं—
उस शख़्स से हार हुई
जो हर तूफ़ान के बाद
टूटे हुए हिस्सों को चुनकर
फिर खड़ा हो जाता था।

Name: Vasu Gangapalli
Theme: Love beyond life, fate, loss, and the mysterious bond between two souls.
Title: Until Tomorrow
Content:
Until Tomorrow 
A Short Story by Vasu Gangapalli

The hospital corridor was unusually quiet that evening.
Pawan sat alone on a metal bench outside the intensive care ward, his elbows resting on his knees and his face buried in his palms. The smell of antiseptic hung heavily in the air. Somewhere in the distance, a machine beeped at regular intervals.
Above him, a tube light flickered.
Once.
Twice.
Then settled into a pale, restless glow.
“Why are you so sad?”
The voice was soft.
Pawan slowly lifted his head.
A girl stood before him.
She looked about his age. There was something strangely familiar about her face, though he was certain he had never seen her before.
“What happened?” she asked, glancing towards the ward.
Pawan swallowed.
“My friend is inside.”
“What happened to him?”
“Brain haemorrhage.”
Her expression changed.
“Will he be alright?”
Pawan shook his head.
“He's in a coma. The doctors don't think he has much time.”
For a moment, neither of them spoke.
“I’m sorry,” she whispered.
Pawan looked down at his hands.
“He's my best friend.”
The girl studied him for a moment.
“You've been sitting here for a long time, haven't you?”
He nodded.
“Come with me.”
“Where?”
“For a walk.”
Pawan looked towards the ward.
“I don't think I should leave.”
“You need a little air,” she said gently. “Sometimes, staying in the same place only makes the pain louder.”
Something about her words made him stand.
They walked out of the hospital.
A small park lay behind the building. The evening had begun to soften. The sky was turning orange, and the branches of a gulmohar tree swayed gently in the breeze.
They sat beneath it.
Two ducks moved lazily across the lake.
For the first time that day, Pawan felt his breathing slow.
“Do you have someone admitted here?” he asked.
“No.”
She smiled.
“My father is a doctor in this hospital. I came to visit him.”
“Oh.”
Pawan looked at the lake.
“I don't usually talk to girls.”
She laughed.
“You mean you don't have girlfriends?”
He smiled faintly.
“Neither do I have boyfriends.”
“Really?”
“Really.”
“Why?”
“I’m shy. And a little reserved.”
She looked at him mischievously.
“Well, I'm not shy.”
“I noticed.”
She laughed.
There was something effortless about talking to her.
They spoke about school, childhood memories, favourite books, silly fears, dreams they had never told anyone about. Every few minutes, one of them would laugh.
Pawan couldn't remember the last time he had laughed like that.
The sun slowly disappeared behind the trees.
“I think we should go back,” she said.
Pawan glanced at the sky.
“I didn't realize it was so late.”
They stood.
He looked at her.
“I'm Pawan.”
He extended his hand.
“Friends?”
She smiled and took it.
“Ankitha.”
“Friends.”
Their hands remained clasped for a moment longer than necessary.
Neither noticed.
Or perhaps both did.
As they walked back towards the hospital, Ankitha suddenly stopped.
“You know something?”
“What?”
“You should smile more.”
Pawan looked puzzled.
“Why?”
“Because it suits you.”
He smiled.
“But there's so much sadness around me.”
“That is exactly why you should smile.”
She looked into his eyes.
“Sometimes a smile is the only thing we can give to sadness before sending it away.”
Pawan stared at her.
“Will I see you tomorrow?”
She smiled.
“I'll be here.”
“Promise?”
“Promise.”
She held out her hand.
“Goodbye, Pawan.”
He shook it.
“Goodbye, Ankitha.”
She walked away.
Pawan stood watching her until she disappeared through the hospital entrance.
He looked at his hand.
A faint fragrance lingered on his fingers.
Jasmine.
He smiled.
I think I'm in love.
The thought frightened him.
And thrilled him.
As he walked back towards the ward, he looked up at the tube light.
If she loves me too, let this flicker.
The tube light flickered.
Pawan stopped.
Then smiled.
“Love,” he whispered.
“What a strange thing.”
He returned to the ward.
Through the glass door, he could see his friend lying motionless on the bed.
His friend's mother sat beside him, asleep in a chair.
Pawan stood there silently.
Life suddenly felt terribly fragile.
One moment, someone was laughing.
The next, they were gone.
No one knew which breath would be the last.
No one knew which goodbye would be final.
Pawan returned to the bench.
He thought about Ankitha.
Her smile.
Her voice.
The warmth of her hand.
I can't wait until tomorrow.
He closed his eyes.
I can't.
Ankitha couldn't wait either.
She had spent years wondering what love would feel like.
And now, when it had finally happened, she didn't want to lose even a minute of it.
So she returned to the hospital.
She found Pawan asleep on the bench.
A peaceful smile rested on his face.
She sat beside him.
Slowly, she took his hand.
It was strangely cold.
She smiled anyway.
She rested her head on his shoulder.
“Pawan,” she whispered.
He didn't wake.
She closed her eyes.
A sudden sound pierced the silence.
Beep.
Beep.
Beep.
Then—
a continuous tone.
Pawan's eyes flew open.
He looked around.
Ankitha was beside him.
Still asleep.
The sound was coming from the ward.
He rushed inside.
His friend lay motionless on the bed.
Pawan grabbed his hand.
“Wake up…”
But there was no response.
The monitor showed a straight line.
Pawan froze.
His friend's mother woke with a cry.
The next few moments became a blur of grief.
Pawan stood beside the bed, tears running down his face.
He had lost his best friend.
Or so he thought.
A hand gently touched his shoulder.
He turned.
Ankitha stood behind him.
She wiped his tears.
“Don't cry.”
He looked at her.
She hugged him.
And for the first time, Pawan noticed something strange.
Her feet made no sound against the hospital floor.
Neither did his.
They walked out of the ward together.
Hand in hand.
A man was waiting at the end of the corridor.
He was dressed simply.
There was nothing frightening about him.
And yet, the moment Pawan saw him, a strange chill passed through his body.
The man looked at him.
“It's time.”
Pawan frowned.
“Time for what?”
“To leave.”
Pawan glanced back at the ward.
“Can't I stay a little longer?”
The man shook his head.
Pawan looked through the glass door again.
And then he saw it.
The body lying on the bed.
The mother crying beside it.
The face beneath the white sheet.
His face.
Pawan stepped backwards.
“No…”
He looked at Ankitha.
“That's… me?”
She nodded.
His memories came rushing back.
The hospital.
The pain.
The darkness.
The moment the world had gone silent.
He had slipped into a coma hours earlier.
The boy he had been talking about wasn't his best friend.
It had been himself.
His soul had simply refused to understand that life had already left his body.
Pawan looked at Ankitha.
“Who are you?”
She smiled through her tears.
“Someone who was waiting for you.”
The stranger stood quietly nearby.
Ankitha turned towards him.
“Please.”
The stranger said nothing.
“Please let him stay.”
“You know I can't.”
“You already took him.”
She held Pawan's hand tighter.
“Please leave his soul with me.”
The stranger looked at her.
“I waited so long for love,” she whispered. “But it never came.”
A tear rolled down her cheek.
“Then I died.”
She looked at Pawan.
“And after my death…”
She smiled.
“…it finally happened.”
Pawan's eyes filled with tears.
The stranger remained silent.
Ankitha stepped closer to him.
“If you have to take him, take us both.”
The stranger looked at her for a long moment.
Then he smiled.
“Don't cry.”
He gently wiped the tear from her cheek.
“It doesn't suit you.”
Ankitha looked at him hopefully.
“I'll come back for both of you,” he said.
“Someday.”
He turned towards the darkness at the end of the corridor.
“Until then…”
He paused.
“…have a little more time.”
The lights flickered.
Once.
Twice.
The corridor fell into darkness for a heartbeat.
When the light returned, the stranger was gone.
Pawan looked at Ankitha.
She smiled.
He held her hand.
Together, they walked towards the hospital garden.
Outside, the moon had risen above the gulmohar tree.
Two ducks slept beside the still waters of the lake.
Pawan looked at Ankitha.
“Do you believe in love after death?”
She smiled.
“I believe love doesn't care where life ends.”
He smiled back.
Above them, the tube light flickered one last time.
And somewhere in the darkness, someone waited patiently for tomorrow.

Name: Aruna Chaturvedi
Title: मन के हारे हार है मन के जीते जीत
Content:
मन के हारे हार है, मन के जीते जीत।
संकल्प अटल हो तो मिलती हर मंज़िल निश्चित।
हार अगर मन में हो तो मंज़िल दूर नज़र आती है।
मन में यदि विश्वास हो, किस्मत भी राह बनाती है।

आईआईटी की हार ने अभिजय का साहस न तोड़ा,
गूगल तक पहुँचने का उसने अपना सपना न छोड़ा।
असफलताओं ने राह रोकी, पर हौसले कभी झुके नहीं,
मन ने जीत का दीप जलाया, इसलिए कदम कभी रुके नहीं।

टाइम्स स्क्वायर पर माँ का गौरव जब मुस्काया,
दुनिया की हर ऊँचाई ने चरणों में शीश झुकाया।
जीवन कहता है— हिम्मत कभी मत हार,
दृढ़ संकल्प से ही मिलता विजयी उपहार।

जो अपने संकल्पों पर हर पल अडिग खड़ा रहता है,
समय भी उसके साहस का सम्मान सदा करता है।
विश्वास की लौ कभी न बुझने देना, यही जीवन की रीत,
सच है, मन के हारे हार है, मन के जीते जीत।

Name: Babita Paul
Title: The Loss Of Love and Self
Content:
And yet he lied to me,
Within the darkest hour of glee.
He smiled,
The unexpected emotions continuously piled.
Was I asking for more, I asked
And the heart refrained from accepting,
How could he do it?
Didn't it hurt him, as though it did to me?
The lies lied on a platter
And tears on a cluster
He smiled through them
I kneeled
Asking for the love I weaved
Is that fair now, I asked
Why wouldn't it be, he said
With all the strength I had
I had given him that last chance
Gracefully he lost.
But did he truly?
Or was it me who lost in the end?
The loss of love and the self!

Name: Amritha Najn
Title: I Missed You
Content:
I Missed You

And I missed you
in chaos and in noise,
in calm and in voice.

You came and you went
like the breeze in my head,
always there,
but only sometimes felt.

When I felt the need
to grab you,
hold you tight,
and cry,

you slipped through
my very fingers,
like you were never mine to hold.

You came and you went,
and I felt you everywhere,
and saw you nowhere.

And yet,

I missed you
a little more.

Name: Gargi Chinchole
Title: Rapid Fire
Content:
A faded Delhi podcaster named Kabir who’s desperate to revive his dying channel, so he brings on Shastri Ji—an eerie, cryptic astrologer—for a clickbait Q&A called Ek Minute, Sau Sawaal. Kabir hits record and fires off lighthearted questions, but Shastri Ji’s answers are deeply unsettling: when Kabir asks, "Worst zodiac sign?" Shastri Ji rasps, "Scorpio. They carry secrets to the grave," and when Kabir pushes, "Worst time to make a major decision?" Shastri Ji flatly replies, "When you are hiding heartbeats under wet cement." Kabir laughs it off for the camera and his senses get distracted by the immense viewership and online comments engagement , but after editing, he can't stop thinking about those weird hints. He starts cross-referencing Shastri Ji's shady answers online and connects the dots to the famous missing person case of Ananya Sharma. Intrigued, Kabir invites Shastri Ji back for a second podcast, asking pre-planned questions  about astrology deep knowledgable questions on astrology but Shastriji is not able to answer any of them,  he confronts him: "You’re not reading charts, are you? Who are you?" That’s when Shastri Ji drops the act, revealing he’s actually Ananya’s uncle who took on a fake astrologer identity after the police closed her file. He tells Kabir the real motive: Ananya was pregnant with the baby of Vikram Randhawa—the wealthy builder’s son—who murdered her because he was engaged to a powerful Minister’s daughter. Arrogant and eager for justice, Kabir rushes to the local police station to file an FIR, but the corrupt officers laugh in his face: "You want us to open a cold case because a fake pandit told you a ghost story?" Just as Kabir gets into a screaming match with them, the new Station Head—a strict, sharp Inspector—steps in, hands Kabir a glass of water, and says, "Sit down, kid. Tell me everything from the beginning." The Inspector reopens the file and hauls Shastri Ji into the interrogation room, but the old man stays maddeningly mysterious, answering every standard question with riddles about planetary positions. Driven to near madness by Shastri Ji's cryptic responses, the Inspector slams his fist on the table: "Enough with the planetary bullshit!" That’s when Kabir steps up to the one-way glass and suggests, "Sir, traditional questioning won't work on him. Let me run a Rapid Fire." The Inspector agrees, and Kabir sits across from Shastri Ji under the harsh interrogation light, setting a timer on his phone. "Rapid Fire, Shastri Ji. Don't think, just answer," Kabir says, leaning in. "A place with no light?" Shastri Ji replies with a subtle, chilling smile, "Under pillar forty-two, where cold water flows." Kabir hits the table: "A silver object?" Shastri Ji whispers, "A tarnished kada, resting on a crushed wrist." Kabir pushes: "The greatest sin?" Shastri Ji looks straight into the camera: "Silencing a child to save a wedding." Following these subtle hints, the police rush to the Cyber Hub construction site, dig up pillar forty-two, and unearth a buried barrel—officially confirming through forensic testing that it is indeed Ananya’s body. To break Vikram’s political immunity, the forensic team extracts fetal DNA from the remains that proves a direct paternal match to Vikram, while digital investigators recover deleted three-year-old toll plaza CCTV logs placing his private SUV at the site at 2:00 AM. But the ultimate smoking gun comes from inside the cement barrel itself: alongside a crushed glass bezel from Vikram’s designer watch, investigators recover an engraved copper ring wedged directly under the barrel’s base—a ring belonging to Ananya's uncle. Armed with this unshakeable proof, the police corner Vikram Randhawa, who walks into the precinct flanked by high-priced lawyers, sneering at the Inspector, "You dug up a construction site on the words of a lunatic. My father-in-law will have your badge by morning." But Kabir sneaks into the control room, hooks his podcast equipment to the station's PA system, and broadcasts his mic through the entire building. Kabir interrupts through the speakers: "Rapid Fire for you now, Vikram! Why did you kill her?" Blinded by the station lights and furious at the public humiliation, Vikram snaps, screaming at the top of his lungs into the live mic: "Because she was pregnant, alright?! She was going to ruin my marriage to the Minister's daughter! She deserved to rot under that cement!" The whole station falls dead silent as his full confession echoes through the hallway, right in front of the press and top officers. As the Inspector slaps handcuffs on a ruined Vikram, the entire case finally collapses into justice, but the tragedy isn't over. Just a few days later, news breaks that Shastri Ji’s lifeless body has been retrieved near the construction site, holding a small note in his hand that reads: “The karma comes back to everyone so it came back to me.” Shortly after hearing the news, a traumatized Kabir walks out to his car in the pitch-black night, only to find a mysterious wax-sealed envelope resting on his windshield."I didn't need the stars to find her body Kabir,... I dug her grave before I even knew it was hers."







Context:

He breaks the seal to find his own personalized horoscope chart drawn inside, followed by a final, heartbreaking confession written before Shastri Ji's death: three years ago, a dirt-poor Shastri Ji was simply paid cash by site managers to dig a deep trench at midnight without asking questions. When he realized his prized heirloom copper ring had slipped off into the pit, he crept back into the dark to search for it—only to witness Vikram lowering a heavy barrel into the fresh grave, discovering to his absolute horror that the girl being entombed beneath the wet concrete was his beloved niece, the only family he had left. The guilt of digging her grave consumed him, driving him to orchestrate Vikram's downfall before taking his own life. The letter ends with a handwritten line in dried red ink:

Name: Nusha Jamila
Title: The Fall
Content:
I remember the dawn
Like it was mere hours ago – 
I stumbled onto you on the pavement, my feet tripping,
And sent us crashing over the piled leaves.
The dawn I first saw you.
The dawn we both met our first fall.
Lying over you, eyes wide, I remember my heart going
Thud. Thud. Thud.

I remember it now
As I climb up the rocky hill,
Past the roots and the dense of trees,
My face plump and eyes puffy.
The browns and greens blur
To my thoughts that race with traitorous memories
And my heart that goes
Thud, thud, thud.

Then came the night;
The night you pulled me in, your arms firm around my waist,
And whispered to me those three words;
Soon your lips met mine.
Under the fireworks, on a New Year’s Eve, I remember,
My eyes closed and palms on your chest,
I fell for you as I felt your nervous heart echo mine:
Thud. Thud. Thud.

Yes, it was the fall that hit me
Like a breath of fresh air
As you breathed into me a liveliness,
A life.
Like the fresh air that I heave in now
As I reach the top of the hill
And view its bleakness with my heart droning
Thud..thud..thud.

But it is the noon of my birthday,
My twenty-fifth, the cursed day,
That fronts my mind as I now near the cliff.
It was the noon you brought me up here,
The noon I lost your breath from me
As I watched you trip and greet your final fall,
With nothing but your scream and my heart in my ears:
Thudthudthudthud.

It’s me here now, at the edge again, alone.
My face wet and mind muddled.
The sky dims as the sun falls,
And I fall along with it – 
My final fall.
I close my eyes against the oncoming greyness
And listen to the finale of my heart’s rhythm:
Thud. Thud. Silence.

Name: Harshad Pandit
Title: Soulful Symphony
Content:
A street mongrel, his weathered coat and hat
At the feet of whom his loyal dog sat
Strumming a violin note, doleful sorrow in heart
Tearing through evening din, like a piercing dart

For company, his tunes and a wagging tail
When love, comrades all left him to wail
A woebegone visage, yet his soul was strong
Scattered coins at his feet, handful for his song

Reminiscent of good old times, his tears ran dry
A true musician’s wealth, the melody he held high
The violin cried out umpteen stories to unfold
More than any number of coins his hat could hold

Entwined art & loyalty where heartbeats meet
A soulful symphony, that's ne'er too discrete
True love was all he sought, all so scanty
The hat on the ground asked questions aplenty

Can the Almighty gainsay his travesty and gloom? 
Destitute life of only drudgery and doom
Yet in his heart, a desire to live, not die
As his music lived on, beyond a silent whimper and sigh.

Name: Nusha Jamila
Title: Celestial Misfortune
Content:
What are stars?
Mere little blinks scattered
Over a canvas of paint so dark;
Yet still they dazzled her.
        No matter they typically are sparse,
        Or often so very guttered,
        But within her they lit an intense spark,
        Albeit fleeting, always a spur.
    
"Just wait," she promised,
"I'll come see you one day."
And wait, she did. And did
In faith, that one day she just may.
        What is life but a comet –
        A cold rock in darkness astray;
        And its companion, time, never honest.
        Both hand-in-hand only betray.
    
Betrayed was she,
Her faith in painful shards,
As the fact was forgone to her
That it was forbidden to want the stars.
        No matter the ploy or the plea,
        Forced was she behind habitual bars,
        Her dreams deserted to an endless defer,
        With only the remnants of brutal scars.
    
Alas! The fate of her starlight desires –
The cosmos reduced them to pitiful satires.
Only a blink, and there it was, the Moon,
Within her palms, unsullied and out of cocoon.
        Oh so bright and so unfairly pure,
        And made all else swoon for sure.
        Yet no, neither the Moon nor Mars she fancied,
        Only those little blinks were all she'll ever need.
    
Deemed was she an ungrateful wretch,
Merely for daring to deny this "boon".
Was she truly at fault, akin to all they allege?
Doubts emerged, her senses less and less attune.
        And so she gradually teetered to the edge,
        As nights wore on beside "her Moon",
        Beneath the dome so mockingly etched
        By fluorescent stars so sham, her utter misfortune.

Name: Dr. Abdul Salam Khan
Title: Beyond the Line
Content:
God created the land; man created the line.
Nature gave us the earth without borders, without boundaries, without divisions. Man drew lines upon it lines of nations, communities, identities, beliefs, and territories. We named them borders, but slowly, we began to treat them as walls. Religion can sometimes create divisions in the minds of people, but art has always stood on the other side of the line where humanity begins, and differences disappear.
Art does not ask, “Who are you?”
Art asks, “What do you feel?”
A colour does not carry a religion. Red is not Hindu, green is not Muslim, blue is not Christian, and yellow is not Buddhist. Colour has no caste, no creed, no nationality, no language. It simply expresses. It speaks where words become silent. It touches emotions before it reaches the intellect. A brushstroke does not know the boundary of a country; a melody does not stop at a border; a sculpture does not ask the faith of the person who looks at it.
True art is always beyond the line.
It rises above demographic jurisdictions, political boundaries, social classifications, and religious identities. It exists in that beautiful space where I become we, where difference becomes dialogue, and where diversity becomes harmony. The artist does not merely create an image; the artist creates a possibility a possibility of seeing the world differently. A painting can bring two strangers together before the same canvas. A song can make people of different cultures move to the same rhythm. A poem can awaken compassion in a heart that knows nothing about the poet. A sculpture can transform silence into conversation.
Art does not divide the world into “us” and “them.” Art reminds us that there is only “us.”
The true purpose of art is not merely decoration, recognition, or applause. Its deeper purpose is to create harmony to extract from the human soul the hidden flow of love, affection, empathy, peace, and brotherhood. Art becomes most powerful when it stops being a possession of an individual and becomes an experience shared by humanity. Perhaps that is why the greatest works of art survive their creators. Civilisations disappear, empires fall, borders move, languages transform, and generations change but art continues to speak. The Ajanta murals still whisper across centuries. The music of great masters still crosses continents. The poetry of Tagore still reminds humanity that the world is larger than any single identity.
As Rabindranath Tagore beautifully envisioned, “An artist is a world citizen.” The artist belongs not to one geography, one religion, or one community, but to the vast human family.
God created the land. Man created the line.
Art crosses the line.
Art erases the distance.
Art connects the heart to the heart.
And perhaps, in the end, art is not only for art’s sake it is for humanity’s sake.
Because where religion may sometimes build walls, art builds bridges; where borders create distance, art creates belonging; and where differences create silence, art gives humanity a common voice.
Art has no religion. Art is the religion of humanity.

Name: Shreyasee das
Theme: Identity,Epic,Inner battle,Journey from outer light to inner light.
Title: THE SHADOW AND THE SUN
Content:
*THE SHADOW AND THE SUN*
_Where Kurukshetra Lives Inside_
_By Shreyasee_

There is a place inside every human
Where Kurukshetra never ended.

Not a field of arrows,
But a field of identities.

On one side stands the world
With all its names, its trophies, its wounds.

On the other stands the soul,
Naked, silent,
Needing no applause to exist.

And between them,
On a chariot that has lost its way,
Stands a man born of the Sun,
Yet living in shadow.

His name is Karna.
Not the Karna of Hastinapur.
The Karna who lives inside us.

He was the Sun who needed a cloud to prove his light.

Sutaputra, they called him,
And he believed it.

Then a curse became his scripture,
Then a crown became his soul.
Angraj, they called him,
And he became a slave to that name.

That is his tragedy,
Not that he was denied,
But that he never denied the denial.

He gave and gave and gave,
His armor, his earrings, his friendship, his life,
But he never took.

Never rest.
Never peace.
Never the simple knowing,
I am enough.

And his loyalty,
That fire-like loyalty to Duryodhan that poets praise?

It was never to Duryodhan.
It was loyalty to his own wound.

Duryodhan did not give him friendship.
He gave him identity.
He said, I make you King.
And for a man who had been called Sutaputra all his life,
That one word became oxygen.

He was not protecting Duryodhan on the battlefield.
He was protecting the only man who had ever given him a name that did not wound.

Is this not us?
Are we not all loyal to those who gave us a name?
To the company that gave us a designation,
To the lover who gave us worth,
To the degree that gave us pride?

We call it loyalty,
But it is slavery to our own ego.

The fire to prove,
But not the power to become the living proof.

Truth has no figure.
Truth has foundation.

A lamp is not true because its light travels far.
It is true because its oil is deep.

THE SCIENCE OF THE SUN

The Sun rides a chariot pulled by seven horses.
They are not horses.
They are light itself, broken into seven colors.

Violet - The Crown.
The highest thought.
In Karna, clouded by the need to be seen as great.

Indigo - The Third Eye.
The eye that sees within.
Karna never opened it.
He saw himself only through the eyes of others.

Blue - The Throat.
The courage to speak truth that liberates,
Not truth that proves.

Green - The Heart.
Love.
In Karna, an ocean, but a wounded ocean.

Yellow - The Will.
The fire to become.
In Karna, the fire to prove he was a warrior,
But never the power to sit quietly and know,
I am a warrior even when no war exists.

Orange - The Creation.
Skill.
The greatest archer in all the land,
Yet a slave to his own skill.

Red - The Root.
Foundation.
Which Karna never had.
His root was never in his soul,
But in his support,
In a curse, in a crown, in a friendship.

When seven horses run in seven directions,
The chariot does not move, though the horses run fast.

Immense speed. Zero arrival.
Born from the Sun, yet never reaching the Sun.

There are two Suns.

Prakash Surya - The Outer Sun.
It gives light to all, but burns itself.
It needs a world to see it.
This is the Karna in us.

Bodha Surya - The Inner Sun.
It does not give light.
It is Light.
It has no sunrise, no sunset.
Its seven horses have become one white fire.
It needs no witness.
This is the Shreyasee in us.

Life is a pilgrimage from Prakash to Bodha,
From seven colors to One,
From proving to being,
From mud to lotus.

A lotus is born in mud.
It does not curse the mud.
It uses the mud to bloom above it.

That was the true aim of the epic,
Not to show who won,
But to show how every soul,
Even the most wounded, can become a lotus.

Even Karna.

THE MEETING

An empty field.
No conches. No armies.
Only two souls.

SHREYASEE:

What word is this, forgiveness, upon thy tongue, O Angraj?

Thou art called noble, great of soul.
Dost thou not know what every child knows?
The light of the Sun can never be bound.

Its hue may shift,
Saffron at dawn, white at noon, blood-red at dusk,
And so its shadow changes shape.
But light remains light.

Thou art but a form of shadow, Karna.
And shadows do not live long where true light reigns.

Thou namest Draupadi guilty.
But is that guilt hers, or is it thine own longing wearing her face?

Thou hast built a palace upon dust.
Thy Guru's curse became thy foundation.
Sutaputra became thy scripture.
But true brilliance needs no crutch.
True valor walks on its own feet.

In what pride callest thou thyself Suryaputra,
When thy seven steeds run scattered?
Thy violet craves a crown, thy red has no root.
How shall thy chariot ever find the Sun?

And thy troth to Duryodhan,
Is it love for a friend,
Or love for the throne that gave thee a name?
Had he not cried Angraj in that sabha, wouldst thou still have loved him?

Speak true, O Sun in chains,
Thou art loyal not to Duryodhan, but to thine own wound.

KARNA:

Peace!

Thou speakest of light as one who has read of fire,
But never been branded by it.

Infinite blaze of the Sun no mortal flesh can bear.
It is shadow that makes the Sun's wrath into a mother's love.
Without shadow, the Sun is but death.

As shadow is part of body, so night is part of Sun.
Man sees the Sun not by light, but by the shadow in his own eye.
Light dwells within, but shadow is the tongue that tells the world of the Sun.

Ego is man's identity.
Without ego, there is no Om.
Without I, there is no beginning.
Ego is Lakshmi. It gives man legs to walk this earth.
And that same ego, when washed in sacrifice, rises as Om.

My friendship is my Dharma.
My seven horses know but one road, the road of my word.
And a word is a mountain.
A mountain waits for none, but it never moves.

SHREYASEE:

True, light is never sundered from shadow.
But without body, where is shadow, Karna?
Without self, where is ego?

Thy brilliance, thy valor, it is a web, O great weaver,
Woven of illusion.
For it is not knit to thy soul.
Thou bearest it as burden and callest burden duty.

Thou hast become slave to thine own gift.
But the Sun is slave to none, not even to its own shining.

What warrior art thou, who needs a war to know he is warrior?
What Sun art thou, that needs a cloud to prove it shines?

Look, every man today has thy fire,
The fire to prove.
But where is the power to become the living proof?

True Suryaputra is not he whose horses run swift,
But he whose horses run together.

Take that name away, Angraj.
Who art thou?

KARNA:

Existence is as a mountain.
A mountain has weight and echo too.
But a mountain waits for none.

SHREYASEE:

But beneath every mountain, Karna,
Beneath every mountain there burns a volcano.

If it should erupt,
What then remains of mountain?
What then remains of its weight, its echo, its identity?

KARNA:

We shall meet again, someday.

SHREYASEE:

We shall see.
When thy seven become One.

The curtain falls.
But inside the reader, the play just begins.

To the reader who is Karna:

Thou hast become Sun for the world,
But hast thou become Sun for thyself?

Thy seven horses are running,
But do they run together?

From mud to lotus,
From proving to being,
That is thy journey.

FOR THE WORLD - THE HEALING

This is not a poem only about Karna.
This is medicine for the modern world.

If humanity understands this one truth,
That the seven horses must run together,
Then many wounds of the world are healed.

Depression ends, because a man stops asking the world, Am I enough?
And begins to say to himself, I am enough.

Anxiety ends, because the chariot no longer runs in seven directions to prove itself.

War of ego in offices ends, because we stop protecting the name that gave us identity, and start protecting truth.

When a child reads this, he will never be slave to Sutaputra, never be slave to Angraj.
He will know, I am neither my insult nor my crown. I am Atma.

When a leader reads this, he will not give people only designations and salary.
He will give them belonging, and freedom from proving.

When a lover reads this, she will not ask, Do you make me worthy?
She will say, I am lotus. Even in mud, I bloom.

The global benefit of this poem is simple:
From competition to completeness,
From comparison to coherence,
From Prakash that burns the world to Bodha that heals it.

If one reader in a hundred understands that his seven horses must become One white fire,
Then his home becomes peaceful, his work becomes worship, his love becomes liberation.

That is why the epic was written.
Not for who won Kurukshetra,
But for how Kurukshetra inside us can end.

May every Karna become Sun.
Not for the world.
For himself

Name: Vasu Gangapalli
Title: Death Comes!
Content:
Death comes! (Ver 1.0)
A Short Story by Vasu Gangapalli 

Frank Willis unlike others loved to meet the death someday. Even if it meant embracing him and sacrificing his life. Many times he thought how he was going to meet him and when?

One day morning, he saw a beautiful young woman walking in the street. She smiled at him. He too smiled back at her. He forgot everything else and was lost. It was love at first sight. Someone placed hand upon his shoulder. He pushed it off and kept staring in her direction. Again the hand was placed on his shoulder. He turned back rather annoyed and found a stranger standing behind him.

“Who are you? Why are you bothering me like this?” Frank asked.

Suddenly, he felt as if he couldn’t breathe and there was a sharp pain in his chest.

“It was only sometime back you were so desperate to meet me and now?” replied the stranger with a grin on his face.

“Yes…but I wasn’t expecting you now.” Frank replied scared.

“I know..even I didn’t come to take you along.” He replied.

“Then?” Frank asked.

“I was passing this way and was surprised to see you here.” He replied. “As you wanted to see me from a long time so I thought to say ‘Hello’ to you.”

The End

Name: Pratima Tiwari
Title: "मैं समय की शिष्य हूँ।"
Content:
"मैं समय की शिष्या हूँ”

"जीवन में हमें अनेक गुरु मिलते हैं—
माता-पिता, शिक्षक, पुस्तकें और अनुभव…
पर एक गुरु ऐसा भी है,
जो बिना कुछ कहे जीवन का सबसे बड़ा पाठ पढ़ा देता है।
वह है— समय।
उसी मौन गुरु को समर्पित मेरी यह स्वरचित कविता—

'मैं समय की शिष्या हूँ।'”

मैं समय की शिष्या हूँ...
हाँ... मैं समय की शिष्या हूँ।

हर पल उससे कुछ सीखा है,
जीवन ने जितना परखा मुझको,
उतना ही मुझको निखारा है।

धूप मिली तो चलना सीखा,
छाँव मिली तो ठहरना सीखा।
आँधियाँ भी आईं जीवन में,
पर हर बार सँभलना सीखा।

रिश्तों ने भी पाठ पढ़ाए,
कुछ अपने होकर दूर हुए।
कुछ अनजाने साथ निभा गए,
कुछ आईने भी चूर हुए।

वक़्त ने सिखाया—
अपेक्षाएँ जितनी कम होती हैं...
मुस्कान उतनी ही सच्ची होती है।

अब शिकायतों का समय नहीं,
स्वीकार करना सीख लिया है।
हर गिरने के बाद स्वयं ही
फिर से उठना सीख लिया है।

अब किसी से आगे निकलना
मेरी मंज़िल नहीं रही।
कल से बेहतर बनना ही
मेरी सबसे बड़ी जीत रही।

चेहरे की हर एक रेखा
अब मुझे कमज़ोर नहीं लगती।
ये उम्र की नहीं...
मेरे अनुभवों के हस्ताक्षर हैं।

मैंने जाना—
दीपक बनने के लिए
पहले स्वयं जलना पड़ता है।
और नदी बनने के लिए
पत्थरों से टकराना पड़ता है।

आज मैं पूर्ण होने का दावा नहीं करती....
पर अधूरी भी नहीं हूँ।
मैं हर दिन
अपने ही कल से बेहतर बनने की
एक छोटी-सी कोशिश हूँ।

क्योंकि...
समय ने मुझे केवल उम्र नहीं दी...
उसने दृष्टि दी है।
उसने केवल अनुभव नहीं दिए...
जीवन को पढ़ने की समझ दी है।

और अंत में...
यदि जीवन आपको कभी परखे...
तो घबराइए मत...क्योंकि...

सोना अग्नि में तपकर कुंदन बनता है,
मनुष्य संघर्षों में तपकर व्यक्तित्व गढ़ता है।

"सीखना ही जीवन है... और मैं , आज भी सीख रही हूँ।
क्योंकि....

मैं समय की शिष्या हूँ...
...और अभी सीखना बाकी है।

– प्रतिमा तिवारी
कवयित्री

Name: DR TUSHAR
Title: Naasthik prem ki kahani
Content:
Naasthik Ne Prem Kar Liya

Na sajdon mein yakeen tha,
na duaon ka koi silsila,
na kisi khuda se shikwa,
na kisi rehmat ki justuju.

Zindagi ko
jitna aankhon se dekha,
utna hi sach maana.

Phir tum mili.

Tumse mohabbat hui,
aur mere saare qaayede
khamosh ho gaye.

Main kehta raha,
ishq bhi toh ek ehsaas hai,
waqt ke saath guzar jayega.

Magar tumhara naam
dil mein utarta gaya,
aur mera inkaar
dheere dheere
kamzor padta gaya.

Maine khuda ko kabhi nahi maana,
magar tumhare liye
haath uthne lage.

Tumhari khairiyat ke liye
jo lafz nikalte the,
unhe kya naam doon?

Dua nahi kehta,
kyunki khuda par yakeen nahi.

Mohabbat kehta hoon,
kyunki tum par
yakeen hai.

Tumse bichhadne ka khauf
kisi azaab se kam nahi,
tumhare milne ki khushi
kisi ibaadat se kam nahi.

Kis kitaab mein likha hai
ki mohabbat ke liye
imaan zaroori hota hai?

Mera dil gawah hai,
maine khuda ko nahi maana,
magar tumhe
poore yaqeen se maana hai.

Aur shayad
meri saari zindagi ka
sabse bada ikraar yahi hai—

Naasthik tha,
isliye khuda se mohabbat na hui,
magar tumse hui...
toh laga,
shayad har cheez ko
khuda kehna zaroori nahi hota.

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Self love, learning to love yourself after hating yourself.
Title: An awkward first date (Me and myself).
Content:
Silence stretches between both of us as we sit together for a coffee date.
This silence is really loud, and, my thoughts seem a lot louder, this just feels awkward
I can't really cherish the moment when its with you, it feels different, a little uneasy
I've hated you for so long, I've sometimes worked against you, I've hurt you
I've personally run a blade across your tender skin, I've despised you inside and out
I want you to be someone else, I want you to behave differently! I want someone strong, confident, muscular, productive. I want someone who can lift me easily.
I want someone who takes care of themselves every single day.
I want someone who is happy.
And you don't even brush your teeth daily, and you don't even shower.
You're like a stick and so incredibly skinny.
You shout at your parents and friends and you hurt them sometimes.
But here I am, and here you are, so I guess we're willing to try again?

This feels really awkward and uncomfortable.
"We're so far apart." You tell me. "We're literally miles away. How do we meet at the same page, ever?"
"It's okay." I tell you. "We'll just take one step forward every day, just forward instead of back, and one day, we'll meet on the same page."
I hope my sincerity shines through in my actions, even if this doesn't feel amazing to you at first. Maybe its uncomfortable.
But I prepared this coffee date table for you and chose the cloth of your favourite colour. Maybe your thoughts are racing and you're not fully in the moment.
But its okay, even if its not exactly how I hoped it'd be.

I really want to take care of you.
I really want to cherish you and love you the hardest during your worst moments
You told me you're afraid of pain, well, in pain I want to look after you really well
Maybe it might hurt less, eventually, I'll keep trying
The first date is really awkward, it feels uncomfortable, and what are we even doing?
I awkwardly take sips of my coffee just to break the ice, and you keep staring away.
But at least we both managed to sit down, and try together.
And if we try enough times, maybe it wouldn't be awkward at all.
We're meant to be together in this lifetime and we have our whole lives ahead of us.
One day at a time, and I hope that eventually when I try, try and try again
One day it'll hit you, and one day we might laugh together at a joke
And one day we might even meet at the same page, the version of each other we both wanted to see
We're just going to try, and eventually, I'm going to be comfortable with you.
I know you already, I just feel like I don't love you. But one day, eventually
We'll meet each other at the same page.
We'll not feel awkward anymore.
The silence will still exist between you and me, but, it won't hurt.
One day.
But for today, let's just take one step forward.

I wish you were someone else, but, while you become that person
I'm still going to love you just the same.

Name: rittik bora
Title: A Walk Towards Freedom
Content:
Beneath a lightless sky,
Where darkness had taken hold,

Faces turned into masks,
Where truth became bankrupt,
And lies bought every prize.

I locked myself behind closed doors,
Shivering in the cold,
Where breathing grew too heavy
To carry me forward,

And liberation
Became a mountain to climb.

Deep within the abyss,
I chose an unseen path,
A walk taken alone,
To find the child I had lost—
To smile again,
And dance
To the beating rhythm of being alive.

Still,
The shadow trails behind—
A reflection of what I refuse to become,
Toward the freedom I once buried.

Name: Tanay Bhushan Desai
Title: The Girl I saw , The Boy I forgot
Content:
I never thought your words
could hurt me like that.

Not from you.

I remember holding my tears
and quietly saying,
“Please… don't.
Don't say things like that.”

But you did.

I swallowed all my anger all the rage inside me
all the things i wanted to say , but I didn't knowing 
that I was hurt as well.

You shouted.
You disrespect me.
You scolded me.
You hit me.

And I stood there.

Not because it didn't hurt.

It did.

I was already at my lowest,
already alone,
already trying to hold myself together,
and somehow
I still chose to stand there for us.

Because when I looked at you,
I didn't only see the person hurting me.

I saw a little girl.

Scared.
Afraid of being hurt again,
afraid of feeling that same pain
all over again.

And I understood. 

I know I scared you too.
I know I made you anxious.
And knowing that I hurt you
has always been something
I could never forgive myself for.
whenever you get hurt , I can feel the pain.

Because how could I hurt someone
whose pain I could feel as my own??

you know all this time , I was scared of hurting and losing you 
and now I have been living in the same fear and that's eating me alive 
knowing that I gave you anxiety make me feel worst, I cry like a child!  


Because beneath everything you said,
beneath the anger and the shouting,
I could still see her.

That frightened little girl inside you.

And I loved her.

I think I loved her so much
that I forgot about the boy
standing beside her.

The boy who was hurting too.

The boy who swallowed his tears
so yours could have a place.

The boy who wanted to scream,
“I am hurting too,”
but stayed quiet
because he was afraid
that leaving you
would hurt you more.

And maybe that's what love was to me—

not forgetting that you hurt me,
but understanding why you did.

Not pretending I didn't deserve better,
but loving you anyway.

You were the one hurting me.

And somehow,
I still loved you more.

Even now,
I think I always will.

Because I never stopped seeing
the little girl inside you.

I'm sorry for making you scared and making you anxious but know that this was not my intension.
But I wish you would stand for us like i did , I wished you had given us a second chance. 
I was hurt too , I was too scared of hurting myself again by trusting someone again but anyways i did bec i was soo in love with you
and i guess that was my biggest mistake . 

I love you like breathing just like Hassan loved Amir Agha but (you)Amir taught me why you should not love someone like Hassan did.

I only wish,
before I spent so long
trying to save her,

I had remembered
to save the boy too.

Name: Izadora Fernandes
Title: I love you
Content:
For when God,
With intention,
And love,
Brought us together,
I'm reminded why.

For when you pray,
With faith,
And I hear you say,
"God, I pray for us",
I'm reminded why.

For when you plan,
With goals,
And always,
Follow God's plan,
I'm reminded why.

For when you smile,
With your eyes,
And see, 
With your heart,
I'm reminded why.

For when you walk,
With those strides,
And move closer,
Saying "Hi!"
I'm reminded why.

For when you lead,
With respect,
And ask,
"Let's go out?",
I'm reminded why.

For when you yawn,
With messy hair,
And whisper,
Words of love,
I'm reminded why.

For when you lean in,
With endearment,
And say,
"Baby, my love,"
I'm reminded why.

For when you ask, "Why?",
With kisses,
And I have,
A never-ending list,
I'm reminded why.

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Gifted kid burnout, burnout, loss of energy, losing your spark.
Title: The gifted kid burnout.
Content:
There was a fire which chose to glow less brightly.

"Why do you glow less brightly now?" You ask, disdainful eyes, voice full of noticeable disapproval.

The fire was glowing brightly.
The fire's force turned inward, and it ate itself up
A blur of pain and self destruction, the embers
Started consuming themselves, just to burn bright
The glorious illuminance, was a haze of pain
As the fire screamed silently, inside its own mouth
An agonising, agitated, uncontrollable thrashing
Beneath a smiling face, a silent plea for help 
And people just admired its glow, its brightness,
its light, that cost itself to produce.

If you have not seen all that
And have not seen the price of excellence
"Why do you glow less brightly now?" You have no right to ask.
