"चाह के भी नहीं रह सकता… और तुम ये जानती हो।"

"Hmm… पता है… पर सोचा आज पूछ लूँ… क्या पता कुछ नया सुनने को मिले।"

"मत पूछा करो ये सवाल… हमने पहले ही इस बारे में बात की है कि मैं राधिका को नहीं छोड़ सकता।"

"ठीक है… नहीं कहूँगी फिर।"

इतने में अभिमन्यु का फोन रिंग हुआ।

"हाँ राधिका… हाँ, डिनर हो गया। बस एयरपोर्ट के लिए निकल रहा हूँ। तुम सो जाओ, मैं सुबह 8 बजे तक घर होऊँगा।"

जितनी देर अभिमन्यु राधिका से बात कर रहा था, देविका बस उससे एक दूरी बनाए हुए, उससे कुछ कदम पीछे चल रही थी।

अभिमन्यु ने जैसे ही फोन काटा, वो रुक गया। उसे पता था हर बार की तरह देविका पीछे हो गई होगी। इसलिए वो रुका और उसके आने का इंतज़ार किया। फिर से देविका ने उसका हाथ पकड़ा और दोनों कार की तरफ चलने लगे।

"कैसे यूँ ही बीत जाता है ये टाइम… तुम अभी तो आए थे।"

"Hmmm… पर ये 5-6 घंटे जो भी मिलते हैं, ये मेरी ज़िंदगी के सबसे खूबसूरत घंटे होते हैं।"

दोनों ने कार का दरवाज़ा खोला और बैठ गए। इस बार अभी ड्राइव करने वाला था। देविका बगल की सीट पर बैठी और उसने अपनी सीट थोड़ी-सी पीछे की और पैर ऊपर करके बैठ गई।

"जब हील्स पहनी नहीं जाती, तो क्यों पहनती हो?"

"बस ऐसे ही… मन था आज।"

"अच्छा…"

"Hmmm…"

फिर कुछ एक मिनट के सन्नाटे के बाद अभिमन्यु बोला,

"मैं तो दिल्ली नहीं आ सकता… और अब मॉ भी देहरादून जा रही हैं, तो तुम आ जाओ… मुंबई।"

देविका ने गहरी साँस ली और बोली,

"अभी, you know… मेरा बिज़नेस यहाँ है, और मैं दिल्ली शायद कभी न छोड़ पाऊँ… और वैसे भी वहाँ भी अलग रहना है, तो मैं यहीं ठीक हूँ।" "तुम तलाक लोगे नही… और मैं ऐसे रहने आऊँगी नही… तो जो जैसे चल रहा है, चलने देते हैं।"

"पर मैं सिर्फ साल में दो बार तुमसे मिलना नहीं चाहता… मैं चाहता हूँ, जब मेरा दिल करे, मैं तुमसे मिलूँ।"

" तुम और तुम्हारे बड़े-बड़े ख़्वाब…" ये कहकर वो ज़ोर से हँसने लगी।

देखते ही देखते एयरपोर्ट आ गया। बीच में कुछ गाने दोनों ने साथ गाए और कुछ फिर से साहिल की, घर की और ऑफिस की बातें करते-करते ये मुलाक़ात भी ख़त्म हो गई।

उसने उसी एयरपोर्ट पर छोड़ा, जहाँ वो दोनों पहली बार मिले थे…

अभिमन्यु ने जाते वक्त उसके माथे को चूमा और देविका ने उसकी पॉकेट में अपना छोटा-सा गिफ्ट रखा और बोली, "फ़्लाइट में खोलना।"

फिर देविका कार में बैठी और घर चली गई।

फ़्लाइट में बैठकर उसने अपनी पॉकेट से गिफ्ट निकाला और उसे खोला। उसमें एक छोटा-सा की-चेन था, जिसके साथ एक चाबी थी… **"हमारा घर"**

और जैसे ही वो फ़्लाइट से लैंड हुआ, उसके फोन पर देविका का मैसेज आया—



"Dear अभिमन्यु,

Happy 10th Anniversary.

सबसे खूबसूरत दिन वो था, जब तुम मुझे मिले। मेरी ज़िंदगी बदल गई, और मुझे ये तुम्हें बताने की ज़रूरत नहीं है, क्योंकि तुम बहुत अच्छे से जानते हो।

Thank you उस दिन एयरपोर्ट पर आने के लिए… Thank you मुझे लिफ्ट देने के लिए… और Thank you मेरी ज़िंदगी में आने के लिए। मुझे पता है तुम कभी मुझे पूरे नहीं मिलोगे… पर मैं हमेशा से पूरी तुम्हारी ही रहूँगी।

मुझे पता है तुम राधिका को, और राधिका तुम्हें नहीं चाहती… पर तुम कभी राधिका को नहीं छोड़ोगे। शायद कभी - कभी husband-wife सिर्फ साथ होते हैं, पर एक-दूसरे के पास नहीं… पर एक बात है… ये घर, जो हमेशा से तुम्हारा इंतज़ार करता है हर साल 5 फ़रवरी को, वो हमेशा करेगा… और मुझे इंतज़ार रहेगा उस दिन का, उस रात का, जब पूरे 24 घंटे हम साथ होंगे…

तुमसे जो भी मिला… जितना भी तुम्हारा वक़्त मिला… और हर साल की ये दो मुलाक़ातें… काफ़ी हैं मेरे लिए… बस हमेशा इतने तुम मेरे रहना |

चलो, फिर मिलते हैं 6 महीने बाद… उसी लीला की टेबल पर… उसी पान की दुकान पर… और उसी एयरपोर्ट पर, जहाँ से ये सब शुरू हुआ था |

सिर्फ तुम्हारी,  
देविका

Name: Khushi Dehliwale
Title: Kuch dostiya aisi bhi
Content:
कुछ दोस्तियाँ ऐसी भी

बस ज़िंदगी की दौड़ से
थोड़ा सा वक़्त चुरा कर,
आज यूँ ही बैठ गए हम बाते करने।

और मेरी दोस्त मुझे कहती है—
“कितना अच्छा लगता है,
जब तुम आ जाती हो।
ज़रूरी है कुछ दोस्तियाँ ऐसी भी।"

काफ़ी लंबे अरसे के बाद,
बातों का सिलसिला कुछ ऐसा चला
कि घंटे कब बीत गए पता ही नहीं चला।
फिर यूँ लगा,
शायद ऐसे ही कहीं,
बातें करते करते बचपन गुज़र गया
और हम बड़े हो गए।
वक़्त बदला, रास्ते बदले,
ज़िंदगी अपनी रफ़्तार से चलती रही,
पर लगाव आज भी वही है,
जैसे कल ही की तो बात हो।
होती हैं न कुछ दोस्तियाँ ऐसी भी।

समय भले ही आगे निकल गया,
पर हमारी दोस्ती वहीं ठहरी है—
उसी हँसी में,
उसी अपनेपन में,
उन्ही बेपरवाह-सी बातों में।

और शायद इसी का सुकून है
कि हाँ, हैं मेरे पास भी
कुछ दोस्तियाँ ऐसी भी।

वक़्त से परे,
दूरियों से परे—
कुछ दोस्तियाँ ऐसी भी।

                    - खुशी देहलीवाले

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Self love, learning to love yourself after hating yourself
Title: An awkward first date (Me and myself).
Content:
Silence stretches between both of us as we sit together for a coffee date.
This silence is really loud, and, my thoughts seem a lot louder, this just feels awkward
I can't really cherish the moment when its with you, it feels different, a little uneasy
I've hated you for so long, I've sometimes worked against you, I've hurt you
I've personally run a blade across your tender skin, I've despised you inside and out
I want you to be someone else, I want you to behave differently! I want someone strong, confident, muscular, productive. I want someone who can lift me easily.
I want someone who takes care of themselves every single day.
I want someone who is happy.
And you don't even brush your teeth daily, and you don't even shower.
You're like a stick and so incredibly skinny.
You shout at your parents and friends and you hurt them sometimes.
But here I am, and here you are, so I guess we're willing to try again?

This feels really awkward and uncomfortable.
"We're so far apart." You tell me. "We're literally miles away. How do we meet at the same page, ever?"
"It's okay." I tell you. "We'll just take one step forward every day, just forward instead of back, and one day, we'll meet on the same page."
I hope my sincerity shines through in my actions, even if this doesn't feel amazing to you at first. Maybe its uncomfortable.
But I prepared this coffee date table for you and chose the cloth of your favourite colour. Maybe your thoughts are racing and you're not fully in the moment.
But its okay, even if its not exactly how I hoped it'd be.

I really want to take care of you.
I really want to cherish you and love you the hardest during your worst moments
You told me you're afraid of pain, well, in pain I want to look after you really well
Maybe it might hurt less, eventually, I'll keep trying
The first date is really awkward, it feels uncomfortable, and what are we even doing?
I awkwardly take sips of my coffee just to break the ice, and you keep staring away.
But at least we both managed to sit down, and try together.
And if we try enough times, maybe it wouldn't be awkward at all.
We're meant to be together in this lifetime and we have our whole lives ahead of us.
One day at a time, and I hope that eventually when I try, try and try again
One day it'll hit you, and one day we might laugh together at a joke
And one day we might even meet at the same page, the version of each other we both wanted to see
We're just going to try, and eventually, I'm going to be comfortable with you.
I know you already, I just feel like I don't love you. But one day, eventually
We'll meet each other at the same page.
We'll not feel awkward anymore.
The silence will still exist between you and me, but, it won't hurt.
One day.
But for today, let's just take one step forward.

I wish you were someone else, but, while you become that person
I'm still going to love you just the same.

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Painful choices, choosing a path when both paths carry regret, trauma
Title: Prometheus (I choose suffering).
Content:
I was standing in front of two burning platforms.
Both were being consumed by menacing fire, and if I started to walk
They would devour my body whole. But I had to choose one.
Instead, I chose a smaller platform above the two burning ones.
It provided me with a fleeting sense of relief, but then, it too started to burn
Licking the tender skin of my feet with immense heat, and I could feel it disintegrate
After a while, the lack of a decision itself starts to burn me and cause me pain.
This platform was not to be, it melted beneath my feet, and I was
Right inside the very fire which I tried so very hard to avoid.

The fire was merciless, and charred my flesh away, reducing it to nothing.
Pain that shot through every inch of my body, straight through my spine and into my brain
A blur of agony and despair, I know not how I walked through fire, all I remember is a haze of pain
My body fused together with the flames, bound tight by pain, the smoke from my own body
Going inside my nose as I inhale, silent screams inside my own mouth, my body turning black
The fire incinerated my very soul, without heeding to my trembling, just another wave of pain.
I had walked through fire, and never wished to do so again.

Now I'm standing in front of two burning platforms again.
And I have to choose one yet again. But if I were to walk, I'll get burnt again.
My raw flesh now exposed to air, charred, burnt, raw and red, will have to get burnt again.
Instead, I once again chose a small platform above the two burning ones.
No, I'm not going to move forward this way, but I just don't want to burn again.
The small platform is not to be, and once again, cannot stand my weight, and is caving with time
Slowly burning as well, burning my feet once again. My already hurt feet tremble with the memory.
The platform is caving in once again, and I stand looking at the two platforms, the only way on.

Dear Prometheus, you already knew what you were doomed to face again and again
You can't avoid this no matter how hard you try, you can try all you like, exhaust yourself
You're just going to be in pain anyway, wherever you are, you already know, don't you?
If you want to move forward and bring fire to humanity, you know what's going to happen
The Caucasus awaits you and the eagle will tear open your torso and feast on your liver
All your emotions, your sadness, anger, hope, and despair, they'll all get devoured every day
Night after night, you know what's going to happen and there's no avoiding it

Dear Prometheus, alas! You know not how strong you are.
You might fear the beak of the eagle penetrating into your body, whimpering in pain,
And watching the eagle eat your insides up as you're helpless, tied up, and disintegrating.
Blood will drip down the eagle's neck, drop by drop, and its going to happen slowly and steadily
Every single day. You might fear all this, but once it's actually happening, the resilience deep inside
Comes out like a reflex, and almost intuitively, you'll walk through fire and make it out alive.
You'll never be the same again. You're going to wear the suffering as a crown one day,
Burns leave scars, ugly, ghastly, blackened, charred scars. You'll wear the rock like a ring
The scars may exist, but you're going to walk forward anyway, and it'll exist but so will you.

The platform is crumbling beneath my feet, everything's crashing down, and I'm already burning
Instead of the platform disintegrating and falling in like last time, I'm going to jump in myself.
I choose suffering that is inevitable. I choose suffering before it chooses me.
If I must burn again, so be it, I'm going to burn again.
The flame inside my heart which carried me through this the last time, I'm going to keep it safe
I can see miles into the future, I'm going to live again. I'm going to walk through fire once again.
I take a deep breath, let clean air fill my lungs for the last time, and tell myself,
"I’m jumping into one of the platforms myself."
"I'll choose my own suffering."
I look down at the two burning platforms with a determined gaze.
What has to happen, will happen again, I must burn again and again and again.

Name: Surya Teja Gorli
Title: తనకి తెలియని నా ప్రపంచం
Content:
శీర్షిక: తనకి తెలియని నా ప్రపంచం

ఈరోజు ఏమైందో నాకు అసలు అర్థం కావడం లేదు…

ఎప్పటిలాగే తనని చూశాను.
ఎప్పటిలాగే తనతో మాట్లాడాను.

కానీ తనని చూస్తుండగానే…
ఒక్కసారిగా ఏదో కొత్తగా అనిపించింది.

ఎప్పుడూ లేని ఆనందం,
ఎందుకో తెలియని ప్రశాంతత.
మనసంతా ఏదో కొత్త అనుభూతితో నిండిపోయింది.

అప్పటి నుంచి ఎందుకో
నా మనసు నా మాట వినడం లేదు.

ఏం చేస్తున్నా,
ఏం ఆలోచిస్తున్నా…
మళ్లీ తనే గుర్తొస్తోంది.

తనని చూస్తుండగానే
ఎందుకో నా చూపు అక్కడే ఆగిపోయింది.

ఏం జరిగిందో తెలియదు…

ఆ క్షణం అయిపోయినా,
నా మనసు మాత్రం ఇంకా అక్కడే ఉన్నట్టనిపించింది.
ఏంటి ఇది?
నాకు తెలియకుండానే నేను తనని ఇష్టపడుతున్నానా?

ఎవరికి చెప్పుకుందాం?

పక్కన ఎవరూ లేరు…
చుట్టూ చూస్తే ఈ పుస్తకాలు, పాత కుర్చీలు తప్ప.

సరే…

ఈరోజు నా మనసులో ఉన్నదంతా
ఈ పుస్తకాలకే చెప్పుకుందాం.

[పుస్తకంలో రాయడం మొదలుపెట్టాను]

30/09/2026
బుధవారం

నా ప్రియమైన డైరీ,

ఈరోజు జరిగిన విషయం నీతో చెప్పకుండా నిద్రపోలేననిపిస్తోంది.
అసలు ఎక్కడి నుంచి మొదలుపెట్టాలో కూడా తెలియడం లేదు…

తనని మొదటి సారి చూసినప్పుడు…
ఏదో సినిమాలో చూపించినట్టుగా ప్రపంచం ఒక్కసారిగా ఆగిపోలేదు.
చుట్టూ ఉన్నదంతా మామూలుగానే ఉంది.
నా గుండె కూడా అలాగే కొట్టుకుంటూనే ఉంది.

కానీ…

ఏదో జరిగింది.

ప్రపంచం ఆగిపోలేదు…
కానీ నేను ఆగిపోయాను.
నిన్ను చూస్తూ…

నా కళ్ల ముందు ఎంతమంది ఉన్నా,
తన తప్ప ఇంకెవరూ కనిపించనంతగా ఆగిపోయాను.

అది ఎందుకో నాకు అర్థం కాలేదు.
నువ్వెవరో కూడా నాకు తెలియదు.
నీ పేరు కూడా తెలియదు.

అయినా ఆ క్షణంలో,
తను మాత్రం నాకు ఏదో తెలిసిన వ్యక్తిలా అనిపించావు.

తనని చూస్తుంటే,
ఎప్పటినుంచో పరిచయం ఉన్నట్టుగా అనిపించింది.

ఏమో… అందుకేనేమో…
తను అక్కడి నుంచి వెళ్లిపోయినా,
నా కళ్ల ముందే ఉన్నట్టుగా అనిపించింది.

నాకు తెలిసి,
నేను తనని మొదటిసారి చూడలేదు.

బహుశా…
ఈ పరిచయం నాకు కొత్తది కాదేమో.

లేదంటే,
మొదటి సారి చూసిన తను
ఇంత పరిచయంగా ఎలా అనిపించింది?

ఇంకా మాట్లాడితే,
నాకు తనలో నచ్చిన మొదటి విషయం తన కళ్లే.

చిన్ని చిన్ని కళ్ళు…
నువ్వు నవ్వినప్పుడు ఇంకాస్త చిన్ని అయిపోయేవి.

నిజం చెప్పనా?

తను నవ్వినప్పుడు,
నా చూపు ముందుగా వెళ్లేది తన కళ్ల దగ్గరకే.

తన నవ్వు తన పెదవుల దగ్గర ఆగిపోదు…
తన కళ్లలో కూడా కనిపిస్తుంది.

తన అందమైన కళ్లను
తన కళ్లద్దాల వెనక దాచేస్తుంది.

కానీ తనకు తెలియని విషయం ఏంటంటే…
తను తన కళ్లను దాచుకున్న ప్రతిసారీ,
నేను మాత్రం వాటిని ఇంకాస్త ఎక్కువగా గుర్తుపెట్టుకున్నాను.

తన నవ్వు గురించి ఏం చెప్పాలి అనుకున్నా,
మళ్లీ నా చూపు తన కళ్ల దగ్గరకే వెళ్లిపోతుంది.

తను ఎప్పుడు చూసినా,
ఆ చిరునవ్వు తన పెదవులపై కనిపిస్తూనే ఉంటుంది.

తన మాటల్లో కూడా తన నవ్వే కనిపిస్తుంది.
తను ఏదైనా చెబుతుంటే,
మధ్యలో వచ్చే ఆ చిన్న నవ్వు
తన మాటలకే ఇంకో అందాన్ని తీసుకొస్తుంది.

తను ఏం చెబుతుందో వింటూ ఉండటం ఒకటైతే,
తను చెబుతూనే నవ్వుతుంటే చూస్తూ ఉండటం ఇంకోటి.

కొన్నిసార్లు,
తను చెప్పే మాటలకంటే
ఆ మాటల మధ్యలో తను నవ్విన క్షణమే ఎక్కువగా గుర్తుండిపోతుంది.

అందుకేనేమో…
తన మాటలు వింటూ ఉండాలనిపించేది.

నిజం చెప్పాలంటే,
నాకు తనలో నచ్చింది తన అందం మాత్రమే కాదు.

ఇంకో విషయం కూడా ఉంది.

తను అందరిలా ఉండదు.
తనకి నచ్చినట్టే ఉంటుంది.

తను వేసుకునే డ్రెస్‌ నుంచి,
తను మాట్లాడే మాటల వరకు…
అన్నింటిలోనూ తనని ప్రత్యేకంగా చూపించే ఏదో ఒకటి ఉంటుంది.

మన తెలుగు సంప్రదాయాల్ని
తనకి నచ్చినట్టుగా, చాలా సహజంగా పాటిస్తుంది.

అందుకే ఏమో…
ఇంతమంది మధ్యలో
తను మాత్రం నాకు ఇంకాస్త ఎక్కువగా కనిపించింది.

తనలో నాకు నచ్చింది
ఒక్క విషయం కాదు.

తనని తను మార్చుకోకుండా
తనలాగే ఉండే ఆ తీరు.

నిజం చెప్పాలంటే…
తను నా జీవితంలోకి వస్తే ఎలా ఉంటుందో
నేను ఊహించుకున్న ఒక క్షణం ఉంది.

తను నా వైపు నడుచుకుంటూ వస్తుంటే,
తనని చూడకముందే
తన పట్టీల శబ్దంతోనే
తను వస్తుందని గుర్తుపట్టగలనేమో.

తను చేతులు కదిపినప్పుడల్లా
గాజులు చేసే ఆ చిన్న శబ్దం
ఎందుకో నాకు చాలా దగ్గరగా అనిపిస్తుందేమో.

నుదుటిన పెట్టుకున్న చిన్న బొట్టు,
తన ముఖానికి ఇంకాస్త అందాన్ని అద్దినట్టుగా
చూస్తూ ఉండిపోతానేమో.

అలా ఒక్కో అడుగు వేస్తూ
తను నా దగ్గరికి వచ్చి…

పెళ్లి చీరలో
నా పక్కన కూర్చుంటే…

ఇన్నాళ్లూ నేను ఊహించుకున్న తను
ఆ రోజు నిజంగా నా పక్కన ఉంటే…

ఆ క్షణంలో ఇంకేం కావాలో కూడా
నాకు అర్థం కాకపోవచ్చు.

కానీ…

అది కేవలం నా ఊహ మాత్రమే.

తను నా గురించి ఏం అనుకుంటుందో నాకు తెలియదు.

తను నన్ను ఇష్టపడుతుందో లేదో కూడా నాకు తెలియదు.

ఇన్ని రోజులు తనతో గడిపిన
ఆ చిన్న చిన్న క్షణాలన్నీ
ఇప్పుడు నా జ్ఞాపకాలుగా మిగిలిపోయాయి.

ఒకవేళ తన మనసులో నేను లేకపోయినా…
తనని ఇష్టపడిన ఈ మనసుని
నేను మాత్రం తప్పు పట్టలేను.

ఎందుకంటే…

"తనని ప్రేమించాలనుకుని నేను ప్రేమించలేదు.
తనని చూస్తూ చూస్తూ… తెలియకుండానే ప్రేమలో పడిపోయాను."

ఇంతే…

ఈరోజు నా మనసులో దాచుకున్నదంతా
ఈ పుస్తకానికి చెప్పేశాను.

తనకి ఇవన్నీ ఎప్పుడైనా తెలుస్తాయో లేదో నాకు తెలియదు.
కానీ ఈరోజు మాత్రం
నా మనసులో ఏం జరుగుతుందో నాకు అర్థమైంది.

ఇక నిద్రపోవాలి…

రేపు తనని మళ్లీ చూసినప్పుడు
ఈరోజు రాసిందంతా గుర్తొచ్చినా,
ఏమీ జరగనట్టే ఉండాలి.

శుభరాత్రి,
నా ప్రియమైన డైరీ.

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Title: Salvation
Content:
9 days out of 10 I pick myself up and start over
I tell myself I don't even need a reason to continue
When storms hit, just get up and walk again
But these days, I just can't seem to do that
I've lost my spark, I'm a burnt out match
What's the point of hoping and wishing if every day your entire being burns as if on fire?
Is this what my life has been reduced to? I wish I could be happy once again
I'm tired, all I've been inhaling is black smoke from my own body burning up, I can't catch a breath

I've lost my light, so lend me yours for a day
Bring your glowing match towards mine and light mine up and we'll glow as two now
When all the time I'm burning, give me a breath of the freshest air
Fill up my lungs and I'll drink it up desperately
Give me a change, a breath of air, a shot of life again, so that even if I'm not moving forward, I stand where I am and take a quiet breath

I've looked at the sky so many times hoping for something different
I feel as if I shut my eyes in the dark night, and when I open it, I expect light to be there somehow
I temporarily take a rest, but when I open my eyes, nothing seems to get better, so nothing helps
Even if you can't fix anything, make a brief light shine in my darkened gaze
I'm tired of looking up and yearning for something that's different 
So please lift up my chin and make me look above 

Carry my pain for a moment and make it dissolve
Give me the salvation that only you can give
Temporarily light up my life, so even if everything's dark, I'll look for the next spark that you produce
Never believed in everything happening for a reason, I don't know if I believe in getting stronger from pain anymore
Everything's crushing me and some days I can't see the point, so I no longer believe.
But I believe in you.

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Slow pace, ambition, stillness, growing together but slowly, balance, patience
Title: Inside the Cocoon
Content:
I just can't help myself, I try my best to stay patient 
But some days I just lose myself in my anger
I want you to skip steps 2-99, let's go right to 100
I'm perfectionistic I know, but it feels so good
I want your beautiful wings out and I want them painted in a thousand different colours
I have dreams for us and I want to make them happen
I want it, I want it, but the more I want it, the farther it goes away, what an irony 
I push you more and more and in the end we're both just exhausted and head palming
Then how do we make this happen?
At what pace do I take it, then?

A red stream and a pure white stream flowing besides each other.
The red one accelerating more and more every single second, as if asking the white one to match its pace.
The white one, ironically, slows down even more.

I can't move like this, please wait for my slow pace
Can you please hold me in your arms while I blossom and bloom within
And reassure me with your warmth every day, while I'm inside the cocoon?
So that I may be everblooming with you, everblooming because of your warmth
The flowers which grow in one day also wither the very next day
We spend a lot of our lives becoming someone else, becoming someone other than ourselves, so why not just enjoy the process and take it slow?
Isn't there a beauty in witnessing a cocoon cracking a little more day after day?
I'm neither here nor there, I'm in limbo, and can you love me even in this state?
When I climb step by step, and in between two steps, when I stand still and fumble
In the quiet whirr of the airplane engine while we are travelling between here and there, in the quiet rocking of the train, can you find that to be a kind of music?
Even in my transient, formless state, please tell me I still shine

The red and white stream seem to get closer, and the red stream slows down.
The white one seems to accelerate just a little. Can they together, break all the obstacles which come in their way?

I understand what you say, but some days, I just can't help myself
I don't want the middle ground, I want the highest possible ground and I want us to make a jump, why can't we?
Some days I lose myself and I just seem to come right back to square one
And some days I just can't find the beauty in your slow pace like I always do
Can you please be patient with me then?

I understand you, but some days, everything seems to go wrong
I can't make myself get out of the bed, I can't make progress
Even the slow pace which I said we'd follow, I need us to slow down even more
Some days I lose myself and I just seem to come right back to square one
And some days I get fed up by your accelerating pace, the pace I can't match
Can you please be patient with me then?

The red and white streams seem to twist into each other, forming a sort of tightly twisted rope made of two strings. The two streams, made stronger by each other, with the force of ambition, and with the beauty of stillness, crumble every obstacle in their way to pieces and drill a hole right through them.
An intertwining and meeting point of ambition and stillness, in other words, divinity.

Name: rittik bora
Title: Privilege
Content:
A palace,
built behind fragile walls,
a crown passed down
upon stones we never laid.

We inherited
the path,
but not the eyes
to question it—
the crown,
not the spine to carry it.

Empty footsteps
wandering through its halls,
until the mirror asks:
who is walking?

Heirs of the past,
or architects of the future?

Let the mirror strip the mask,
until nothing borrowed remains.

A privilege we pass along—
a voice
for those who come next,
not a path to follow,
but a compass to guide,
a gate left open,
and the courage
to lay their own stones.


                                        -------- Ritwik Bora

Name: Gunjan Mittal
Theme: “सियाचिन का प्रहरी — देशभक्ति, कर्तव्य और बलिदान”
Title: सियाचिन का प्रहरी
Content:
सियाचिन का प्रहरी

एक सैनिक की अधूरी चिट्ठी

सुबह के पाँच बजे थे।

गाँव अभी नींद में था।

गलियों में सन्नाटा था। कहीं-कहीं किसी मंदिर की घंटी की हल्की आवाज़ सुनाई दे रही थी। लेकिन राजेश के घर में उस दिन नींद किसी की आँखों में नहीं थी।

राजेश अपनी सेना की वर्दी पहनकर आईने के सामने खड़ा था।

आज वह पहली बार अपने गाँव से इतनी दूर जाने वाला था।

माँ चुपचाप उसके लिए खाना बाँध रही थी।

बार-बार डिब्बा खोलती, कुछ और रखती और फिर बंद कर देती।

राजेश मुस्कुराया।

“माँ, इतना खाना कौन खाएगा?”

माँ ने उसकी तरफ देखा।

“माँ हूँ। पता नहीं वहाँ तुझे समय पर खाना मिलेगा भी या नहीं।”

राजेश कुछ नहीं बोला।

उसे पता था कि माँ की चिंता खाने की नहीं थी।

वह अपने बेटे की चिंता कर रही थी।

पिता दरवाजे के पास खड़े थे।

उन्होंने राजेश को बुलाया।

“बेटा।”

“जी, पिताजी।”

कुछ पल दोनों एक-दूसरे को देखते रहे।

फिर पिता ने कहा—

“देश की सेवा करना आसान शब्द है। निभाना बहुत मुश्किल।”

राजेश ने उनके पैर छुए।

“मैं कोशिश करूँगा कि आपको कभी शर्मिंदा न होना पड़े।”

पिता ने उसके कंधे पर हाथ रखा।

“हमें तुझ पर पहले से गर्व है।”

राजेश घर से बाहर निकला।

दरवाजे पर माँ खड़ी थी।

उसकी आँखें भर आई थीं।

राजेश ने पीछे मुड़कर देखा।

माँ ने हाथ हिलाया।

राजेश ने भी हाथ हिलाया।

फिर वह आगे बढ़ गया।

उसे नहीं पता था कि अगली बार जब वह उस घर की चौखट देखेगा, तो कितना समय बीत चुका होगा।

---

कुछ महीनों बाद राजेश की पोस्टिंग सियाचिन में हुई।

जब उसे पहली बार बताया गया, तो उसने सिर्फ इतना कहा—

“जी, सर।”

उसके साथी ने मज़ाक में पूछा—

“तुझे डर नहीं लग रहा?”

राजेश हँसा।

“डर क्यों नहीं लगेगा?”

“फिर जा क्यों रहा है?”

राजेश ने आसमान की ओर देखा।

“क्योंकि सीमा पर किसी को तो खड़ा होना पड़ेगा।”

सियाचिन पहुँचते ही उसे समझ आया कि किताबों में पढ़ी हुई कठिनाई और उसे जीना दो अलग चीजें हैं।

चारों ओर बर्फ।

तेज़ हवा।

कठोर ठंड।

कई बार ऐसी परिस्थितियाँ कि सामान्य जीवन की छोटी-छोटी चीजें भी बहुत बड़ी सुविधा लगने लगती थीं।

पानी आसानी से उपलब्ध नहीं था।

बर्फ को पिघलाकर पानी तैयार करना पड़ता।

खाना सीमित होता।

हर चीज़ सोच-समझकर इस्तेमाल करनी पड़ती।

कपड़े सिर्फ कपड़े नहीं थे—वे जीवन की सुरक्षा का हिस्सा थे।

हर कदम सावधानी से रखना पड़ता।

राजेश ने पहली रात अपनी चौकी के बाहर खड़े होकर तिरंगे को देखा।

हवा तेज थी।

तिरंगा पूरी ताकत से लहरा रहा था।

राजेश ने धीरे से कहा—

“मैं यहाँ हूँ।”

उसके साथी ने पूछा—

“किससे बात कर रहे हो?”

राजेश मुस्कुराया।

“अपने घर से।”

साथी हँस पड़ा।

लेकिन राजेश सच कह रहा था।

उसे लगता था—

जहाँ तिरंगा है, वहीं उसका घर है।

---

सियाचिन में दिन धीरे-धीरे बीतने लगे।

घर से दूर रहना आसान नहीं था।

माँ की आवाज़ याद आती।

पिता की डाँट याद आती।

छोटी बहन की शरारतें याद आतीं।

गाँव की गलियाँ याद आतीं।

गर्म चाय याद आती।

और सबसे ज्यादा—

घर का वह आँगन याद आता जहाँ शाम को पूरा परिवार साथ बैठता था।

एक दिन राजेश को घर से चिट्ठी मिली।

लिफाफा खोलते समय उसके हाथ थोड़े काँपे।

अंदर माँ की लिखावट थी।

“बेटा,

यहाँ सब ठीक हैं।

तू अपनी चिंता मत करना।

बस समय पर खाना खा लेना।

ठंड बहुत होगी वहाँ। अपना ध्यान रखना।

तेरी बहन रोज पूछती है कि भैया कब आएँगे।

तेरे पिता कहते हैं कि तू बहादुर है।

लेकिन मैं माँ हूँ।

मुझे तू हमेशा वही बच्चा लगता है जो स्कूल जाते समय मेरा हाथ पकड़कर सड़क पार करता था।

जल्दी वापस आना।

तेरी माँ।”

राजेश ने चिट्ठी कई बार पढ़ी।

फिर उसे अपनी जेब में रख लिया।

उस रात उसने किसी से ज्यादा बात नहीं की।

उसने आसमान की तरफ देखा और बहुत धीरे कहा—

“माँ… मैं वापस आने की पूरी कोशिश करूँगा।”

लेकिन उसके दिल में एक और आवाज़ थी—

“और अगर नहीं आया, तो भी तिरंगा नहीं झुकने दूँगा।”

---

समय बीतता गया।

एक दिन पानी की कमी बहुत ज्यादा थी।

जवानों को पानी बहुत संभालकर इस्तेमाल करना पड़ रहा था।

एक साथी जवान ने कहा—

“राजेश, आज तो पानी की बहुत परेशानी है।”

राजेश ने अपनी बोतल उसकी तरफ बढ़ा दी।

“ले।”

“नहीं, तुझे भी चाहिए।”

“हम बाँटकर पी लेंगे।”

साथी ने पूछा—

“तू हर चीज़ बाँट देता है क्या?”

राजेश मुस्कुराया।

“सीमा पर अकेले कौन जीता है?”

उसकी बात छोटी थी।

लेकिन उसका मतलब बड़ा था।

राजेश के लिए वफादारी सिर्फ देश के प्रति नहीं थी।

वह अपने साथियों के प्रति भी उतना ही वफादार था।

उसे मालूम था—

अगर एक जवान कमजोर पड़ा, तो बाकी सभी प्रभावित होंगे।

इसलिए वह अपनी थकान छिपा लेता।

अपनी परेशानी छिपा लेता।

अपनी चिंता छिपा लेता।

लेकिन ड्यूटी कभी नहीं छिपाता।

---

एक रात मौसम अचानक बिगड़ गया।

तेज़ बर्फीली हवा चलने लगी।

दृश्यता बहुत कम हो गई।

चौकी पर सभी जवान सतर्क थे।

राजेश लगातार निगरानी कर रहा था।

एक साथी ने कहा—

“थोड़ी देर आराम कर ले।”

राजेश ने सिर हिलाया।

“तुम कर लो।”

“तू कब आराम करेगा?”

राजेश ने तिरंगे की तरफ देखा।

“जब ये आराम करेगा।”

साथी ने कहा—

“तिरंगा थोड़ी आराम करता है!”

राजेश हँसा।

“तो फिर मैं भी नहीं।”

दोनों कुछ क्षण हँसे।

लेकिन अगले ही पल दोनों फिर अपनी ड्यूटी पर लग गए।

यही सैनिक का जीवन था।

कुछ सेकंड की हँसी।

फिर लंबी जिम्मेदारी।

---

दिन कठिन थे।

कभी भोजन सीमित होता।

कभी पानी की चिंता।

कभी नींद पूरी नहीं होती।

कभी मौसम शरीर को थका देता।

कभी घर की याद मन को।

लेकिन राजेश हर सुबह एक काम जरूर करता।

वह तिरंगे को देखता।

और खुद से कहता—

“आज भी ड्यूटी पूरी करनी है।”

उसे मालूम था कि उसके पीछे करोड़ों लोग अपने घरों में चैन से सो रहे हैं।

किसी बच्चे को पता नहीं था कि उसके स्कूल जाने से पहले सीमा पर कोई जवान रात भर जाग रहा है।

किसी परिवार को पता नहीं था कि उनके घर की रोशनी के पीछे किसी सैनिक की लंबी रात छिपी है।

राजेश यही सोचता था—

“अगर मैं यहाँ खड़ा हूँ, तो मेरे देश का कोई बच्चा अपने घर में चैन से सो रहा होगा।”

यही विचार उसे आगे बढ़ाता।

---

एक दिन उसे फिर घर से चिट्ठी मिली।

इस बार चिट्ठी उसकी छोटी बहन ने लिखी थी।

“भैया,

मैंने आज स्कूल में भाषण दिया।

मैंने कहा कि मेरा भाई सैनिक है।

सबने तालियाँ बजाईं।

मुझे बहुत गर्व हुआ।

लेकिन जब घर आई तो माँ चुप बैठी थी।

वह आपकी पुरानी तस्वीर देख रही थी।

भैया, आप जल्दी आना।

मैंने आपके लिए राखी संभालकर रखी है।”

राजेश की आँखें नम हो गईं।

उसने चिट्ठी मोड़ी।

जेब में रखी।

और कुछ देर अकेला बैठा रहा।

उसे पहली बार लगा—

वह सिर्फ अपने लिए नहीं लड़ रहा।

उसके पीछे उसका पूरा परिवार खड़ा है।

और उसके आगे पूरा देश।

---

फिर एक दिन सीमा पर स्थिति अचानक तनावपूर्ण हो गई।

सभी जवानों को सतर्क कर दिया गया।

राजेश ने अपने साथियों की तरफ देखा।

किसी के चेहरे पर डर था।

किसी के चेहरे पर चिंता।

राजेश ने कहा—

“डरना मत।”

एक जवान ने पूछा—

“तुझे डर नहीं लग रहा?”

राजेश ने सच कहा—

“बहुत लग रहा है।”

“फिर इतना शांत कैसे है?”

राजेश ने जवाब दिया—

“बहादुरी का मतलब डर न होना नहीं है। डर के बावजूद अपनी ड्यूटी पर खड़े रहना है।”

उस रात सभी जवान अपने-अपने स्थान पर थे।

राजेश की निगाह लगातार सामने थी।

उसके हाथ ठंड से काँप रहे थे।

शरीर थका हुआ था।

लेकिन आँखें जाग रही थीं।

क्योंकि उसके पीछे तिरंगा था।

---

अगले कुछ घंटों में हालात और कठिन हो गए।

राजेश ने अपने साथियों को सुरक्षित रखने के लिए कई बार अपनी स्थिति बदलकर निगरानी की।

एक समय ऐसा आया जब उसे खुद बहुत जोखिम उठाना पड़ा।

उसके साथी ने कहा—

“राजेश, पीछे हट!”

राजेश ने जवाब दिया—

“तुम लोग आगे जाओ। मैं देखता हूँ।”

“लेकिन—”

“ये आदेश है।”

उसने अपने साथियों को सुरक्षित स्थान की ओर भेज दिया।

कुछ देर बाद स्थिति संभल गई।

लेकिन राजेश वापस नहीं लौटा।

सियाचिन की बर्फीली खामोशी में उस दिन एक और सैनिक की कहानी अमर हो गई।

उसके साथी उसकी जेब से एक मुड़ी हुई चिट्ठी निकाल पाए।

वही चिट्ठी।

उसकी बहन की।

और उसके साथ एक छोटा-सा कागज।

उस पर सिर्फ एक वाक्य लिखा था—

“मेरी आखिरी साँस भी अगर देश के काम आ जाए, तो समझना मैं हारकर नहीं गया।”

---

राजेश की खबर उसके घर पहुँची।

माँ ने कुछ नहीं कहा।

बस उसके कमरे में जाकर उसकी वर्दी को छुआ।

पिता ने तिरंगे को सलाम किया।

बहन ने वह राखी निकालकर अपने हाथ में रख ली।

घर में रोना था।

लेकिन उस रोने के बीच गर्व भी था।

क्योंकि राजेश ने अपने जीवन का वह वादा पूरा किया था जो उसने बचपन में किया था।

---

लेकिन कहानी यहीं खत्म नहीं हुई।

कई महीनों बाद एक नए जवान की पोस्टिंग उसी चौकी पर हुई।

उसकी पहली रात थी।

बाहर बर्फीली हवा चल रही थी।

अचानक उसे लगा—

जैसे कोई उसके पीछे खड़ा है।

वह पलटा।

एक सैनिक कुछ दूरी पर दिखाई दिया।

वर्दी में।

शांत।

उसने तिरंगे की तरफ देखा।

फिर नए जवान से कहा—

“ड्यूटी संभालो।”

जवान ने पूछा—

“आप कौन हैं?”

सैनिक ने मुस्कुराकर कहा—

“जिसने कल संभाली थी।”

अगले ही पल वह आकृति बर्फीली धुंध में गायब हो गई।

सुबह जवान ने अपने अधिकारी को पूरी बात बताई।

अधिकारी कुछ देर चुप रहे।

फिर उन्होंने राजेश की तस्वीर निकाली।

जवान तस्वीर देखकर स्तब्ध रह गया।

वही चेहरा।

वही आँखें।

वही वर्दी।

अधिकारी ने सिर्फ इतना कहा—

“राजेश को गए हुए कई महीने हो चुके हैं।”

जवान ने बाहर देखा।

तिरंगा हवा में लहरा रहा था।

और बर्फ पर कुछ कदमों के निशान थे।

वे चौकी से शुरू होते थे…

और तिरंगे के पास जाकर खत्म हो जाते थे।

---

आज भी जब सियाचिन की रात बहुत शांत होती है, तो वहाँ के जवान कहते हैं कि कभी-कभी बर्फीली हवा में किसी के कदमों की आवाज़ सुनाई देती है।

किसी को राजेश दिखाई देता है या नहीं—

यह कोई नहीं जानता।

लेकिन एक बात हर जवान जानता है।

सीमा की ड्यूटी कभी खत्म नहीं होती।

राजेश का शरीर वहाँ नहीं है।

उसका परिवार उससे दूर है।

उसकी बहन की राखी अब भी शायद उसकी तस्वीर के पास रखी है।

उसकी माँ अब भी शायद दरवाजे की ओर देखती है।

लेकिन सियाचिन की उस चौकी पर तिरंगा आज भी लहरा रहा है।

और जब भी कोई नया जवान उस तिरंगे को सलाम करता है—

शायद कहीं न कहीं राजेश मुस्कुराता होगा।

क्योंकि उसने देश को सिर्फ अपने जीवन से नहीं,

अपनी आखिरी सांस से भी वफादारी दी थी।

और शायद इसीलिए—

कुछ सैनिक मरते नहीं।

वे बस…

एक शरीर से निकलकर
देश की याद बन जाते हैं।

जय हिंद।

Name: Nisha RG
Theme: Husband and wife love , care, and their strength of being together
Title: RAMAN’S SHANKARI
Content:
SHORT STORY -2
Raman’s Shankari
Raman was lying on the hospital bed with the life-saving ventilator and the bedside hospital cardiac monitor constantly making beeping sounds which felt demanding and never-ending. Shankari, with a blank face, caressed him. She looked at him again and again, She felt like he was smiling at her until the gentle pat on her shoulder by the duty nurse made her come around. She walked outside the ICU with a bleeding heart in an untaught state. While walking, she knew there was no hope of recovery for him. Her neighbour, an old friend of Shankari, Sharada, was waiting outside patiently with her breakfast. Sharada, seeing her crestfallen face, could not help but succumb to tears. She wiped her eyes and said, 
“Ayyo Shankari, you look all the more tired. Come and sit here. Please have something. 
Why didn't you drink the tea? “
Shankari remained silent. Her voice was dead with grief and fatigue. Sarada took a steel glass, poured some hot tea from a steel flask and gave it to her. Shankari took the steaming glass filled with tea and drank it. It wetted her already parched tongue and throat. She finished the tea, looked at Sarada and said, 
“ I don't think there is a comeback for him. 
I don’t know what to do or where to go. 
His younger brother, Divakar, took him to the hospital; he was the one covering his medical expenses. 
He went to the hospital canteen to have his breakfast. 
Sarada, I know I cannot ask for more from god. Death is the only respite for him.” 
She took a deep breath, leaned on the wall and closed her eyes. Sarada took the glass from the fragile hands of Shankari. She looked at her old friend and sighed deeply. She had known her since childhood. Sarada is well aware of her situation and how she feels right now. Sarada herself had lost her husband 10 years back. She lives with her youngest Son and family. But in Shankari’s case, she has no one to care for.
Sharada with the steel glass went towards the washbasin which is in the right-hand corner of the floor to wash it off.  After sitting idle for some time, she got up and walked towards the nursing station. There, she met the duty nurse and enquired about Raman’s condition. “Nurse, I want to know about Raman, who was admitted to the ICU. 
Is there any hope?” asked Sharada. 
“No, mother. This time, he is not going to survive. 
His internal organs are in such bad condition. Now he is on a ventilator. 
The doctor will talk to his relatives about removing the ventilator today “ 
said the duty nurse without a tinge of concern. Sharadha walked back with a downward spiral of emotions. Now, what will happen to Shankari? Who will take care of her? 
Even her condition at her Son’s house is appalling. Her daughter-in-law supports her staying because she goes for the 100-day guaranteed work scheme of the government. She sells milk, eggs and receives a meagre widow's pension. 
               Shankari and Raman are childless and homeless. They have been staying in a one-bedroom house for rent for many years now. They had to sell their properties and house for the treatment of Divakar’s daughter, who had cancer 10 years ago. But post-treatment, Divakar’s wife and daughter were against their staying in their house. Divakar remained silent when his wife and daughter mistreated them. Raman never complained. Instead, they tolerated their injustice and dismal surroundings. Later, when the taunting became unbearable, they decided to shift to a rental house. They both sold poori, curry, tea and coffee for a living in the evening. They were happy with whatever meagre amount they could save. But Raman developed an inclination towards alcohol, and soon he became a chronic alcoholic. After drinking, he lays bare his heart. All his suppressed emotions flow out. It was like wearing his emotions on his sleeve. He cried and said, 
“ I am a big failure. Jobless, propertyless and childless. 
Even my parents favoured my brothers and sisters over me”. 
Shankari remained silent. But once he slinks away to sleep, Shankari cries her heart out. However, in the morning, Raman feels sorry for it and asks for her forgiveness. 
Shankari very well knew that Raman loved her from the bottom of his heart. But the problem is that life was unfair to him. He was a man of dreams and ambitions. He loved to study philosophy and art. He painted and sculpted. But his father, Soman was against all this.  He wanted him to study law, practice law, and become a lawyer. His brothers  Chandran and Divakar, though they had ambitions like him, were afraid to go against the wishes of their arrogant, adamant father. The only person who supported him silently was his mother Janaaamma. But his mother could not go against the hard decisions of his father. She had to bear the wrath of her husband for supporting her son, including physical and verbal abuse. But she took it all. She fought for his claim silently with prayers and tears. Raman went to JNU with the support of her mother. His father was so angry that he did not talk to her for a week and slept outside the bedroom on a screwpine mat as though protesting. His mother had high hopes for him. She cried in the dark corridors of their kitchen. Found solace in prayers. Unfortunately, however, Raman found himself caught up in politics and party activities in college. During the initial months of college, he was a keen learner and observer of everything around him. But the temptation to know and try new things was enticing. He drank liquor, took the first puff of a cigarette, travelled to Haridwar for the Kumbha Mela and encountered the Aghoris and Digambars. He was fascinated by their strange esoteric lifestyle. When the news reached his father’s ears about Raman exploring the Aghori way of life, his brothers left for Haridwar immediately. It was a herculean task for them to find Raman among the huge gathering of devotees. At last, when they saw him he was in a mood for nothing. He neither resisted nor made any objections. He smelled of ashes and cannabis. They couldn't accept his present situation. They left for Kerala the next day. After reaching the house, to the horror of his brothers, their father started hitting him with his belt. They tried to dissuade him. Raman felt the seething pain of the belt tearing through his skin. He felt helpless and ashamed. He couldn't complete his studies. His dreams were shattered. He was not allowed to go out without the knowledge of his belligerent father who constantly cursed and abused him with words. His brothers ‘ got into prestigious government services, got married, and had kids and families of their own. But   Raman became a thorn in the side of the entire family. They tried to avoid him on every family occasion. He became an outcaste in his own family. His father's abuses and torments started getting on his nerves and one day he gathered the courage to face him. He lashed out at his father for making his life miserable. He cried, screamed, shouted and even tried to hit his father once. He was caught by his mother who slapped him instantly. He left the house at that moment never to return. His mother kept on calling his name, 
“ My Son Ramu. Don't go away. Please come back. Don't leave your mother. My son, Ramu... Ramu”. 
Her words of appeal made him cry inside out. But he was determined to go, escape from the hard clutches of his father. He left for Mumbai, did odd jobs to survive, made some money and came back to his hometown after 8 long years. 
During this time he had broken off his relations with his family, the death of his father was unknown to him. But he didn't feel a tinge of sadness about the loss of his father but rather a relief. He hated his father by the time he left for Mumbai. His mother was left in the care of a home care nurse much to his surprise. His brothers had brought lands, built houses and shifted with their families. Their ancestral home started to deteriorate. When he came to visit his mother after eight long years he was taken aback seeing his mother. She became thin and frail, with no hair on her head, playing with a plastic toy parrot. She didn't remember him, got annoyed and became grumpy seeing a stranger at home. The nurse at last broke the silence and said, 
“ Are you Raman, Janamma’s son? “. “ Yes I am, “said Raman in a heavy voice. “
Your brothers said you left the house and committed suicide. Your father after hearing the news of your death news collapsed on the floor. He suffered from a paralytic attack and was bedridden for two years. I took care of your father now your mother. She is suffering from Alzheimer's disease. She remembers nothing. Not even her name.” 
said the home nurse sans feelings. 
Raman got up from his chair, moved towards his mother took her hands and pressed them against his face. His eyes became dazed with tears. He kissed his mother on her forehead, left the room and sat on the charpoy of the verandah. Unfortunately, his mother remained oblivious to the moment. The home nurse came looking for him and asked “ 
Are you alright brother?”. He remained silent for some seconds. “ Does my brother come and visit her? “ asked Raman. “
They visit their mother once a month to take her to the hospital. An auto driver Kuttan brings vegetables and provisions. In case of any emergency, I will inform the neighbour Shantha Akka. She has a landline in her house.  Other than these short visits nobody bothers to come here.” 
said the nurse. Shankar sat there for some time, then left. He started visiting his mother daily. On such a visit he met Shankari with Sharada for the first time at a bus stop. This became recurrent as they were studying in an institute providing teacher training. Even Shankari started noticing him. Soon they had their first smile, first meeting, first talk. For all their firsts Sharada became a pleased watcher. Slowly and steadily their relationship grew stronger, and then it became the talk of the town. Shankari’s parents though financially low gave her a good education. Shankari and Sharada aspired to become teachers, but fate had other plans. Bhaskaran Nair a retired headmaster, a friend and confidante of Soman came to visit Raman at his home. Seeing Bhaskaran Nair from a distance Raman stood up and welcomed him warmly. He sat in a chair. 
“Hey Raman what are you up to? How is Janamma? And what about your love story? “ he looked at Raman with a strict demeanour as if a father would. Raman smiled with an uneasy shyness which is alien to him. 
“Uncle, it is high time I speak about her I mean Shankari. Yes, I love her.. No, we are in love…. Yes, I want to marry her.  We want to spend our lives together. Can you help me? I can only rely upon you Uncle. You know because I have none to take care of” 
He spoke with moisture in his eyes.  Bhaskar Nair looked at Raman, smiled and said,” 
Let me talk to her parents.” 
The marriage was a simple ceremony held in the nearby temple followed by a tea party. Her parents were flat broke but they were ready to give her hand to someone. At least she gets saved from this necessitous life. Her marriage saree, thaali was offered by Raman himself. Ramani and Shankari did not live a life in the fast lane but both remained significant others to each other. Sarada saw her son Mani who came to take her home along with him after work. Sarada wiped her tears and said “ Mani can I stay a bit longer today? I think Raman is nearing the end of his life. Shankari needs me my son.”. Her son looked at Shankari sitting on the chair with her head leaning against the wall. He had known her since childhood. Mani said 
,” Amma we both must stay by her side. Let us be together in this”. 
Sarada nodded. She looked at Sankari who was sitting on a chair with closed eyes leaning her head on the wall. Sarada knew she was powerless to steer the direction of the wheel of her life. What after Raman? . This question was haunting her since Raman’s health condition worsened. His brothers considered her a thorn in their side. She took a deep breath and walked towards her. She saw Raman’s brothers coming out of the doctor’s cabin. After some time, two doctors, three nurses and a compounder went inside the ICU. Sharada realised what was happening inside. Raman’s fate is sealed. She said a silent prayer to herself. Divakar called Mani to his side. They talked for hardly 3 minutes. Mani came back, looked at Sharada and said,” Amma his body will be taken to the crematorium. They just want to finish off the hospital formalities. They are not interested in paying any homage to him. Also, Chandran uncle asked me to take Shankari aunty to an old age home in Trivandrum. 
He will pay me travel expenses for that. 
Amma how will we tell this to Shankari aunty? asked Mani. 
“ Son give me some time to talk to her” said Shankari wiping her tears.
She sat down, with trembling hands she touched the hands of Shankari. She tried to wake her up. Shankari opened her eyes. 
“ Shankari everything is over. He is no more. His brothers are here. They are taking him to the crematorium. They even asked Mani to take you to an old age home.” Sharada said without looking into the face of Shankari. 
She nodded and sighed heavily. “ Amma it will take almost an hour for the official formalities to be completed. The bill is not yet ready” said Mani.
Shankari closed her eyes, sans tears. Her face was composed. She did not scream, yell, cried her heart out just leaned her head against the wall. It felt like ages waiting for the bill to get paid. After an hour or something Raman’s brothers, their kids and some men from the neighbourhood walked alongside a body. Nobody bothered to stop or ask Shankari to have a final look. Sharada and Mani looked at each other. His body passed them. She tried to wake up Shankari. It was when she touched her face that Sharada realised that she could never wake her up. Shankari entered her eternal rest with Raman to another. Thus without the last adieu, she left Sharada to mourn.

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Self love, learning to love yourself after hating yourself, forgiveness.
Title: An awkward first date (Me and myself).
Content:
Silence stretches between both of us as we sit together for a coffee date.
This silence is really loud, and, my thoughts seem a lot louder, this just feels awkward
I can't really cherish the moment when its with you, it feels different, a little uneasy
I've hated you for so long, I've sometimes worked against you, I've hurt you
I've personally run a blade across your tender skin, I've despised you inside and out
I want you to be someone else, I want you to behave differently! I want someone strong, confident, muscular, productive. I want someone who can lift me easily.
I want someone who takes care of themselves every single day.
I want someone who is happy.
And you don't even brush your teeth daily, and you don't even shower.
You're like a stick and so incredibly skinny.
You shout at your parents and friends and you hurt them sometimes.
But here I am, and here you are, so I guess we're willing to try again?

This feels really awkward and uncomfortable.
"We're so far apart." You tell me. "We're literally miles away. How do we meet at the same page, ever?"
"It's okay." I tell you. "We'll just take one step forward every day, just forward instead of back, and one day, we'll meet on the same page."
I hope my sincerity shines through in my actions, even if this doesn't feel amazing to you at first. Maybe its uncomfortable.
But I prepared this coffee date table for you and chose the cloth of your favourite colour. Maybe your thoughts are racing and you're not fully in the moment.
But its okay, even if its not exactly how I hoped it'd be.

I really want to take care of you.
I really want to cherish you and love you the hardest during your worst moments
You told me you're afraid of pain, well, in pain I want to look after you really well
Maybe it might hurt less, eventually, I'll keep trying
The first date is really awkward, it feels uncomfortable, and what are we even doing?
I awkwardly take sips of my coffee just to break the ice, and you keep staring away.
But at least we both managed to sit down, and try together.
And if we try enough times, maybe it wouldn't be awkward at all.
We're meant to be together in this lifetime and we have our whole lives ahead of us.
One day at a time, and I hope that eventually when I try, try and try again
One day it'll hit you, and one day we might laugh together at a joke
And one day we might even meet at the same page, the version of each other we both wanted to see
We're just going to try, and eventually, I'm going to be comfortable with you.
I know you already, I just feel like I don't love you. But one day, eventually
We'll meet each other at the same page.
We'll not feel awkward anymore.
The silence will still exist between you and me, but, it won't hurt.
One day.
But for today, let's just take one step forward.

I wish you were someone else, but, while you become that person
I'm still going to love you just the same.

Name: V G VYSAKH
Theme: The poem explores the harsh reality of modern society, where young minds entering academic institutions—promised education, opportunity, and true freedom are instead trapped and choked by the invisible, oppressive chains of caste, religion, politics, and gender bias. It highlights how these toxic divisions destroy individual potential and human essence. Ultimately, it serves as a powerful call to shatter these artificial walls, reminding us that humanity is one and that the gift of conscious thought (BORN TO TROUTH) was given to unite and elevate mankind, not to divide and destroy it.
Title: BORN TO TROUTH
Content:
Under the veil of dawn, the campus gates swing wide,
Welcoming eager minds, where boundless dreams reside.
Yet shadows lurk in corners, where colors divide,
Casting poisoned labels on every human side.
Red, blue, and green, the fluttering banners rise,
Feeding grand illusions built on hollow lies.
They promise education, a brilliant guiding light,
While tightening iron chains to choke away the sight.
Success is caged and cornered by political decree,
Judged by factional colors, not what a soul can be.
Break down the walls of caste, of dogma, and of creed,
We must unite as one for humanity’s sole need.
The seventh sense was given to question and to think,
Not to build up hatred or push men to the brink,
Not to fracture futures or start a bitter war,
We are human beings, and we are so much more.

Name: Aman Kashyap
Title: Catonia soaked her last rays
Content:
The sun rose 
And touched 
The island of Ebulloy
As the sun 
Showered,
Drops of life on
the land, creatures
woke,
Breathing peace,
enriching security,
And advancing buoyancy
Their visions made
the skies smile blue
effervescence,
As Catonia towers,
She imbibes
The rays and spreads 
Her wings of leaves
Her roots,
Drink the rays and
crystalise
And enlighten the land
golden 
As they nourish the Truffelians
As they offer,
Their scrumptious meals
To the island
As they educate the Wisolians
As they breathe their astute
wisdom,
Into the island's air
As they embolden the Glarions
For their unbridled
Courage and bravery 
After the sun sleeps
Grimbook,
Arrives of on the island
The bearer of the red axe
The hunter with a thousand aims
And gifted with a bow,
To never let him falter 
From his sight
As the night rose 
And eclipsed 
All the worries 
Two sides unaware
Grimbook advanced,
Using his bow,
Not losing sight
Of the towering Catonia 
The Truffelians 
The Wisolians
The Glarions 
Wrapped up in the
night's darkness,
And the silence of
twinkling dreams
Or maybe safeguarded
From the morning's 
Impending
Nightmare,
The stars turning into
Fireballs of doom
And crashing
The golden land
turned barren 
The skies roared,
blood and agony 
The meals stagnate 
The wisdom loses
The bravery betrays and
Falters 
As Catonia soaked her last rays

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Title: Salvation
Content:
9 days out of 10 I pick myself up and start over
I tell myself I don't even need a reason to continue
When storms hit, just get up and walk again
But these days, I just can't seem to do that
I've lost my spark, I'm a burnt out match
What's the point of hoping and wishing if every day your entire being burns as if on fire?
Is this what my life has been reduced to? I wish I could be happy once again
I'm tired, all I've been inhaling is black smoke from my own body burning up, I can't catch a breath

I've lost my light, so lend me yours for a day
Bring your glowing match towards mine and light mine up and we'll glow as two now
When all the time I'm burning, give me a breath of the freshest air
Fill up my lungs and I'll drink it up desperately
Give me a change, a breath of air, a shot of life again, so that even if I'm not moving forward, I stand where I am and take a quiet breath

I've looked at the sky so many times hoping for something different
I feel as if I shut my eyes in the dark night, and when I open it, I expect light to be there somehow
I temporarily take a rest, but when I open my eyes, nothing seems to get better, so nothing helps
Even if you can't fix anything, make a brief light shine in my darkened gaze
I'm tired of looking up and yearning for something that's different 
So please lift up my chin and make me look above 

Carry my pain for a moment and make it dissolve
Give me the salvation that only you can give
Temporarily light up my life, so even if everything's dark, I'll look for the next spark that you produce
Never believed in everything happening for a reason, I don't know if I believe in getting stronger from pain anymore
Everything's crushing me and some days I can't see the point, so I no longer believe.
But I believe in you.

Name: MANJUNATH J
Title: Are You Sure?
Content:
I was deleting useless screenshots from my phones one night, the room dark, the only light a pale blue glow breathing against tired faces.

Random images. Blurred moments. Things that meant nothing anymore.

Tap. Select. Delete.

And then the screen asked "Are you sure you want to delete this?"

Are you sure.

Three simple words. Programmed. Mechanical. Cold. Yet somehow... kinder than some people.

Because even a machine hesitates before erasing something it once stored.

It pauses. It confirms. It gives a warning that once it's gone, it may never return.

But in real life?

Some people delete hearts without a notification. No "Are you sure?" No "This action cannot be undone." No final conversation.

Just silence.

Just distance growing like a crack in glass until everything shatters quietly.

Even devices understand that deletion is permanent. That removing something should require intention.

But some humans erase years as if love were just storage space taking up too much room.

No courtesy. No explanation. No dignity for the memories that once felt eternal.

And what makes it darker-

Even trash has a folder. Even deleted files go to a recycle bin, a small mercy where regret can still breathe.

But when relationships end without a word, there is no recycle bin. No archive of what was felt. No recovery option.

Just absence.

Just the echo of what once existed lingering like a notification that will never be opened again.

It's strange, isn't it?

Metal and code are designed to respect loss. To ask for confirmation. To give a second chance.

Yet some hearts don't even pause before pressing delete.

And every time the screen asks, "Are you sure?"

It reminds us

Even a machine knows the weight of erasing something.

If only everyone did.

Name: Megha Vicky Sonkla
Title: वो यहीं है
Content:
चाहती हूँ न लिखूँ उसे,
न लिखूँ उसके बारे में,
न उसका ज़िक्र करूँ।

पर कैसे?

जब भी लिखने लगती हूँ,
वो कलम में आकर बैठ जाता है,
उँगलियों से लिपट जाता है,
और हर वो शब्द, काग़ज़ पर उतरने से पहले
ज़ेहन में आता है, उसमें पसर जाता है।

और बात तो सही है—
जब से गया है वो मुझे छोड़कर,
असल में वो तो यहीं है,

मुझमें।

मेरे हर ख़याल में,
मेरे हर सवाल में,
मेरी हर बात में,
मेरी हर ख़ामोशी में,

तो कैसे न लिखूँ उसे,
कैसे न लिखूँ उसके बारे में,
कैसे न उसका ज़िक्र करूँ,

क्योंकि मेरा हर शब्द वही है,
असल में वो यहीं है...

Name: Sakshi Singh
Content:
Two seventeen in the dead of night,
The world was still, the moon was white.
The clock stood frozen, the silence grew,
Then something whispered, “I see you.”

Three slow knocks came from the door,
Then came three knocks… from the floor.
I held my breath and asked, “Who’s there?”
A voice replied, “You’re not alone in here.”

The window opened on its own,
A breath of ice crossed through the room.
The curtains moved, though there was no breeze,
And something whispered through the trees.

I turned around—there was no one,
Yet footsteps came, one by one.
Closer… closer… then they stopped,
Right beside me… and then they dropped.

I looked at the mirror on the wall,
My reflection wasn’t there at all.
A stranger stood where I should be,
Smiling silently back at me.

I shut my eyes and counted ten,
Opened themand there it was again.
But this time, standing by my side,
Was something wearing the face I hide.

The clock struck two seventeen once more,
Though I had broken it long before.
A voice came softly from behind—
“You’ve been looking for me all this time.”

I turned around. The room was bare,
No footsteps, no shadow anywhere.
Then slowly, my reflection smiled…
While I stood frozen, terrified.

The mirror whispered one last line,
And every breath inside me died

“She is gone. You are still here…
But I am the one looking through your eyes.”

Name: Ruma Chakraborty
Title: Loving
Content:
LOVING 
I got used to
taking up the whole bed when I slept,
Not cower or squeeze in one corner,
Waking up to lazy mornings,
not cooking on Sundays,
Letting dust collect and roost
Coming back home whenever I wanted.

I got used to
not having to explain myself,
Seeking permission for small things
and doing what I love
without anyone criticising me.
I drank, till intoxicated, the
Sound of my own voice,
Long forgotten in disciplined silence.

I got used to
eating at midnight, under the moon
and watching my favourite shows on the Net.
Singing out loud
and dancing around the house, 
My House.

I got used to
receiving calls all the time
and answering messages very late,
going out solo, 
travelling every other weekend,
This journey with me, 
Didn't know it felt this good...

I got used to
the smell of coffee in the morning
and walking barefoot in the garden,
being late when it's my turn to get ready
and cancelling appointments at the last minute
just because.
I got used to
me,
my things,
my life
Being alone...
And for the first time 
I lived...

Name: abhaya nakade
Title: कसे सांगू?
Content:
कसे सांगू?
कसे सांगू ते भाव मनी काय,
ना ते कळे कोणाला.
नाते हे जगावेगळे आपुले,
कसे सांगू कोणाला.
बोलनी खूप, बोलनही,
न बोललेले जाणे माझा कान्हा.
मनी उमलती सख्याचे भाव,
असा तो माझा पाठीीराखा.
कसे सांगू माझे भाव कोणाला?
ना कळे हे नाते.
जरी नसे तू जवळी माझ्या,
तरी वसे अंतरी माझ्या.
कशी सांगू तुझी ओढ मनी लागे,
जशी विठ्ठला लागे ओढ
आपुल्या लेकरांची.
तशी मला लागे ओढ
तुझ्या सख्यप्रितीची.
क्षणाक्षणाला वाढत जाई,
आस तुझ्या सहवासाची.
मनी अनंत भाव त्याचे,
मुखी मात्र हास्य सदा.
अंतरी भावनांचा अथांग सागर,
कसे सांगू कोणाला?
कधी सखा, कधी बंधू,
कधी पुत्र, कधी मायबाप.
असे हे जगावेगळे,
आपुले अनोखे नाते.
कसे सांगू हे भावनांचे नाते
आपल्या लोकांना?
ज्यांनी उमजला नाही कृष्ण,
ते काय जाणती या प्रेमाला?
कसे सांगू कोणाला,
हे आपुले अजब नाते.
शब्द हरवती वाटेवर,
प्रेमाची नाळ अंतरी अखंड नांदे.
— लेखिका : अभया नकाडे ❤️

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Learning to love yourself again after hating yourself
Title: An awkward first date (Me and myself).
Content:
An awkward first date (Me and myself)

Silence stretches between both of us as we sit together for a coffee date.
This silence is really loud, and my thoughts seem a lot louder; this just feels awkward.
I can't really cherish the moment when it's with you; it feels different, a little uneasy.
I've hated you for so long, I've sometimes worked against you, I've hurt you.
I've personally run a blade across your tender skin; I've despised you inside and out.
I want you to be someone else, I want you to behave differently! I want someone strong, confident, muscular, productive. I want someone who can lift me easily.
I want someone who takes care of themselves every single day.
I want someone who is happy.
And you don't even brush your teeth daily, and you don't even shower.
You're like a stick and so incredibly skinny.
You shout at your parents and friends, and you hurt them sometimes.
But here I am, and here you are, so I guess we're willing to try again?

This feels really awkward and uncomfortable.
"We're so far apart," you tell me. "We're literally miles away. How do we meet at the same page, ever?"

"It's okay," I tell you. "We'll just take one step forward every day, just forward instead of back, and one day, we'll meet on the same page."
I hope my sincerity shines through in my actions, even if this doesn't feel amazing to you at first. Maybe it's uncomfortable.
But I prepared this coffee date table for you and chose the cloth of your favourite colour. Maybe your thoughts are racing and you're not fully in the moment.
But it's okay, even if it's not exactly how I hoped it'd be.

I really want to take care of you.
I really want to cherish you and love you the hardest during your worst moments.
You told me you're afraid of pain; well, in pain, I want to look after you really well.
Maybe it might hurt less, eventually; I'll keep trying.
The first date is really awkward, it feels uncomfortable, and what are we even doing?
I awkwardly take sips of my coffee just to break the ice, and you keep staring away.
But at least we both managed to sit down and try together.
And if we try enough times, maybe it wouldn't be awkward at all.
We're meant to be together in this lifetime, and we have our whole lives ahead of us.
One day at a time, and I hope that eventually, when I try, try and try again,
one day it'll hit you, and one day we might laugh together at a joke.
And one day we might even meet at the same page, the version of each other we both wanted to see.
We're just going to try, and eventually, I'm going to be comfortable with you.
I know you already; I just feel like I don't love you. But one day, eventually,
we'll meet each other at the same page.

We'll not feel awkward anymore.
The silence will still exist between you and me, but it won't hurt.
One day.
But for today, let's just take one step forward.

I wish you were someone else, but while you become that person,
I'm still going to love you just the same.

Name: Dipanwita Dey
Title: Earth's Lovely Lullabies
Content:
Earth's Lovely Lullabies
Once we have chained our souls with grown-up fears,
When the raindrops wash the earth’s worn face,
The years have washed our childish grace,
As we have worn our masks throughout the years.

Then I saw a caterpillar change, twirling,
Attaching a silky pad to its chrysalis,
And transforming into a butterfly,
Flying free as its wings start unfurling.

“Please tell me why you stopped playing?” she says.
I have no words, just tears staining my skin,
And a smile belonged to her within.
Her voice was the mist on those rainy days.

Once the final raindrop quietly falls,
I heard my name within the distant calls.

From the stunning colors, lively greeting,
I held her hands and we laughed  we were free.
Within this rain, she walked and danced with me,
Then the nightly dreams began retreating.

Understanding my mind must not go back there,
The smile I thought had disappeared for good,
Returned  the blessing where we once had stood.
We ran in the dark corridors of the night’s air,

Far from the icy grips of a full moon,
Resting, waiting for their splendor to soar.
The night’s shadows fade, and the sun rays roar,
Warming the earth ,the sun is near high noon.

Now enjoying life’s nectar, like my butterfly,
Whose beauty is the earth’s lovely lullaby.

Name: Bijoyalaxmi  Mohapatra
Title: MY FIRST BRUSH WITH LOVE
Content:
MY FIRST BRUSH WITH LOVE
Any person goes through a sea change in life during their teens. Teens are a difficult phase of life, irrespective of whether you are brought up in a small town, a big city, or born into a rich or low-income family. 
This is a phase where approval or validation from both elders and peers matters. The choices you make, or the mistakes you make, may impact your life forever. This is the time when even the most studious kids at school start taking an interest in the opposite sex. Adjectives like “attractive”, “charming”, “good-looking”, and “beautiful” are all that one wants to hear. Everybody wants to be in love or be loved.
Maya was a small-town girl in her teens. She was the second child and felt neglected at home as her all-rounder elder sister and her naughty younger sister received all the attention, both at home and school. 
Everyone around Maya found her beautiful and frequently mentioned it. Her parents never reinforced it at home, and she never took the comment to heart. But hearing those words in her teens felt reassuring. Maya was average in her studies; she looked plump, and her crooked teeth made her hesitant to smile. She began to stoop and lost her confidence. Her mother advised her to join swimming. But she didn't join swimming classes because she worried she wouldn't look good in a swimming costume. Menstruation and an evolving body tortured her more. The last nail in the coffin was the arrival of her new classmate, Meera from Delhi. She had a figure to die for, long, beautiful, thick, lustrous hair. Meera knew she was attractive and would flaunt her perfect legs in short dresses. All the boys in her school were really into her. She felt she had lost the last chance to find a boyfriend. She would always ask her best friend, Molly, to read her palm and predict when she would find her Mr. Perfect. 
Maya was in the 9th standard that year, and her father appointed a tuition teacher to help her with her studies. The teacher was a young boy and an excellent student studying at IIT Kharagpur. His name was Sujoy Chatterjee. They were formally introduced, and the next week he started teaching her. 
Maya was very shy and never looked him in the eye during her tuition classes. She didn't find him handsome at first, though her elder sister spoke volumes about his charm. To break the ice between them, Sujoy always showed interest in Maya's likes, dislikes, interests, fears, and confusions, not only as a student but also as a person. He often quoted incidents from his school days to draw parallels and make Maya feel that all children her age behaved the same way, felt the same emotions, and that nothing was wrong with her. Slowly, Maya felt confident and expressed herself better. Sujoy treated her as an equal. At times, he would ask her for her opinion on certain topics concerning him. Nobody had ever asked for Maya’s opinion before. She felt important because Sujoy treated her as an equal. At times, Maya would also share many incidents from school with Sujoy. They exchanged views on many topics. By the end of the year, they had become good friends. 
She was in the 10th standard now, and it was a crucial year for her. Maya had started admiring Sujoy for his sincerity, intelligence, and charm. She would look forward to meeting him every week. Slowly, tuition classes began to feel like little dates. Maya would steal moments during these tuition classes to admire his striking smile, his lovely eyes with long, curly eyelashes, his blemish-free fair complexion, and cherry-red lips. On many occasions, he called her beautiful, innocent, a rare combination at her age. He said, I have never met a girl like you before. He would teasingly ask whether she had a boyfriend, and if yes, it would break his heart and make him jealous. Sujoy said, "I am sure many boys in your school like you." He was the first man to treat her like this. Maya was falling in love with him.
One day, Sujoy left his pen and his umbrella by mistake at Maya’s house. Maya touched the umbrella's fabric; it was soft and silky and smelled awesome. Coincidentally, the pen also smelled the same. The fragrance was “Old Spice Aftershave Lotion,” and the smell tickled Maya’s senses; she imagined Sujoy would kiss her one day. The fateful day arrived when Sujoy kissed her, but Maya did not enjoy it a bit. On the contrary, she felt humiliated, dirty, as if somebody treated her like trash. It felt more like lust than love. She was hurt and angry; Sujoy was scared, his face turned red, and he realized he had made a mistake. He apologized, and he left. Maya could not study peacefully for a few days. Sujoy gathered the courage and came back to teach her. Silence and discomfort hung between them. Since Maya was madly in love, she forgave him to ease things between them.
Now Sujoy found excuses to touch her, hold her hand, and pull away slowly whenever he felt her parents approaching. She felt butterflies in her stomach whenever his hand touched hers. Maya loved his touch, comforting, reassuring. Falling in love is a lovely feeling. The same monotonous life becomes exciting, and each day feels blissful. People in love say sweet nothings to each other. Maya often felt distracted from her studies and tried very hard to concentrate. All year, Maya waited for Sujoy to profess his love for her. She was dying to hear the three magical words “I LOVE YOU”. But Sujoy never said them. Maya expected him to make promises like, “I will stay in touch” and “I will come back next year to see you.” Maya was so much in love with Sujoy that she wanted to marry him and grow old with him. 
Maya could not gather the courage to open her heart to him. Firstly, she was young, a schoolgirl, and did not want to be ridiculed. Second, Sujoy was from a wealthy family, and Maya’s family was humble. At times, Sujoy gave the impression as if he was enjoying harmless flirting. This dichotomy was very painful for a teenager. 
Finally, Maya’s board exams were over, and Sujoy completed his final year of engineering. Sujoy got a job at a renowned company. He took Maya out to dinner to celebrate. Throughout the evening, Maya kept waiting for Sujoy to propose. But it never happened. The next day, he met Maya at her home to say a final goodbye. He had to catch a train in an hour. Sujoy said, “All the best, Maya” “Study Well”. We will meet again after my convocation. Normally, Sujoy used to say, “When do we meet next?” at the end of every tuition class. Maya terribly missed this phrase. She knew in her heart he would never come back. Maya wanted to hug him and say she loved him and couldn’t live without him. Her life would be meaningless without him. But she couldn't say it, and she watched him leave. It was ripping her heart. Still, she stood there and waved at him with a smile.
Molly, Maya’s friend, visited her that same evening, and when she asked about Sujoy, Maya cried bitterly. She said she couldn't tell him how much she loved him, and that he left forever. Her first love will always remain unrequited. Molly said nothing; her eyes welled up too. She just hugged her tight and let her cry as long as she wanted, till she felt better.

Name: Tanay Bhushan Desai
Title: A Prayer for Her
Content:
God…
if You’re listening,
listen to me the way only You can—
through the cracks in my voice,
through the tears I’m too tired to wipe away.

I love her.
Not just the bright part she shows the world,
but the tired,
quiet,
broken corners she hides like wounds
she thinks no one could love.

I love her sadness
like it is a language only my heart was built to speak.
I love the silence she sinks into when she’s hurting.
I love the way she keeps walking
even when the world keeps taking pieces of her.

And God…
I don’t want to fix her,
I just want to be beside her
while she finds her way back to herself.

So hear me—
give me your sign,
take my hand,
we will be fine.
Promise I won’t let You down.
Just know that she doesn’t have to do this alone.
Promise… I’ll never let her down.

I would take every sin she carries,
every weight,
every shadow—
put it on my shoulders,
on my skin,
on my bones—
if it means she can breathe without shaking.

And her laugh, God…
Her laugh is the most beautiful sound
You ever created.
It stops my heart,
every time,
like heaven paused for a moment
just to listen.

I am crying not because I am weak
but because it hurts to love someone
this deeply,
this helplessly,
this honestly.

So, God…
please keep her safe
when I can’t reach her.
Keep her warm
when the world turns cold.
Let her feel my presence
parallel to hers—
right beside her
even when she cannot see me.

Because I choose her.
In this life.
In the next.
In every silent prayer
my heart has ever whispered.

Name: Divya Iyer
Title: Ganpati Bappa Morya
Content:
There is a particular kind of tiredness that belongs only to Mumbai. It is the tiredness of the 8:47 fast local, of lunches eaten standing, of ambitions that wake up before we do. We move through this city like trains on a timetable ..efficient, punctual, and slightly numb. And then, one monsoon evening, the first dhol sounds through the lanes, and something inside us remembers that we are not machines. We are devotees. And our most beloved guest has arrived!!
This is the part I find endlessly moving..the most overworked people in the country find time for Bappa. Not because they have it.. nobody in Mumbai has time .. but because they would not dream of letting Him wait. The man who skipped his own wedding anniversary dinner will be home before the aarti. The woman who takes calls through family functions will keep her phone face-down, because Bappa eats first. When you love someone this much, time is not found.. it is created. Ganesh Chaturthi is proof that Mumbai's heart was never as busy as its calendar.
And observe what the festival does to the act of eating. In this city, we eat like we are refuelling vehicles. But for ten days, the first modak of the season is not eaten.. it is offered. Hands are joined. Eyes are closed. Gratitude is spoken aloud before a single bite. In a life where we are always reaching for the next thing, this festival insists we begin with thankfulness. That pause .. that one pause before the first morsel .. is perhaps the most radical act a Mumbaikar performs all year.
Then comes Visarjan, and here the festival turns profound. For ten days we have dressed Him, fed Him, sung to Him, loved Him as our own. And then, with drums and dancing and tears that we don't bother to hide, we carry Him to the sea and let Him go. Mumbai .. a city that clings to everything, to flats and jobs and grievances ..shows us, once a year, how to release with grace and even with joy. Nothing stays, and that is precisely why everything is precious. Bappa leaves so that we learn to hold things lightly, and love them fully while they are here.
And look at who stands in the immersion crowd.. every kind of Mumbaikar there is. The chairman and the delivery boy, soaked to the bone, chanting the same words. In front of Bappa, Mumbai forgets its favourite question  "What do you do?" Here, everyone is simply a child of Bappa!! For ten days, Mumbai remembers what it truly is .. not a city of strangers rushing past each other, but a family, gathered around one beloved guest, finally, wonderfully home.
So what's the takeaway for the rest of the 355 days? Steal the festival's structure, not just its dates. Feed your people first .. literally and emotionally. Protect one evening where the phone waits and the family eats. Celebrate small wins properly, loudly, with modak-level enthusiasm. And once in a while, visarjan something .. a worry, an old complaint, a grudge, a hurt.. into the sea of the past, and dance your hearts out while doing it.
Ganesh Chaturthi is Mumbai's annual reminder: we are not machines that commute. We are people who, given half a reason and one beloved guest, will happily lose track of time. May Bappa bless us that we carry atleast one-tenth of that spirit into the other ten months!!
Ganpati Bappa Morya!!

Name: Pulak Patra(Asher Graves)
Title: Zephyr's Daffodil
Content:
For centuries the estranged pagan was trapped in enmities.
Lost in its world.
Blurred between the lines.
It grew
Deranged, degraded, desolate, distasteful
As if
Those were the only tongue it spoke.

Dormant, docile, depressing
Were its routine
Can’t fathom normalcy
So stopped doing it completely 
Change seemed futile after all.

Tired of the ramifications
 Solitude drove the hollow doll.
It grew colder like pride.
Hopelessly narrating its soulless stride.
Hoping for a slice of life.
But every opportunity life threw
It dodged like an expert fellow god.
Stupendous and done with its tomfoolery 
Life greets it with goodbyes.
Hopeless now it continues.
To exist is enough 
It says but that’s a blatant lie.
Any hope and it jumps back like a scared kitty on the roadside!
Miraculously, 
It stumbled upon a miracle bride.
Hesitant still but desperation drives.
It extended its hand with a weakening smile!
Bracing for impact, expecting lies.
But to its surprise
Her hands didn’t lie 
The excitement it felt can’t be summarised.
Adrenaline rush felt shy at its sight
For the first time in centuries the estranged pagan felt butterflies~
Oh, how wonderful it is to live.
How sweet is everything!
How beautiful is life!!
But happiness of this extent is short-lived.
The canvas felt “Too Sweet” to dye
Yet again fate rolled its die
Beautiful life turned to a blatant lie
And as he looked up to meet her eye
She vanished
Leaving nothing behind
As if a breeze blew her away from the site
And as it started to leave her side
Just then the Zephyr’s Daffodil arrived! 
For centuries the estranged pagan held back.
But this time…
This time 
“He” speaks with flowing fire.
He speaks and speaks and speaks.
Every word’s intensity growing louder.
Higher, until he couldn’t.

The solid ground became a quagmire.
But his words were too heavy to retire.
Nature felt pity for him 
Thus, it rained for quite a while!
The pagan now like a vicious arachnid 
Down the ladders of frenzied spirals
Felt all sorts of emotions 
But no word could extrapolate the description
Inexplicable expression became pleading hands
But what’s gone is gone
No one’s exempt!
The pagan asks with a weak voice.
“Why me?” 
But that’s a story for another time
For now, please accept 
The final line
Woven with a beautiful lie
A resting place for the wandering knight.

Like a Ferris wheel on a meadowed hill 
A standstill or Zephyr’s Daffodil.

-Pulak Patra(Asher Graves)

Name: Dr. Pradeep Babu
Title: " सड़क का जाम या गिलास का जाम (जाम ही जाम) "
Content:
" सड़क का जाम या गिलास का जाम (जाम ही जाम) "
चारों ओर लगा है जाम,
रुका हुआ है सारा काम।
सड़क पर गाड़ियों की कतार,
हर कोई है बड़ा लाचार।
बोले कोई—“जल्दी जाना है”,
कोई बोले—“देर हो जाना है।”
हॉर्न बजें सुबह से शाम,
भाई! चारों ओर लगा है जाम। 
घर से निकले लेकर काम,
रास्ते में मिल गया जाम तमाम।
आगे बस और पीछे कार,
बीच में फँसा स्कूटर सवार।
हॉर्न बजा-बजा थक जाएँ,
गाड़ी फिर भी आगे न जाए।
दफ्तर छूटा, छूटी ट्रेन,
मिला नही हमे कही भी चैन,
चेहरे पर दिखने लगी परेशानी गंभीर।
मंजिल पास, मगर बेकार,
जाम ने करा दिया इंतजार।
ट्रैफिक वाला हाथ उठाए,
सबको धीरे-धीरे समझाए।
“भाई, धीरज थोड़ा धरना,
हॉर्न बजाकर क्या है करना?”
कोई बोले—“मेरी गलती नहीं”,
दूजा बोले—“मेरी गलती नहीं।”
सबके अपने-अपने काम,
किसके कारण लगा ये जाम?
बहस हुई और बढ़ा बवाल,
जाम बना है मजेदार सवाल।
शाम हुई तो बदला नाम,
गिलासों में सजने लगा जाम।
एक बोला—“आज है आराम”,
दूजा बोला—“भर दो जाम।”
पहला जाम गया मुस्काकर,
दूजा पहुँचा लड़खड़ाकर।
तीसरे ने जब खोला ज्ञान,
सबने पकड़े अपने कान!
घरवाली बोली—“बस भी करो,
कल फिर सड़क का जाम भरो!”
सड़क का जाम करे परेशान,
गिलास का जाम करे हैरान।
एक में गाड़ी रुकती जाए,
दूजे में हाथ पैर डगमगाएँ।
एक में देर से पहुँचे धाम,
दूजे में भूलें अपना नाम।
दोनों का है अपना काम—
एक सड़क पर, दूजा गिलास में जाम l
जाम जिंदगी में आते हैं,
रुककर फिर चलना सिखलाते हैं।
मुश्किल में भी रखना धीर,
हँसकर रहना सदा गंभीर।
रास्ता चाहे हो बदनाम,
हँसते-हँसते काटो जाम।
सड़क खुले या बीते शाम,
जीवन चलता रहे अविराम।
यही जिंदगी का है पैगाम—
रास्ते में आए लाखों जाम,
मुस्कुराकर चलते रहो,
मत रुकने दो जीवन का काम।
डा.प्रदीप बाबू 
देहरादून (उत्तराखण्ड)
