Name: P. NITHYANANDHI
Theme: Father of invention in Class room teaching
Title: SICK AT HEART
Content:
SICK AT HEART
The classroom was unusually quiet that Monday morning. The Blackboard stood silently against the wall, while a small piece of chalk rested beside it. Once, they had been the centre of every lesson.
“Hi, my dear friend,” said the Chalk Piece. “Shall we go outside and play?”
The Blackboard looked at him. “Why, Whity? Today is Monday. Students will come to the classroom.”
The Chalk Piece looked around the empty room. “But nowadays, we are used very less in the classroom.”
The Blackboard remained silent for a moment. Then it sighed. “I feel sick at heart, Whity. All the students are keen on smart classes now.”
“What is a smart class?” asked the Chalk Piece.
The Blackboard explained that smart classes used advanced technology and digital media to help students learn. “They are also called digital or new media classrooms. Technology has improved a lot. Everyone seeks new ways.”
The Chalk Piece tried to comfort his old friend. “Don't be piteous, Blacky. We are the fathers of invention in classroom teaching. We have been part of so many lessons and so many students' memories.”
The Blackboard looked at the empty classroom and slowly smiled.
“Perhaps we have to adjust according to time.”
The Chalk Piece rested beside the Blackboard. They knew that the classroom was changing, but they also knew that no new technology could erase the lessons and memories they had written together.

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Self love, learning to love yourself again after hating yourself
Title: An awkward first date (Me and myself).
Content:
Silence stretches between both of us as we sit together for a coffee date.
This silence is really loud, and, my thoughts seem a lot louder, this just feels awkward
I can't really cherish the moment when its with you, it feels different, a little uneasy
I've hated you for so long, I've sometimes worked against you, I've hurt you
I've personally run a blade across your tender skin, I've despised you inside and out
I want you to be someone else, I want you to behave differently! I want someone strong, confident, muscular, productive. I want someone who can lift me easily.
I want someone who takes care of themselves every single day.
I want someone who is happy.
And you don't even brush your teeth daily, and you don't even shower.
You're like a stick and so incredibly skinny.
You shout at your parents and friends and you hurt them sometimes.
But here I am, and here you are, so I guess we're willing to try again?

This feels really awkward and uncomfortable.
"We're so far apart." You tell me. "We're literally miles away. How do we meet at the same page, ever?"
"It's okay." I tell you. "We'll just take one step forward every day, just forward instead of back, and one day, we'll meet on the same page."
I hope my sincerity shines through in my actions, even if this doesn't feel amazing to you at first. Maybe its uncomfortable.
But I prepared this coffee date table for you and chose the cloth of your favourite colour. Maybe your thoughts are racing and you're not fully in the moment.
But its okay, even if its not exactly how I hoped it'd be.

I really want to take care of you.
I really want to cherish you and love you the hardest during your worst moments
You told me you're afraid of pain, well, in pain I want to look after you really well
Maybe it might hurt less, eventually, I'll keep trying
The first date is really awkward, it feels uncomfortable, and what are we even doing?
I awkwardly take sips of my coffee just to break the ice, and you keep staring away.
But at least we both managed to sit down, and try together.
And if we try enough times, maybe it wouldn't be awkward at all.
We're meant to be together in this lifetime and we have our whole lives ahead of us.
One day at a time, and I hope that eventually when I try, try and try again
One day it'll hit you, and one day we might laugh together at a joke
And one day we might even meet at the same page, the version of each other we both wanted to see
We're just going to try, and eventually, I'm going to be comfortable with you.
I know you already, I just feel like I don't love you. But one day, eventually
We'll meet each other at the same page.
We'll not feel awkward anymore.
The silence will still exist between you and me, but, it won't hurt.
One day.
But for today, let's just take one step forward.

I wish you were someone else, but, while you become that person
I'm still going to love you just the same.

Name: Ruma Chakraborty
Title: Unkindest Cut of All
Content:
The butcher wiped his chopper at the edge of the wood block to rid it of the congealing, clotting blood of the slaughtered animal. With something akin to almost nurturing, he inspected the gleaming knife and went quietly back to the hacking of the goat carcass. Lovingly preparing choicest cuts of meat for the connoisseurs of mutton, a delicacy in this part of the country.

As dusk approached, he checked the shop once more with his sweeping glance to make sure it was spotlessly clean. Downing the shutters, he stepped into the darkening alley and turned the corner for the shortcut to his shanty. 

The knife was driven home with a brutality even he did not know. Twisted and pulled out with no thought of precision. Even as he lost consciousness and eventually his life, he grimaced at the disregard for clean cuts and noticed how the bloodied knife was dumped, uncleaned in the dumpster beside him, with his blood congealing in clumpy clots on the blade and hilt.

way of sitting, talking, laughing
everything, everytime he judges
thinking deeply, tries to find out his grudges

rushed to mirror, chopped off her ponytail
now, lookalike a boy
no more grudges, nothing to wail
feels she, in changed boy wear
smiling ear to ear
started chopping her doll's hair
to impress him had tried
with all her might
and then had friends, hangouts, and even late nights
ever since, had refused colours so bright
not only a single, many were
reasons which killed the girl in her

GIRL IN HER!

Name: Gargi Chinchole
Title: The Rapid Fire ✨
Content:
A faded Delhi podcaster named Kabir who’s desperate to revive his dying channel, so he brings on Shastri Ji—an eerie, cryptic astrologer—for a clickbait Q&A called Ek Minute, Sau Sawaal. Kabir hits record and fires off lighthearted questions, but Shastri Ji’s answers are deeply unsettling: when Kabir asks, "Worst zodiac sign?" Shastri Ji rasps, "Scorpio. They carry secrets to the grave," and when Kabir pushes, "Worst time to make a major decision?" Shastri Ji flatly replies, "When you are hiding heartbeats under wet cement." Kabir laughs it off for the camera and his senses get distracted by the immense viewership and online comments engagement , but after editing, he can't stop thinking about those weird hints. He starts cross-referencing Shastri Ji's shady answers online and connects the dots to the famous missing person case of Ananya Sharma. Intrigued, Kabir invites Shastri Ji back for a second podcast, asking pre-planned questions  about astrology deep knowledgable questions on astrology but Shastriji is not able to answer any of them,  he confronts him: "You’re not reading charts, are you? Who are you?" That’s when Shastri Ji drops the act, revealing he’s actually Ananya’s uncle who took on a fake astrologer identity after the police closed her file. He tells Kabir the real motive: Ananya was pregnant with the baby of Vikram Randhawa—the wealthy builder’s son—who murdered her because he was engaged to a powerful Minister’s daughter. Arrogant and eager for justice, Kabir rushes to the local police station to file an FIR, but the corrupt officers laugh in his face: "You want us to open a cold case because a fake pandit told you a ghost story?" Just as Kabir gets into a screaming match with them, the new Station Head—a strict, sharp Inspector—steps in, hands Kabir a glass of water, and says, "Sit down, kid. Tell me everything from the beginning." The Inspector reopens the file and hauls Shastri Ji into the interrogation room, but the old man stays maddeningly mysterious, answering every standard question with riddles about planetary positions. Driven to near madness by Shastri Ji's cryptic responses, the Inspector slams his fist on the table: "Enough with the planetary bullshit!" That’s when Kabir steps up to the one-way glass and suggests, "Sir, traditional questioning won't work on him. Let me run a Rapid Fire." The Inspector agrees, and Kabir sits across from Shastri Ji under the harsh interrogation light, setting a timer on his phone. "Rapid Fire, Shastri Ji. Don't think, just answer," Kabir says, leaning in. "A place with no light?" Shastri Ji replies with a subtle, chilling smile, "Under pillar forty-two, where cold water flows." Kabir hits the table: "A silver object?" Shastri Ji whispers, "A tarnished kada, resting on a crushed wrist." Kabir pushes: "The greatest sin?" Shastri Ji looks straight into the camera: "Silencing a child to save a wedding." Following these subtle hints, the police rush to the Cyber Hub construction site, dig up pillar forty-two, and unearth a buried barrel—officially confirming through forensic testing that it is indeed Ananya’s body. To break Vikram’s political immunity, the forensic team extracts fetal DNA from the remains that proves a direct paternal match to Vikram, while digital investigators recover deleted three-year-old toll plaza CCTV logs placing his private SUV at the site at 2:00 AM. But the ultimate smoking gun comes from inside the cement barrel itself: alongside a crushed glass bezel from Vikram’s designer watch, investigators recover an engraved copper ring wedged directly under the barrel’s base—a ring belonging to Ananya's uncle. Armed with this unshakeable proof, the police corner Vikram Randhawa, who walks into the precinct flanked by high-priced lawyers, sneering at the Inspector, "You dug up a construction site on the words of a lunatic. My father-in-law will have your badge by morning." But Kabir sneaks into the control room, hooks his podcast equipment to the station's PA system, and broadcasts his mic through the entire building. Kabir interrupts through the speakers: "Rapid Fire for you now, Vikram! Why did you kill her?" Blinded by the station lights and furious at the public humiliation, Vikram snaps, screaming at the top of his lungs into the live mic: "Because she was pregnant, alright?! She was going to ruin my marriage to the Minister's daughter! She deserved to rot under that cement!" The whole station falls dead silent as his full confession echoes through the hallway, right in front of the press and top officers. As the Inspector slaps handcuffs on a ruined Vikram, the entire case finally collapses into justice, but the tragedy isn't over. Just a few days later, news breaks that Shastri Ji’s lifeless body has been retrieved near the construction site, holding a small note in his hand that reads: “The karma comes back to everyone so it came back to me.” Shortly after hearing the news, a traumatized Kabir walks out to his car in the pitch-black night, only to find a mysterious wax-sealed envelope resting on his windshield."I didn't need the stars to find her body Kabir,... I dug her grave before I even knew it was hers."







Context:

He breaks the seal to find his own personalized horoscope chart drawn inside, followed by a final, heartbreaking confession written before Shastri Ji's death: three years ago, a dirt-poor Shastri Ji was simply paid cash by site managers to dig a deep trench at midnight without asking questions. When he realized his prized heirloom copper ring had slipped off into the pit, he crept back into the dark to search for it—only to witness Vikram lowering a heavy barrel into the fresh grave, discovering to his absolute horror that the girl being entombed beneath the wet concrete was his beloved niece, the only family he had left. The guilt of digging her grave consumed him, driving him to orchestrate Vikram's downfall before taking his own life. The letter ends with a handwritten line in dried red ink:

Name: Dr.Pradeep Babu

Content:
" वैकुंठ छोड़ आओ गिरधारी "
वैकुंठ छोड़ आओ गिरधारी,
कलियुग हाथ पसारे।

कैसा यह व्यवहार हुआ?
निर्दोषों के हिस्से आखिर,
क्यों इतना अत्याचार हुआ।
कहीं सफर में बस जलती है,
चीखें नभ तक जातीं,
माँ की आँखों के आगे ही,
उसकी दुनिया ढह जाती।
माँ की गोदी सूनी होती,
पिता खड़ा मूरत बनकर,
अपने ही उस लाल को ढूंढे,
आँखों मे सागर भरकर।
किससे पूछें न्याय कहाँ है,
किसको व्यथा सुनाएँ?
आँसू बनकर शब्द सभी अब,
आँखो से बहते जाएँ।
हे मुरलीधर! अब मत देखो,
मौन खड़े उस पार कहीं,
एक बार फिर मुरली बजाओ,
दर्द सुनाई दे रहा है हर कहीं। 
आओ कान्हा, हाथ पकड़ लो,
टूटे मन को थामो तुम,
जिसके घर का दीप बुझा है,
उस घर उजियारा भर दो तुम।
पुत्र पिता को घर से निकाले,
कैसा यह व्यवहार हुआ,
जिसने उँगली थाम चलाया,
आज वही लाचार हुआ।
पति-पत्नी के पावन रिश्ते,
क्यों बनते अब भार यहाँ,
जहाँ प्रेम के फूल खिलें थे,
क्यों उठती दीवार वहाँ?
वैकुंठ छोड़ आओ गिरधारी,
अब मत देर लगाओ,
मुरली की मधुर तान सुनाकर,
मानव को मानवता का पाठ पढ़ाओ।
वैकुंठ छोड़ आओ गिरधारी,
कलियुग हाथ पसारे।
डा. प्रदीप बाबू
देहरादून (उत्तराखण्ड)

For when God,
With intention,
And love,
Brought us together,
I'm reminded why.

For when you pray,
With faith,
And I hear you say,
"God, I pray for us",
I'm reminded why.

For when you plan,
With goals,

Follow God's plan,
I'm reminded why.

For when you smile,
With your eyes,
And see, 
With your heart,
I'm reminded why.

With those strides,

Saying "Hi!"
I'm reminded why.

For when you lead,
With respect,
And ask,

I'm reminded why.

For when you yawn,
With messy hair,
And whisper,
Words of love,
I'm reminded why.

For when you lean in,
With endearment,
And say,
"Baby, my love,"
I'm reminded why.

For when you ask, "Why?",
With kisses,
And I have,
A never-ending list,
I'm reminded why.

Name: Trisha Vallamkonda Prathap
Title: His Love Story
Content:
He was taught not to feel,
So he turned his heart into steel.
He thought life was just cruel to anneal,
And all his scars he should conceal.

For him nothing was a big deal,
He didn't know how to appeal.
Why do you need to feel?
He believed all you need is zeal.

But one day he saw a girl in teal,
Just a cute kitten had made her squeal.
She instantly made his mind reel;
He knew she'll be his keel.

Even removing an orange peel
Or sharing a simple meal
Caused his broken parts to heal;
She was the engine, he the wheel.

With feelings he couldn't conceal
And a ring he was scared to reveal,
He finally bent down to kneel
And wrapped his future in an unbreakable seal.

Name: Kiran Dhaware
Title: Helping hand are better than praying lips
Content:
It was a busy day in a bustling suburb, and I was waiting for my bus to Worli. As soon as it arrived, the crowd surged forward, pushing and scrambling to get in. Amid the rush, I reached for my purse to buy a ticket, only to realize it was gone. Stolen. Panic set in. I had no money, and tears began to roll down my cheeks.

Just then, a kind man walked up to me and gently offered me a handful of change. I hesitated, trying to refuse. But he smiled warmly and said, “Take it, my child. You remind me of my daughter, you’ll need this more than I do right now.”

When I asked how I could ever repay his kindness, he simply replied, “Help someone else in need, just like I did... Because helping hands are better than praying lips!

When I found myself in the above situation, what stood out to me most was the person who offered a helping hand. There were plenty of people around, yet only one chose to step forward. He helped me without knowing who I was, where I came from, or whether I’d ever be able to return the favor. 
We all live fast-paced lives, constantly navigating different phases: growth, setbacks, milestones. Highs and lows are part of our human experience. But do we ever stop to think about how we bounce back? What helps us push through tough times? What gives us the strength to carry on? 

Often, it’s the helping hands we encounter along the way that lift us up. We’re surrounded by support, even when we don’t always see it. And sometimes, the people who go beyond offering thoughts and prayers, those who take real action are the ones who truly make a difference. From childhood to adulthood, our parents provide for both our emotional and physical needs. Teachers pass on wisdom. Siblings encourage us to explore new paths. Naturally, we wish to give back in return. But the truth is, genuine help can't really be repaid not just because of the act itself, but because of its timing. Time, once given, can never be returned and sometimes, it arrives at exactly the moment we need it most.

Only loved ones care??
Well, not always.
Alongside the care we receive from our loved ones, there are times when strangers step in to help us too. Life brings us in contact with all kinds of people, each with their own motives and paths. Among them, there are those who offer help simply because they care driven by genuine kindness and empathy. Without these helping hands, it’s hard to imagine how we’d make it through some of life’s toughest moments.

Think about it struggles like running low on money, losing a job, failing an important exam, or facing health challenges. These situations can shake us emotionally and mentally. During such times, seeking support isn’t just okay it’s necessary. But it’s also important to reach out to the right person, someone who truly understands and is willing to help.

"Hands that give, help us live"

Have you ever felt something like this?
I’ve lived through many situations where the kindness of helping hands got me through some of the darkest times. Whether it was parents, teachers, mentors, students, friends, or even strangers each played a role. I’m deeply grateful for all of them. In those moments when I felt stuck and helpless, their support gave me the strength to see things in a new, more hopeful light. Truly, helping hands speak louder than praying lips, they offer real hope when everything feels uncertain. After all, nothing is permanent. We overcome life’s hardest moments with the quiet support of those I call angel investors. It reminds us that helping and uplifting others should be one of our life’s goals.

Don’t expect anything in return
Helping others without expecting anything back says everything about who we are. In today’s world, it’s often easier to find surface beauty than it is to find a genuinely good character. But that kind of character - pure, selfless- can be taught and passed down. We must teach the next generation that true help means giving without conditions. When we help others, we shape ourselves into better human beings. And what do we get in return? Not money, not favors just blessings. And those blessings are powerful enough to keep the cycle of goodness going.

Mother Teresa’s words ring true: “Helping hands are better than praying lips.” True compassion isn’t always easy. But kindness has a way of circling back. Karma is real. So whenever you can, lend a hand because what goes around comes around 💞💞💞💞

Name: Amit Mohan
Title: Fragrance of Your Absence
Content:
Sometimes the air turns tender-
as if your footsteps are near,
and even the wind pauses,
unsure whether to whisper or to weep.

I tell myself I’ve learned
to live without you,
yet my heart still rehearses
the sound of your name in silence,
the way light bends when it finds your face.

The noise of the world-
its endless errands,
its proud and pointless arguments-
all fades into a hum
when I imagine you
standing by the door, smiling,
as if no time has passed.

People speak kindly now,
they call me strong,
but kindness is a thin cover
for the emptiness that hums beneath.

And still...
on quiet nights,
a fragrance moves across the room,
the air trembles as if touched by wings.
I know it’s you,
not gone,
only changed.
You live between my breaths,
in the hush that follows prayer,
in every dawn
that feels like forgiveness.

I know you’d come again-
not to stay, but to remind me
that nothing truly leaves
what it has once deeply touched.

Name: Shuchi Patra
Title: My Lady of the Dreamy Nights!
Content:
The very substance of the ambitious is merely the shadow of a dream.” —William Shakespeare 

Inspired by this quote - 

(Sonnet of 14 lines verse with the rhyme pattern abab cdcd efef gg )

My Lady of the Dreamy Nights!

Thou art, oh, so beautiful, my lady, like the mesmerizing, wondrous twinkling star
My lady doth enchant, captivate, and put me into a trance
I stretch my hands towards thee, yet seem so far!
I know thou canst only be my dream, for just a glance

Thou canst never be mine, but even in my dreams thou floatest away, out of my reach?
I bathe in thy heavenly luminance afar and to thee offer my worship now,
My ravishing lady of the sparkling, dreamy nights, thy elegance, thy charm, thy pristine celestial splendor doth bewitch
Oh, my ethereal, angelic damsel, thou hast stolen my heart, never to return; take my bow!

Thy sublime loving caress draws me nearer
With thee residing in my heart, I am so blessed
Oh, my lady, as thy spell turns deeper and dearer
Banishing any gloom, in life's every trough, every crest

The very substance of the ambitious is merely the shadow of a dream
My ambition lies in the mere desire even to touch thy soul or its shadow, setting my life agleam!
© Shuchi Patra

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Avoidance, avoiding emotions, pain, trauma, dissociation
Title: Avoidant (if I pretend I'm okay, then, I'm okay)
Content:
A landscape full of catastrophic, utter destruction.
Buildings are burning down, crashing down, going up in flames.
But only if I look at it. I'll just run away from here, I don't want to think
I'll shut my eyes and soothe myself to sleep, a gentle rocking in the midst of storm
Nothing's okay, darling, but just sleep tight, won't you? It's all okay.

Let's pretend our wounds don't exist, and let's not tend to them at all
I'm going to bury myself into a screen and eternally numb my thinking so I don't even have to think
My fingers mechanically scroll, as new content appears, and I absorb nothing
I know in the depth of my consciousness, I'm not okay, but I don't want to write about it, I can't describe it
Let's just not talk about it, everything's fine, I'm saying its fine

Can you stop for a second, and stop running from everything?
Your heart is full of despair, waiting to be acknowledged. But you just play another game, another reel, another text pretending you're normal.
Look at you comforting other people when you yourself are breaking down.
Can you stop for a second and look at the devastation inside your own heart?
Can you stop telling people they should live while you feel that you yourself should not?
You're rapidly running on the treadmill thinking if you run hard enough, you can get away forever.

Maybe the storm outside is just too loud. Although only and only if you face it
You will know yourself, you will figure it out, and you're going to be better.
You'll feel better only if you walk out in the storm, and pull a shelter on the roof, and cover your drowning garden outside your house.
But no, its too loud! There's thunder, and lightning; maybe it might be better if I go take care of my garden, or else my roof, but
I don't want to go out there at all. Let's pull the blinds, play some music, and pretend there's no storm, and if I set my headphones high enough, I'll drown everything out.
If you shout at me, I just want to walk out of the room. If you talk to me, I just want to drown you out with my headphones. Let's pull the blinds and sleep tight tonight
I can't hear it, and therefore nothing's happen, although I should probably acknowledge it
Not dealing with the rain will hurt later, I know.
But for now, I just want to pull the blinds and sleep peacefully, there's nothing outside, everything's fine.

A perfect storm of feelings and experiences swim around in my mind.
My mother crying. My dad shouting at me. The lack of a decision. The things my friends said to me. The fights at home. The expectations of other people.
They're all there, somewhere... somewhere outside the house, hammering away against the walls, probably ruining my garden and causing havoc I'll regret.
The longer I wait, the uglier forms they take, the morph themselves into ghastly creatures, and will tear apart my roof
But for now, nothing exists! I'm going to pull the blinds on them. One more reel, one more game, one more text, one more comforting someone, one more skincare routine. I'm perfectly okay.

I'm perfectly okay.

Name: Sakshi Singh
Title: The biggest lie I ever told
Content:
The biggest lie I ever told was that I wasn’t waiting for you.
Because the truth is… I still stop for a second whenever someone looks like you.
You left long ago,
but my heart never received the goodbye.
I learned to smile in front of everyone,
yet every night I silently grieve the life
we were supposed to have.
The cruelest part isn’t that you chose to leave
it’s that you left me with memories
that refuse to.
So yes…
The lie is that I don’t wait for you anymore.
The truth is,
I’ve only accepted that you’ll never come back,
not that I’ve stopped hoping.
It’s the one that survives,
even after the person is gone.

Name: Shreyasee das
Theme: Somewhere between love and goodbye the feeling of God in between these
Title: BRONTIDE
Content:
BRONTIDE

Somewhere betwixt love and valediction, they stood — not broken, but liminal, bathed in limpid effulgence.

He was Nebulon — once nebulous, once sere, carrying unspoken verities like cumulonimbus in his chest. Yet within him slept a palimpsest of light, waiting to alchemize silence into orison.

She was Nyra — Vidushi, lucid, lambent, diaphanous as monsoon dawn. Her Anahata was mellifluous, roseate, halcyon — an emporium of agape that did not censure his thunder, but enshrined it.

They met upon this auric earth — golden, peregrinating through caliginosity, yet still susurrous with hope. An earth weary of rapacity, of evanescent love, of forests made sere. They chose otherwise — sempiternal tenderness over transient haste, reverent slowness over frenetic forgetting.

For a season they were pluvial benediction — petrichor after aridity, psithurism of leaves, iridescent, ineffable, concinnate. A syzygy — two souls in euphonious consonance.

Then came sacred abscission — not cataclysm, not lachrymal ruin, but autumnal apotheosis. For trees know: caducity is palingenesis. To abscise is to burgeon. To shed is to effloresce.

And in that shedding —

BRONTIDE.

A fulgurant, numinous thunder within antahkarana. A sonorous anamnesis, beatific, beneficent.

His Vishuddha effloresced, unfettered, finding euphonic voice at 741 Hz — veridical, luminous.

Her Anahata effulged, incandescent, felicitous, seraphic at 639 Hz — transmuting old vellichor into jubilant becoming.

He walked forth — hierophant for golden earth, altruistic. She remained — autumnal regina, eyes holding cerulean thunder, silence now mantra.

Betwixt rainy ethereal sky and gilded falling petal, love did not wane.

It sublimated — lambent, resplendent, ever ascending.

Name: Aruna Chaturvedi
Title: मेरी माँ की साड़ी
Content:
माँ कुछ रिश्, की साड़ी केवल वस्त्र नहीं होती, वह बेटी के बचपन, संस्कार और अनंत प्रेम की सबसे सुंदर धरोहर होती है।"
माँ को इस दुनिया से गए पूरे आठ वर्ष हो चुके है, लेकिन
ते समय के साथ समाप्त नहीं होते, वे स्मृतियों में और गहरे उतर जाते हैं। आज सुबह से ही  मन बहुत व्याकुल था। आज मेरी बेटी की सगाई थी। घर में चारों ओर खुशियों का वातावरण था, पर मेरे भीतर एक अजीब-सी कसक उठ रही थी। आज यदि माँ होतीं तो सबसे अधिक प्रसन्न वही होतीं। माँ, मेरी बेटी को दुलारतीं, उसकी नजर उतारतीं, और अपनी साड़ी के पल्लू से उसका माथा सहलाकर आशीर्वाद देतीं।हर तैयारी में उनकी सलाह होती, हर रस्म में उनका स्नेह और हर मुस्कान में उनका आशीर्वाद।शायद इसी कारण सुबह से मन बहुत भारी था और माँ की याद बार-बार आँसू बनकर आँखों में उतर रही थी।
इन्हीं विचारों में डूबी मैं अलमारी तक पहुँची। धीरे से सूटकेस खोला। सबसे नीचे सहेजकर रखी माँ की प्रिय साड़ी निकाली। वर्षों बाद जब उस साड़ी पर हाथ फेरा, तो लगा जैसे कपड़े को नहीं, माँ के स्नेहिल स्पर्श को छू रही हूँ। पलभर में स्मृतियों के बंद दरवाज़े खुल गए और आँखों से आँसू बह निकले।
याद आया... बचपन में जब रात को नींद नहीं आती थी, माँ अपनी साड़ी का पल्लू मेरे हाथ में थमा देती थीं। पता ही नहीं चलता था कि कब उसी पल्लू को थामे-थामे गहरी नींद में सो जाती। जैसे उस आँचल में दुनिया भर की शांति समाई हो।
थोड़ी बड़ी हुई तो माँ जहाँ-जहाँ जातीं, मैं उनकी साड़ी का पल्लू पकड़े पीछे-पीछे चल देती। वह पल्लू मेरे लिए किसी डोर से कम नहीं था। विश्वास था कि जब तक यह हाथ में है, दुनिया की कोई भी कठिनाई कोई मुसीबत  मेरा कुछ नहीं बिगाड़ सकती।
पिताजी कभी डाँटते तो मैं भागकर माँ की साड़ी के पीछे छिप जाती। सच ही तो है, बच्चे के लिए सबसे सुरक्षित स्थान माँ का आँचल ही होता है। माँ यदि पड़ोस तक भी चली जातीं, तो मैं दौड़ती हुई उनके पीछे पहुँच जाती। लोग हँसते हुए कहते, "देखो,बछिया आ गई।" माँ को उनका मजाक चुभता और  वो मुझे समझती "बेटा, थोड़ा अकेले रहना भी सीखो।" लेकिन मेरी दुनिया तो बस माँ थीं।
आज वही सारी यादें चलचित्र की तरह आँखों के सामने घूम रही थीं। फर्क बस इतना था कि आज माँ का पल्लू था, पर माँ नहीं थीं।

"माँ..." बेटी की आवाज़ ने मेरी तंद्रा तोड़ी।
वह मेरे पास आई। मेरी नम आँखें देखकर बोली, "क्या हुआ माँ? आज तो खुश होने का दिन है।"
मैं चुप रही। तभी उसकी नज़र माँ की साड़ी पर पड़ी। उसने साड़ी उठाई और मुस्कुराकर बोली, "माँ, क्या आज मैं नानी की यही साड़ी पहन लूँ? मेरी सगाई है... नानी का आशीर्वाद भी तो मेरे साथ रहेगा।"
उसकी बात सुनकर मेरी आँखें भर आईं। मैंने प्यार से कहा, "बेटा, यह सिर्फ साड़ी नहीं है, तीन पीढ़ियों का प्यार है और साड़ी उसकी ओर बढ़ा दी।
कुछ देर बाद जब वह साड़ी पहनकर मेरे सामने आई, तो लगा जैसे समय आठ वर्ष पीछे लौट आया हो। वही सहज मुस्कान, वही सादगी, वही ममता... एक पल को लगा, माँ स्वयं मेरे सामने खड़ी हैं।
मैंने बेटी को कसकर गले लगा लिया। तभी भीतर से एक आवाज़ आई—"तू माँ को कहाँ ढूँढ़ रही थी? वह कभी तुझसे दूर गई ही नहीं। वह तेरे संस्कारों में थी, तेरी स्मृतियों में थी और आज तेरी बेटी के रूप में फिर तेरे सामने खड़ी है।"
उस दिन समझ आया कि माँ की साड़ी कभी पुरानी नहीं होती। । वह पीढ़ियों को जोड़ने वाला वह धागा होती है, जिसमें त्याग, प्रेम, संघर्ष और अनगिनत आशीर्वाद बुने होते हैं।उसमें वर्षों बाद भी ममता की वही खुशबू बसती है। सच ही कहा गया है—माँ चली जाती है, पर उसकी साड़ी में लिपटा स्नेह कभी पुराना नहीं होता। हर बेटी के लिए माँ का आँचल ही उसका पहला घर, पहली पाठशाला और जीवन का सबसे सुरक्षित संसार होता है।"

अरुणा चतुर्वेदी

Name: rittik bora
Title: A Walk Towards Freedom
Content:
Beneath a lightless sky,
Where darkness had taken hold,

Faces turned into masks,
Where truth became bankrupt,
And lies bought every prize.

I locked myself behind closed doors,
Shivering in the cold,
Where breathing grew too heavy
To carry me forward,

And liberation
Became a mountain to climb.

Deep within the abyss,
I chose an unseen path,
A walk taken alone,
To find the child I had lost—
To smile again,
And dance
To the beating rhythm of being alive.

Still,
The shadow trails behind—
A reflection of what I refuse to become,
Toward the freedom I once buried

Name: Surabhi Rani
Title: एक दिन यूँ ही…
Content:
एक दिन यूँ ही…

माँ से मैंने पूछा ,
धीरे से…
“माँ…
तेरे सपनों में
कौन-कौन से रंग बसते हैं?”
माँ चौंकी।
हाथ का काम पल भर को ठहरा,
और होंठों पर हल्की हँसी उतर आई—
“अचानक यह सवाल क्यों?”
मैंने कहा—
“मैं तेरे लिए कुछ सपने बुनना चाहती हूँ,
बताओ न…
उनमें कौन-कौन से रंग भरूँ?”
माँ कुछ देर चुप रही,
जैसे स्मृतियों की अलमारी में
धीरे-धीरे कुछ खोज रही हो।
फिर बोली—
“भरना ही है तो
गाँव जाने वाली बस की गंध भर देना,
जो, मिलाती है मेरे बचपन की गलियों से
जहाँ नाम के आगे
जिम्मेदारियों का बोझ नहीं था।
उसमें एक ऐसी सुबह का रंग भी भरना
जिसमें आँख खुले
तो किसी काम की परछाईं
दरवाज़े पर खड़ी न मिले।
थोड़ा-सा सुकून भी भर देना,
जहाँ आवाज़ें हों
पर ताने न हों,
बातें हों
पर उनका कोई हिसाब न हो।
और एक छोटा-सा कोना भी रखना,
जहाँ मैं थोड़ी देर
सिर्फ अपने लिए बैठ सकूँ,
और अपने ही सपनों को
चुपचाप जी सकूँ…”
इतना कहकर माँ अचानक ठहर गई।
फिर धीमे से बोली—
“क्यों पूछती है यह सब?
तेरे पिता ने भी
कभी यूँ ही पूछा था…
आज तूने पूछा,
कल शायद कोई और पूछेगा।
पर इच्छाओं का यह कागज़
अक्सर यूँ ही
अलमारी में बेरंग पड़ा रह जाता है।
माँओं के सपने
न पूरी तरह टूटते हैं,
न ही पूरे होते हैं—

वे बस
अनगिनत जिम्मेदारियों के नीचे
धीरे-धीरे
दब जाते हैं।”
                     -सुरभि रानी

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Self love, learning to love yourself after hating yourself
Title: An awkward first date (Me and myself).
Content:
Silence stretches between both of us as we sit together for a coffee date.
This silence is really loud, and, my thoughts seem a lot louder, this just feels awkward
I can't really cherish the moment when its with you, it feels different, a little uneasy
I've hated you for so long, I've sometimes worked against you, I've hurt you
I've personally run a blade across your tender skin, I've despised you inside and out
I want you to be someone else, I want you to behave differently! I want someone strong, confident, muscular, productive. I want someone who can lift me easily.
I want someone who takes care of themselves every single day.
I want someone who is happy.
And you don't even brush your teeth daily, and you don't even shower.
You're like a stick and so incredibly skinny.
You shout at your parents and friends and you hurt them sometimes.
But here I am, and here you are, so I guess we're willing to try again?

This feels really awkward and uncomfortable.
"We're so far apart." You tell me. "We're literally miles away. How do we meet at the same page, ever?"
"It's okay." I tell you. "We'll just take one step forward every day, just forward instead of back, and one day, we'll meet on the same page."
I hope my sincerity shines through in my actions, even if this doesn't feel amazing to you at first. Maybe its uncomfortable.
But I prepared this coffee date table for you and chose the cloth of your favourite colour. Maybe your thoughts are racing and you're not fully in the moment.
But its okay, even if its not exactly how I hoped it'd be.

I really want to take care of you.
I really want to cherish you and love you the hardest during your worst moments
You told me you're afraid of pain, well, in pain I want to look after you really well
Maybe it might hurt less, eventually, I'll keep trying
The first date is really awkward, it feels uncomfortable, and what are we even doing?
I awkwardly take sips of my coffee just to break the ice, and you keep staring away.
But at least we both managed to sit down, and try together.
And if we try enough times, maybe it wouldn't be awkward at all.
We're meant to be together in this lifetime and we have our whole lives ahead of us.
One day at a time, and I hope that eventually when I try, try and try again
One day it'll hit you, and one day we might laugh together at a joke
And one day we might even meet at the same page, the version of each other we both wanted to see
We're just going to try, and eventually, I'm going to be comfortable with you.
I know you already, I just feel like I don't love you. But one day, eventually
We'll meet each other at the same page.
We'll not feel awkward anymore.
The silence will still exist between you and me, but, it won't hurt.
One day.
But for today, let's just take one step forward.

I wish you were someone else, but, while you become that person
I'm still going to love you just the same.

Name: Sky
Title: Search of light.
Content:
Dark skies. Stars drifted far away from me.

I rubbed my eyes and looked again. I found myself standing beneath them, so close to the heavens, as though only a flight of stairs separated me from the stars and the moon.

The moon was huge—as huge as the night. Its pale whiteness wandered across the heavens and spilled over the distant lands.

The distant lands, somewhere in those lands of others. I stood alone, alone in the green, green field.

Short, well-kept grass pressed beneath my naked feet.

Yet no light ever reached my soul.

Under that clear sky, my chest ached. My heart cried. There was no wound upon me, nothing that could explain the pain, yet it was unbearable.

Still, I stood.

Still.

And I let the cold wind carry my soul away.

Away,

Somewhere far from this world.

To a world filled with lights. With colors. With the things that could give meaning to my life.

In search of things. I had wandered through the world of others in search of things.

For any light.

For any color.

Anything at all.

But I failed. Failed to fill my soul.

The ache returned. It crawled back into my soul.

I stood in the field, field green field.

Nobody was there to hold my cold hands.

And share their warmth, some warmth with me.

Yet my search had never stopped.

My eyes, scrutinizing gaze of mine.

Moved through the field to find something.

Something that could take me away.

My eyes found nothing.

But my ears heard something.

A gentle lapping.

The whisper of a stream against the sleeping earth, singing a soft and distant song.

Like a call of a whale.

I turned toward it.

And I let the song carry my feet.

One step.

Then another.

Soon, my eyes found lights drifting upon the river.

Something within my soul loosened.

I ran toward them.

As I neared the river, I slowed.

The water lay before me like a mirror.

My eyes softly moved through the river.

There, they were.

The stars.

The stars I could never reach were resting within the river.

Everything I had searched for was there—

a canvas of the sky, painted in the darkest hours of moonlight.

I stepped closer.

My eyes lowered.

And then I found myself standing within the river, surrounded by stars.

All those lights.

All those colors.

Everything I had ever longed for.

The water trembled.

My reflection broke into a thousand pieces and merged with the lights I had spent so long searching for.

I stepped back.

My heart rose within my chest.

Even beneath the coldness of the night, sweat gathered upon my skin.

Everything I needed was there.

Within the river.

I gathered myself.

Every fragment of strength that remained, I collected.

Every last piece of courage, I gathered into my crying heart.

The gentle wind brushed against me.

For a moment, it felt as though it whispered that everything I had ever wanted would soon be mine.

I stepped toward the river.

My legs resisted.

You know that resistance.

The kind that comes when some part of you knows that everything is about to end—and believes that perhaps it will end for the better.

The tears of the last cry.

The sorrow of the last smile.

The coldness that will vanish for something better.

Yet, you know that resistance to losing the ache,

'Cause it feels so familiar.

Yet I made the choice.

The last visit to a life that had grown too cold.

And every bit of the past asked me for a—

A warm heart.

A smiling face.

Someone to make you feel alive again.

Someone with whom you could share your laughter.

Your joy.

Every part of my soul, my blood, my skin—

Everything within me wanted only one thing.

To live.

To live a life that meant something.

Something good.

But somewhere along the way, I had lost something precious within myself.

The ability to feel.

The joy.

The wonder.

The dreams that once belonged to me.

They had all vanished, slowly, quietly, until I became nothing more than a body carrying the remains of a life I no longer recognized.

Everything I had ever counted on had become a disappointment.

I stepped into the river.

Because I had nowhere to go.

The ground disappeared beneath my feet.

And I fell.

The water rushed around me, took me within its shoulders.

It hugged me with a coldness that almost felt warm.

Its touch was strangely gentle.

Almost heavenly.

My legs had nothing to stand upon, yet I felt as though something carried me toward the sky.

My hands had nothing to hold, yet I felt suspended in the air.

My body sank into the depths.

I opened my eyes.

The lights were gone.

No stars.

No moonlight.

Nothing remained of the beautiful world I had seen above.

Everything I had found within the river—

vanished.

Faded.

Dissolved.

Broken.

Darkness.

Perhaps this was the truth.

Whatever I touched, I took its light away.

Water rushed into my nose.

Into my mouth.

My body fought for a breath.

My hands moved on their own.

My legs thrashed like a frightened creature searching for land.

Even though I had wanted an end—

something within me refused it.

My soul screamed for life.

I moved my hands.

Back and forth.

Again.

Again.

But the shore was too far.

I sank deeper into the river's arms.

My final breaths escaped like bubbles, drifting upward without me.

Like the stars.

Like everything else I had ever lost.

I sank into the abyss.

I was like a bird without wings, falling through a world where nothing could carry me.

My eyes slowly closed.

Only if my life had not been meaningless.

Only if there had been something more to hold on to.

Perhaps I gave up too easily.

Maybe I should have moved my hands harder.

Maybe I should have screamed for help.

Maybe—

Maybe I should have tried my best.

But it was too late for regrets.

Wasn't it?

I was falling into darkness.

I was fading into darkness.

Everything stopped.

I was no longer falling.

I was floating.

Somewhere.

Somewhere beyond the darkness.

My eyes opened.

I was deep beneath the river, far from the shore, far from the world I had belonged to.

Yet I was surrounded by light.

Stars twinkled around me.

Everywhere.

Colors moved through the darkness like living things.

Warmth surrounded me.

It was as though the sky itself had fallen beneath the river, and I had awakened among the stars.

I reached out.

My fingers brushed against one.

It twinkled and drifted away, shy as a girl turning from a stranger.

I swam after them.

Not to hold them.

Not to possess them.

Only to admire their beauty.

They moved around me, close enough to touch.

Yet something inside me remained empty.

The ache in my chest had disappeared.

But the emptiness remained.

A hollow place had been carved into my soul.

So, I swam onward.

I was no longer searching for the stars.

I was searching for something that could feel mine.

Then I heard it.

A gentle wave.

The whisper of a spirit in the depth, singing a soft and distant song.

Like a call of a whale.

A brightness far greater than the faint blue radiance surrounding me.

Somewhere in the distant depths.

I turned toward it.

And there, within the blue darkness, I saw a whale.

It moved through the water like a creature born from the heavens.

Blue light surrounded its enormous body.

Tiny sparks shimmered along its skin.

I froze.

I could only stare.

I could only hear.

Its calls, that made my heart beat again.

The whale’s eyes were toward mine.

And it was swimming toward me.

There was no fear in its eyes.

No anger.

No sorrow.

Only gentleness.

Only love.

I remained still and let its light reach mine.

Let its beauty find mine.

Let its soul find mine.

It came closer than anything ever had.

The whale moved its fins.

Soft waves traveled through the water around its enormous body.

Then it stopped beside me.

Its light spread across my body.

Across my face.

Into my soul.

And something within me warmed.

A warmth I had forgotten for long.

Slowly, I raised my hand.

The whale's eye was enormous, shining like a pearl on the ocean.

It moved its tail gently, closing the distance between us.

I reached toward it.

To feel.

Not to possess its beauty.

To feel it.

For the first time in a long while, I found something.

Something that wasn’t mine, didn’t belong to me, yet I found peace in it as it was.

The whale lowered itself.

Its head drifted away from me.

For a moment, I thought it was leaving.

Then its back rose beneath my legs.

It carried me.

Its body became my ground.

Gave me the support of a father, to stand over it.

Gave me the warmth of a mother, when I clung to its back.

I clung to its back.

My eyes grew heavy.

The whale carried me upward.

Toward the surface.

Toward the shore.

The stars slowly disappeared behind us.

Yet I no longer needed them.

I had found something else to hold on to.

The divine whale carried me somewhere.

Somewhere, maybe somewhere we call the afterlife...

My eyes were closed.

Its gentle call echoed through the water like a song.

A song of gentleness.

A song of care.

The very things I had spent my life searching for in others.

Before I surrendered to sleep, I understood something.

I had found something I should have known earlier.

Somewhere within the depths of the river.

I had found something; it was too late...

It was time for me to sleep.

The body floated somewhere upon the surface of a river.

The body had traveled somewhere far, far from its world.

The river waves pushed it. From shore to shore, bank to bank. From one place to another, like a boat with no man, no soul.

The night was empty. No stars. No moon.

The whale was gone.

There was only the body.

It drifted onward until the river finally carried it toward its end.

Slowly, the waves pushed the body toward the edge.

Then, as though the river itself had decided where it belonged, it carried the body onto the land.

Nights passed. Days dissolved.

The mud dried.

Wild grass grew around the body.

I opened my eyes.

I opened my eyes and looked back at the river.

Under the moonlight, it was empty.

The miracle had vanished. Whether I had woken from a dream or from something else—I didn't know.

For a moment, I wondered if it had ever existed, and even I...

I stood.

Then I turned my back toward the river.

Toward the lights I had once believed were everything.

And I walked.

Into the grass.

The field was no longer the neat green meadow I had entered.

The grass had grown wild now, rising almost to my hips.

The path ahead was dark.

Uncertain.

I could not see where it ended.

But I kept walking.

Because I had learned something in the darkness.

A path did not have to be visible for me to take the next step.

I walked toward the middle of the field.

And there—

stood a home.

My home.

Its roof was dark beneath the moon.

Its walls were scarcely touched by the pallid light.

Beside it stood an old tree, its naked branches spread against the sky, each limb like the crooked hand of some forgotten watcher.

Everything was quiet.

Utterly quiet.

I walked toward the house.

Then I heard it.

Laughter.

Soft at first.

Then another voice.

Then another.

Warm sounds spilled through the walls, breaking the silence that had followed me for so long.

I stopped.

My eyes rested upon the house.

And for the first time, I smiled.

I had spent so long wandering through the world of others, searching for light.

I had searched the heavens.

I had searched the river.

I had searched the stars.

But somewhere in the depths of that memory, when I had been on the back of the whale—the divine whale—I understood something.

Perhaps the light I had been seeking was never meant to be found in the world of others.

Perhaps I had carried a little of it all along.

Fireflies emerged from the wild grass.

One.

Then another.

Then dozens.

Tiny lights flickered around me.

I walked through the grass, making my own path toward home.

The fireflies followed.

Or perhaps they only seemed to.

Either way, they lit the darkness before my feet.

And behind the walls of my home—

There was laughter.

There was warmth.

There was life.

And for the first time in a long while,

I walked toward it.

And nothing was disappearing.

Title: Emancipation of Heart Feelings
Content:

Name: abhaya nakade
Title: कसे सांगू?
Content:
कसे सांगू?
कसे सांगू ते भाव मनी काय,
ना ते कळे कोणाला.
नाते हे जगावेगळे आपुले,
कसे सांगू कोणाला.
बोलनी खूप, बोलनही,
न बोललेले जाणे माझा कान्हा.
मनी उमलती सख्याचे भाव,
असा तो माझा पाठीीराखा.
कसे सांगू माझे भाव कोणाला?
ना कळे हे नाते.
जरी नसे तू जवळी माझ्या,
तरी वसे अंतरी माझ्या.
कशी सांगू तुझी ओढ मनी लागे,
जशी विठ्ठला लागे ओढ
आपुल्या लेकरांची.
तशी मला लागे ओढ
तुझ्या सख्यप्रितीची.
क्षणाक्षणाला वाढत जाई,
आस तुझ्या सहवासाची.
मनी अनंत भाव त्याचे,
मुखी मात्र हास्य सदा.
अंतरी भावनांचा अथांग सागर,
कसे सांगू कोणाला?
कधी सखा, कधी बंधू,
कधी पुत्र, कधी मायबाप.
असे हे जगावेगळे,
आपुले अनोखे नाते.
कसे सांगू हे भावनांचे नाते
आपल्या लोकांना?
ज्यांनी उमजला नाही कृष्ण,
ते काय जाणती या प्रेमाला?
कसे सांगू कोणाला,
हे आपुले अजब नाते.
शब्द हरवती वाटेवर,
प्रेमाची नाळ अंतरी अखंड नांदे.
— लेखिका : अभया नकाडे ❤️

Name: Nithya S
Title: In the Company of Silence
Content:
Sometimes
what the soul asks for
is not noise,
not movement,
not answers 
only quiet.

A moment to turn inward,
to sit beside yourself
like an old friend,
without hurry,
without expectation.

It is alright
to do nothing at all.
The heart too
needs stillness
to hear its own voice.

And in that silence,
life begins to reveal
its small forgotten joys 

sunlight resting on the floor,
rain whispering at the window,
a cup of tea gone warm in your hands,
the comfort of your own breath.

So take time
to be with yourself.
For often,
the gentlest moments
are the ones
we were too busy to notice.

Name: Surya Teja Gorli
Title: తనకి తెలియని నా ప్రపంచం
Content:
శీర్షిక: తనకి తెలియని నా ప్రపంచం

ఈరోజు ఏమైందో నాకు అసలు అర్థం కావడం లేదు…

ఎప్పటిలాగే తనని చూశాను.
ఎప్పటిలాగే తనతో మాట్లాడాను.

కానీ తనని చూస్తుండగానే…
ఒక్కసారిగా ఏదో కొత్తగా అనిపించింది.

ఎప్పుడూ లేని ఆనందం,
ఎందుకో తెలియని ప్రశాంతత.
మనసంతా ఏదో కొత్త అనుభూతితో నిండిపోయింది.

అప్పటి నుంచి ఎందుకో
నా మనసు నా మాట వినడం లేదు.

ఏం చేస్తున్నా,
ఏం ఆలోచిస్తున్నా…
మళ్లీ తనే గుర్తొస్తోంది.

తనని చూస్తుండగానే
ఎందుకో నా చూపు అక్కడే ఆగిపోయింది.

ఏం జరిగిందో తెలియదు…

ఆ క్షణం అయిపోయినా,
నా మనసు మాత్రం ఇంకా అక్కడే ఉన్నట్టనిపించింది.
ఏంటి ఇది?
నాకు తెలియకుండానే నేను తనని ఇష్టపడుతున్నానా?

ఎవరికి చెప్పుకుందాం?

పక్కన ఎవరూ లేరు…
చుట్టూ చూస్తే ఈ పుస్తకాలు, పాత కుర్చీలు తప్ప.

సరే…

ఈరోజు నా మనసులో ఉన్నదంతా
ఈ పుస్తకాలకే చెప్పుకుందాం.

[పుస్తకంలో రాయడం మొదలుపెట్టాను]

30/09/2026
బుధవారం

నా ప్రియమైన డైరీ,

ఈరోజు జరిగిన విషయం నీతో చెప్పకుండా నిద్రపోలేననిపిస్తోంది.
అసలు ఎక్కడి నుంచి మొదలుపెట్టాలో కూడా తెలియడం లేదు…

తనని మొదటి సారి చూసినప్పుడు…
ఏదో సినిమాలో చూపించినట్టుగా ప్రపంచం ఒక్కసారిగా ఆగిపోలేదు.
చుట్టూ ఉన్నదంతా మామూలుగానే ఉంది.
నా గుండె కూడా అలాగే కొట్టుకుంటూనే ఉంది.

కానీ…

ఏదో జరిగింది.

ప్రపంచం ఆగిపోలేదు…
కానీ నేను ఆగిపోయాను.
నిన్ను చూస్తూ…

నా కళ్ల ముందు ఎంతమంది ఉన్నా,
తన తప్ప ఇంకెవరూ కనిపించనంతగా ఆగిపోయాను.

అది ఎందుకో నాకు అర్థం కాలేదు.
నువ్వెవరో కూడా నాకు తెలియదు.
నీ పేరు కూడా తెలియదు.

అయినా ఆ క్షణంలో,
తను మాత్రం నాకు ఏదో తెలిసిన వ్యక్తిలా అనిపించావు.

తనని చూస్తుంటే,
ఎప్పటినుంచో పరిచయం ఉన్నట్టుగా అనిపించింది.

ఏమో… అందుకేనేమో…
తను అక్కడి నుంచి వెళ్లిపోయినా,
నా కళ్ల ముందే ఉన్నట్టుగా అనిపించింది.

నాకు తెలిసి,
నేను తనని మొదటిసారి చూడలేదు.

బహుశా…
ఈ పరిచయం నాకు కొత్తది కాదేమో.

లేదంటే,
మొదటి సారి చూసిన తను
ఇంత పరిచయంగా ఎలా అనిపించింది?

ఇంకా మాట్లాడితే,
నాకు తనలో నచ్చిన మొదటి విషయం తన కళ్లే.

చిన్ని చిన్ని కళ్ళు…
నువ్వు నవ్వినప్పుడు ఇంకాస్త చిన్ని అయిపోయేవి.

నిజం చెప్పనా?

తను నవ్వినప్పుడు,
నా చూపు ముందుగా వెళ్లేది తన కళ్ల దగ్గరకే.

తన నవ్వు తన పెదవుల దగ్గర ఆగిపోదు…
తన కళ్లలో కూడా కనిపిస్తుంది.

తన అందమైన కళ్లను
తన కళ్లద్దాల వెనక దాచేస్తుంది.

కానీ తనకు తెలియని విషయం ఏంటంటే…
తను తన కళ్లను దాచుకున్న ప్రతిసారీ,
నేను మాత్రం వాటిని ఇంకాస్త ఎక్కువగా గుర్తుపెట్టుకున్నాను.

తన నవ్వు గురించి ఏం చెప్పాలి అనుకున్నా,
మళ్లీ నా చూపు తన కళ్ల దగ్గరకే వెళ్లిపోతుంది.

తను ఎప్పుడు చూసినా,
ఆ చిరునవ్వు తన పెదవులపై కనిపిస్తూనే ఉంటుంది.

తన మాటల్లో కూడా తన నవ్వే కనిపిస్తుంది.
తను ఏదైనా చెబుతుంటే,
మధ్యలో వచ్చే ఆ చిన్న నవ్వు
తన మాటలకే ఇంకో అందాన్ని తీసుకొస్తుంది.

తను ఏం చెబుతుందో వింటూ ఉండటం ఒకటైతే,
తను చెబుతూనే నవ్వుతుంటే చూస్తూ ఉండటం ఇంకోటి.

కొన్నిసార్లు,
తను చెప్పే మాటలకంటే
ఆ మాటల మధ్యలో తను నవ్విన క్షణమే ఎక్కువగా గుర్తుండిపోతుంది.

అందుకేనేమో…
తన మాటలు వింటూ ఉండాలనిపించేది.

నిజం చెప్పాలంటే,
నాకు తనలో నచ్చింది తన అందం మాత్రమే కాదు.

ఇంకో విషయం కూడా ఉంది.

తను అందరిలా ఉండదు.
తనకి నచ్చినట్టే ఉంటుంది.

తను వేసుకునే డ్రెస్‌ నుంచి,
తను మాట్లాడే మాటల వరకు…
అన్నింటిలోనూ తనని ప్రత్యేకంగా చూపించే ఏదో ఒకటి ఉంటుంది.

మన తెలుగు సంప్రదాయాల్ని
తనకి నచ్చినట్టుగా, చాలా సహజంగా పాటిస్తుంది.

అందుకే ఏమో…
ఇంతమంది మధ్యలో
తను మాత్రం నాకు ఇంకాస్త ఎక్కువగా కనిపించింది.

తనలో నాకు నచ్చింది
ఒక్క విషయం కాదు.

తనని తను మార్చుకోకుండా
తనలాగే ఉండే ఆ తీరు.

నిజం చెప్పాలంటే…
తను నా జీవితంలోకి వస్తే ఎలా ఉంటుందో
నేను ఊహించుకున్న ఒక క్షణం ఉంది.

తను నా వైపు నడుచుకుంటూ వస్తుంటే,
తనని చూడకముందే
తన పట్టీల శబ్దంతోనే
తను వస్తుందని గుర్తుపట్టగలనేమో.

తను చేతులు కదిపినప్పుడల్లా
గాజులు చేసే ఆ చిన్న శబ్దం
ఎందుకో నాకు చాలా దగ్గరగా అనిపిస్తుందేమో.

నుదుటిన పెట్టుకున్న చిన్న బొట్టు,
తన ముఖానికి ఇంకాస్త అందాన్ని అద్దినట్టుగా
చూస్తూ ఉండిపోతానేమో.

అలా ఒక్కో అడుగు వేస్తూ
తను నా దగ్గరికి వచ్చి…

పెళ్లి చీరలో
నా పక్కన కూర్చుంటే…

ఇన్నాళ్లూ నేను ఊహించుకున్న తను
ఆ రోజు నిజంగా నా పక్కన ఉంటే…

ఆ క్షణంలో ఇంకేం కావాలో కూడా
నాకు అర్థం కాకపోవచ్చు.

కానీ…

అది కేవలం నా ఊహ మాత్రమే.

తను నా గురించి ఏం అనుకుంటుందో నాకు తెలియదు.

తను నన్ను ఇష్టపడుతుందో లేదో కూడా నాకు తెలియదు.

ఇన్ని రోజులు తనతో గడిపిన
ఆ చిన్న చిన్న క్షణాలన్నీ
ఇప్పుడు నా జ్ఞాపకాలుగా మిగిలిపోయాయి.

ఒకవేళ తన మనసులో నేను లేకపోయినా…
తనని ఇష్టపడిన ఈ మనసుని
నేను మాత్రం తప్పు పట్టలేను.

ఎందుకంటే…

తనని ప్రేమించాలనుకుని నేను ప్రేమించలేదు.
తనని చూస్తూ చూస్తూ… తెలియకుండానే ప్రేమలో పడిపోయాను.

ఇంతే…

ఈరోజు నా మనసులో దాచుకున్నదంతా
ఈ పుస్తకానికి చెప్పేశాను.

తనకి ఇవన్నీ ఎప్పుడైనా తెలుస్తాయో లేదో నాకు తెలియదు.
కానీ ఈరోజు మాత్రం
నా మనసులో ఏం జరుగుతుందో నాకు అర్థమైంది.

ఇక నిద్రపోవాలి…

రేపు తనని మళ్లీ చూసినప్పుడు
ఈరోజు రాసిందంతా గుర్తొచ్చినా,
ఏమీ జరగనట్టే ఉండాలి.

శుభరాత్రి,
నా ప్రియమైన డైరీ.

Name: Aruna Chaturvedi
Title: मां, तुम्हारी बहुत याद आती है
Content:
मंच पर जब सम्मान मिला,
तालियों का शोर उठा,
मन बेचैन, चुपचाप
तुम्हें ही खोजने लगा।
किसी ने पूछा मुझसे,
"सब तो है पास तुम्हारे,
फिर इन आँखों में क्यों नमी है?"
कैसे मैं बताऊँ—
माँ, तुम जो नहीं हो,
इसी बात की कमी है।
काश! तुम आज साथ होतीं,
तो कुछ और बात होती।
उपलब्धियों पर मेरी
तुम पीठ थपथपातीं।
घर आने की खबर पाकर
पलकों के पाँवड़े बिछातीं।
स्वागत में मेरी मैया
मंगल-गीत गुनगुनातीं।
"लाडो..." कहकर मुझको
अपने गले लगातीं।
यही बात याद करके
आँखें मेरी भर आती हैं।
माँ, तुम्हारी बहुत याद आती है।
जब मन बहुत घबराया,
तेरा चेहरा याद आया।
"मैं हूँ न..." कहकर तुमने
मेरा हौसला बढ़ाया।
जीवन की बस एक तमन्ना है—
जब भी मैं जन्म पाऊँ,
माँ के रूप में सदा ही
हर बार तुम्हें ही पाऊँ।
यही विनती बार-बार
साँसें मेरी दोहराती हैं।
मेरी हर धड़कन, हर प्रार्थना में
माँ, तुम्हारी बहुत याद आती है...
माँ, तुम्हारी बहुत याद आती है।

Har gali aur har khet.

Jis noor se hua har insaan nek.

Name: Moumita Pal Das
Title: Aurora
Content:
You are my aurora
My beautiful northern light 
Your love paints my darkest skies
In shades of blue and green 
Turning my shades into light...

Rare for others to witness
But somehow i found you 
A miracle across the night sky
I shine with the light for you....

When the world falls dark 
I only have to look your way
For you are my northern light 
My reason to believe in another day..

You make my nights brighter 
Without ever asking the darkness to leave 
You simply stay holding me tightly 
Letting the sadness away..

And if someday 

All the lights in the universe fade
If the stars forget how to shine
The sky loses all its colour..
I would still find a way to you
 
Because you are my Aurora..
My rarest wonder 
My beautiful Northern light.

Name: Ruth Anthony
Title: Honey and Hurt
Content:
In the wilderness
of my wounded heart,
Pain and sorrow
played their part,
Which felt like
walking on thorns.

Those wounded scars
ran so deep within me,

That even
walking on thorns
felt like
numb legs
untouched by pain.

And is that
anything I gained?

Not to blame anyone,
Just a quiet truth.

Some people were
honey to me,
And hurt to my soul.

And then I found...
In the warmth of HIS embrace
lies abundant showers of joy and grace.

He is like
a spoonful of honey,
Who enriched
my life with
the sweetness of rain.

I got immersed in
the Honeyed Ocean
of HIS Love.
HIS Love comforted
my heart with
everlasting Peace.
Like a dove,
A Blessing from
Heaven above.

He is the hero
of my heart,
The Shepherd
of my soul,

Who makes
my life blossom
like a flower.

He is my CHRIST,
my Redeemer,
Who died for me
on the cross,
That I may flourish
in the garden of
HIS selfless LOVE.

And that is the journey of
Honey and Hurt.
Some spread
honey in your life,
And you taste
its sweetest side.

Some bring
hurt,
Leaving the heart
bruised and traumatized.

Yet there is a lesson in both,
Be your own honey in the sweetness,
And your own strength in the hurt.

And there you learn
to lean on God
Rather than this
fleeting world.

-Ruth Anthony

Name: Nisha RG
Theme: Husband and wife love and mutual understanding, building a life together from scratch
Title: RAMAN’S  SHANKARI
Content:
SHORT STORY -2
Raman’s Shankari
Raman was lying on the hospital bed with the life-saving ventilator and the bedside hospital cardiac monitor constantly making beeping sounds which felt demanding and never-ending. Shankari, with a blank face, caressed him. She looked at him again and again, She felt like he was smiling at her until the gentle pat on her shoulder by the duty nurse made her come around. She walked outside the ICU with a bleeding heart in an untaught state. While walking, she knew there was no hope of recovery for him. Her neighbour, an old friend of Shankari, Sharada, was waiting outside patiently with her breakfast. Sharada, seeing her crestfallen face, could not help but succumb to tears. She wiped her eyes and said, 
“Ayyo Shankari, you look all the more tired. Come and sit here. Please have something. 
Why didn't you drink the tea? “
Shankari remained silent. Her voice was dead with grief and fatigue. Sarada took a steel glass, poured some hot tea from a steel flask and gave it to her. Shankari took the steaming glass filled with tea and drank it. It wetted her already parched tongue and throat. She finished the tea, looked at Sarada and said, 
“ I don't think there is a comeback for him. 
I don’t know what to do or where to go. 
His younger brother, Divakar, took him to the hospital; he was the one covering his medical expenses. 
He went to the hospital canteen to have his breakfast. 
Sarada, I know I cannot ask for more from god. Death is the only respite for him.” 
She took a deep breath, leaned on the wall and closed her eyes. Sarada took the glass from the fragile hands of Shankari. She looked at her old friend and sighed deeply. She had known her since childhood. Sarada is well aware of her situation and how she feels right now. Sarada herself had lost her husband 10 years back. She lives with her youngest Son and family. But in Shankari’s case, she has no one to care for.
Sharada with the steel glass went towards the washbasin which is in the right-hand corner of the floor to wash it off.  After sitting idle for some time, she got up and walked towards the nursing station. There, she met the duty nurse and enquired about Raman’s condition. “Nurse, I want to know about Raman, who was admitted to the ICU. 
Is there any hope?” asked Sharada. 
“No, mother. This time, he is not going to survive. 
His internal organs are in such bad condition. Now he is on a ventilator. 
The doctor will talk to his relatives about removing the ventilator today “ 
said the duty nurse without a tinge of concern. Sharadha walked back with a downward spiral of emotions. Now, what will happen to Shankari? Who will take care of her? 
Even her condition at her Son’s house is appalling. Her daughter-in-law supports her staying because she goes for the 100-day guaranteed work scheme of the government. She sells milk, eggs and receives a meagre widow's pension. 
               Shankari and Raman are childless and homeless. They have been staying in a one-bedroom house for rent for many years now. They had to sell their properties and house for the treatment of Divakar’s daughter, who had cancer 10 years ago. But post-treatment, Divakar’s wife and daughter were against their staying in their house. Divakar remained silent when his wife and daughter mistreated them. Raman never complained. Instead, they tolerated their injustice and dismal surroundings. Later, when the taunting became unbearable, they decided to shift to a rental house. They both sold poori, curry, tea and coffee for a living in the evening. They were happy with whatever meagre amount they could save. But Raman developed an inclination towards alcohol, and soon he became a chronic alcoholic. After drinking, he lays bare his heart. All his suppressed emotions flow out. It was like wearing his emotions on his sleeve. He cried and said, 
“ I am a big failure. Jobless, propertyless and childless. 
Even my parents favoured my brothers and sisters over me”. 
Shankari remained silent. But once he slinks away to sleep, Shankari cries her heart out. However, in the morning, Raman feels sorry for it and asks for her forgiveness. 
Shankari very well knew that Raman loved her from the bottom of his heart. But the problem is that life was unfair to him. He was a man of dreams and ambitions. He loved to study philosophy and art. He painted and sculpted. But his father, Soman was against all this.  He wanted him to study law, practice law, and become a lawyer. His brothers  Chandran and Divakar, though they had ambitions like him, were afraid to go against the wishes of their arrogant, adamant father. The only person who supported him silently was his mother Janaaamma. But his mother could not go against the hard decisions of his father. She had to bear the wrath of her husband for supporting her son, including physical and verbal abuse. But she took it all. She fought for his claim silently with prayers and tears. Raman went to JNU with the support of her mother. His father was so angry that he did not talk to her for a week and slept outside the bedroom on a screwpine mat as though protesting. His mother had high hopes for him. She cried in the dark corridors of their kitchen. Found solace in prayers. Unfortunately, however, Raman found himself caught up in politics and party activities in college. During the initial months of college, he was a keen learner and observer of everything around him. But the temptation to know and try new things was enticing. He drank liquor, took the first puff of a cigarette, travelled to Haridwar for the Kumbha Mela and encountered the Aghoris and Digambars. He was fascinated by their strange esoteric lifestyle. When the news reached his father’s ears about Raman exploring the Aghori way of life, his brothers left for Haridwar immediately. It was a herculean task for them to find Raman among the huge gathering of devotees. At last, when they saw him he was in a mood for nothing. He neither resisted nor made any objections. He smelled of ashes and cannabis. They couldn't accept his present situation. They left for Kerala the next day. After reaching the house, to the horror of his brothers, their father started hitting him with his belt. They tried to dissuade him. Raman felt the seething pain of the belt tearing through his skin. He felt helpless and ashamed. He couldn't complete his studies. His dreams were shattered. He was not allowed to go out without the knowledge of his belligerent father who constantly cursed and abused him with words. His brothers ‘ got into prestigious government services, got married, and had kids and families of their own. But   Raman became a thorn in the side of the entire family. They tried to avoid him on every family occasion. He became an outcaste in his own family. His father's abuses and torments started getting on his nerves and one day he gathered the courage to face him. He lashed out at his father for making his life miserable. He cried, screamed, shouted and even tried to hit his father once. He was caught by his mother who slapped him instantly. He left the house at that moment never to return. His mother kept on calling his name, 
“ My Son Ramu. Don't go away. Please come back. Don't leave your mother. My son, Ramu... Ramu”. 
Her words of appeal made him cry inside out. But he was determined to go, escape from the hard clutches of his father. He left for Mumbai, did odd jobs to survive, made some money and came back to his hometown after 8 long years. 
During this time he had broken off his relations with his family, the death of his father was unknown to him. But he didn't feel a tinge of sadness about the loss of his father but rather a relief. He hated his father by the time he left for Mumbai. His mother was left in the care of a home care nurse much to his surprise. His brothers had brought lands, built houses and shifted with their families. Their ancestral home started to deteriorate. When he came to visit his mother after eight long years he was taken aback seeing his mother. She became thin and frail, with no hair on her head, playing with a plastic toy parrot. She didn't remember him, got annoyed and became grumpy seeing a stranger at home. The nurse at last broke the silence and said, 
“ Are you Raman, Janamma’s son? “. “ Yes I am, “said Raman in a heavy voice. “
Your brothers said you left the house and committed suicide. Your father after hearing the news of your death news collapsed on the floor. He suffered from a paralytic attack and was bedridden for two years. I took care of your father now your mother. She is suffering from Alzheimer's disease. She remembers nothing. Not even her name.” 
said the home nurse sans feelings. 
Raman got up from his chair, moved towards his mother took her hands and pressed them against his face. His eyes became dazed with tears. He kissed his mother on her forehead, left the room and sat on the charpoy of the verandah. Unfortunately, his mother remained oblivious to the moment. The home nurse came looking for him and asked “ 
Are you alright brother?”. He remained silent for some seconds. “ Does my brother come and visit her? “ asked Raman. “
They visit their mother once a month to take her to the hospital. An auto driver Kuttan brings vegetables and provisions. In case of any emergency, I will inform the neighbour Shantha Akka. She has a landline in her house.  Other than these short visits nobody bothers to come here.” 
said the nurse. Shankar sat there for some time, then left. He started visiting his mother daily. On such a visit he met Shankari with Sharada for the first time at a bus stop. This became recurrent as they were studying in an institute providing teacher training. Even Shankari started noticing him. Soon they had their first smile, first meeting, first talk. For all their firsts Sharada became a pleased watcher. Slowly and steadily their relationship grew stronger, and then it became the talk of the town. Shankari’s parents though financially low gave her a good education. Shankari and Sharada aspired to become teachers, but fate had other plans. Bhaskaran Nair a retired headmaster, a friend and confidante of Soman came to visit Raman at his home. Seeing Bhaskaran Nair from a distance Raman stood up and welcomed him warmly. He sat in a chair. 
“Hey Raman what are you up to? How is Janamma? And what about your love story? “ he looked at Raman with a strict demeanour as if a father would. Raman smiled with an uneasy shyness which is alien to him. 
“Uncle, it is high time I speak about her I mean Shankari. Yes, I love her.. No, we are in love…. Yes, I want to marry her.  We want to spend our lives together. Can you help me? I can only rely upon you Uncle. You know because I have none to take care of” 
He spoke with moisture in his eyes.  Bhaskar Nair looked at Raman, smiled and said,” 
Let me talk to her parents.” 
The marriage was a simple ceremony held in the nearby temple followed by a tea party. Her parents were flat broke but they were ready to give her hand to someone. At least she gets saved from this necessitous life. Her marriage saree, thaali was offered by Raman himself. Ramani and Shankari did not live a life in the fast lane but both remained significant others to each other. Sarada saw her son Mani who came to take her home along with him after work. Sarada wiped her tears and said “ Mani can I stay a bit longer today? I think Raman is nearing the end of his life. Shankari needs me my son.”. Her son looked at Shankari sitting on the chair with her head leaning against the wall. He had known her since childhood. Mani said 
,” Amma we both must stay by her side. Let us be together in this”. 
Sarada nodded. She looked at Sankari who was sitting on a chair with closed eyes leaning her head on the wall. Sarada knew she was powerless to steer the direction of the wheel of her life. What after Raman? . This question was haunting her since Raman’s health condition worsened. His brothers considered her a thorn in their side. She took a deep breath and walked towards her. She saw Raman’s brothers coming out of the doctor’s cabin. After some time, two doctors, three nurses and a compounder went inside the ICU. Sharada realised what was happening inside. Raman’s fate is sealed. She said a silent prayer to herself. Divakar called Mani to his side. They talked for hardly 3 minutes. Mani came back, looked at Sharada and said,” Amma his body will be taken to the crematorium. They just want to finish off the hospital formalities. They are not interested in paying any homage to him. Also, Chandran uncle asked me to take Shankari aunty to an old age home in Trivandrum. 
He will pay me travel expenses for that. 
Amma how will we tell this to Shankari aunty? asked Mani. 
“ Son give me some time to talk to her” said Shankari wiping her tears.
She sat down, with trembling hands she touched the hands of Shankari. She tried to wake her up. Shankari opened her eyes. 
“ Shankari everything is over. He is no more. His brothers are here. They are taking him to the crematorium. They even asked Mani to take you to an old age home.” Sharada said without looking into the face of Shankari. 
She nodded and sighed heavily. “ Amma it will take almost an hour for the official formalities to be completed. The bill is not yet ready” said Mani.
Shankari closed her eyes, sans tears. Her face was composed. She did not scream, yell, cried her heart out just leaned her head against the wall. It felt like ages waiting for the bill to get paid. After an hour or something Raman’s brothers, their kids and some men from the neighbourhood walked alongside a body. Nobody bothered to stop or ask Shankari to have a final look. Sharada and Mani looked at each other. His body passed them. She tried to wake up Shankari. It was when she touched her face that Sharada realised that she could never wake her up. Shankari entered her eternal rest with Raman to another. Thus without the last adieu, she left Sharada to mourn.

Title: आइना।
Content:
एक आईना मेरे मन का
वो स्वर्ण बिंब तेरे तन का

क्षण स्वर्ण रहा जो जीवन का ।
एक चाँद सदा चमके जग में
एकचांद तुम्हारे जीवन में
एकचांद हमारे मन में था
उन स्वर्णिम इच्छा के फल का।
जो पूर्ण नहीं वरदान हो तुम
जीवन का प्रतिमान हो तुम

Name: Dr Medhini Pandith
Title: The Woman in the Mirror
Content:
The Woman in the Mirror

Every morning, she looked into the mirror.

Not to admire herself.

Not to fix her hair.

Not even to see whether she looked tired.

She looked into it to make sure she was still there.

For years, the woman in the mirror had been familiar but distant. She knew the face—its tired eyes, its small lines, the smile that appeared whenever someone needed reassurance.

But she did not know the woman behind that face anymore.

She had once been a girl who wrote poems on the last pages of her notebooks. A girl who laughed too loudly, dreamed without permission, and believed that life would somehow make room for all her wishes.

Then life happened.

Responsibilities arrived quietly.

One by one, her dreams became later.

Her happiness became after everyone else is happy.

Her opinions became whatever you think is best.

Her tears became private.

And somewhere between being a daughter, a wife, a mother, a friend, and the person everyone called when they needed something, she stopped being herself.

Nobody noticed.

Perhaps that was the saddest part.

One Sunday morning, she stood before the mirror again.

The house was unusually quiet.

For once, nobody was calling her name.

She looked at her reflection and whispered,

“Who are you?”

The woman in the mirror did not answer.

Instead, she remembered.

She remembered the girl who wanted to write.

The girl who wanted to travel.

The girl who wanted to wear bright colours without worrying whether they suited her.

The girl who had once believed that being loved did not mean being needed every minute.

A tear rolled down her cheek.

She wiped it away.

Then, unexpectedly, she smiled.

Not the smile she gave others.

Her own.

She walked to the cupboard and pulled out an old box.

Inside were unfinished poems, photographs, a dried flower, a broken pen, and a notebook with her name written across the first page.

She opened it.

The first sentence she had written years ago was still there:

“One day, I will become the woman I dream of being.”

She read it twice.

Then she laughed softly.

“Maybe,” she whispered, “I don't have to become her.”

“Maybe she has been waiting for me.”

That morning, she did something small.

She made herself a cup of tea.

She sat by the window.

And she wrote.

Not for publication.

Not for praise.

Not for anyone else.

Just for herself.

The words came slowly at first.

Then they came like rain after a long summer.

She wrote about the years she had given away.

She wrote about the people she had loved.

She wrote about the dreams she had buried.

She wrote about forgiveness.

And finally, she wrote about beginning again.

When she finished, the sun had moved across the room.

She closed the notebook.

Then she returned to the mirror.

The same face looked back at her.

The same lines.

The same tired eyes.

Nothing about her appearance had magically changed.

But something inside her had.

For the first time in years, she did not search the reflection for the woman she had lost.

She recognized the woman who had survived.

The woman who had loved deeply.

The woman who had broken and healed quietly.

The woman who had spent years looking for herself in the approval of others.

And the woman who had finally come home.

She touched the mirror gently.

“I'm sorry,” she whispered.

The reflection smiled.

Not because the past had changed.

But because the future still could.

That evening, she opened her notebook again.

At the bottom of the last page, she wrote:

“I spent half my life becoming everything everyone needed.

Now I will spend the rest becoming someone I can love.”

She closed the book.

And for the first time, when she walked away from the mirror,

she didn't look back.

Because she finally understood something:

Sometimes finding yourself isn't about discovering a new person.

Sometimes it is simply about returning to the woman you were before the world convinced you to forget her.
