Name: Ayushman Gajendra
Title: An Empty Chair - A Mute Spectator of a Man's Life
Content:
An Empty Chair: A Mute Spectator of a Man’s Life
By Ayushman Gajendra

“Some objects don’t just occupy a place in our homes; they preserve the stories of the people who once sat on them.”
To every man out there—you must have sat on countless chairs throughout your life. But have you ever wondered what these chairs carry besides your weight? They carry countless memories, silently witnessing every chapter of your life.
A man’s journey with a chair begins in childhood, when he sits on it, solving sums or sketching something that fascinates his young mind. As the years pass, he grows into a student, completes his education, and eventually steps into adulthood. One day, almost unnoticed, he takes over the responsibilities of the family from the tired hands of his father, becoming its pillar and breadwinner.
Through every achievement and every failure, the chair remains his silent companion. It witnesses the applause that fills the room, the criticism that echoes within it, the sleepless nights, the silent sacrifices, and the countless battles fought without an audience.
Time moves on. His children grow up, build careers, and become busy with lives of their own. Ironically, the man who once spent his days working tirelessly for his family now spends his evenings sitting on that same chair, reading a book or simply waiting for the sound of the front door to open, hoping to spend a few moments with the people who once waited for him.
Sometimes they sit beside him. Sometimes they don’t. Not because they love him any less, but because life has become busier than anyone had imagined. In the twilight of his life, the chair becomes more than a piece of furniture. It becomes his place of reflection, gratitude, prayers, and silent conversations with himself as he waits for peace and salvation.
Through this piece, I simply wish to offer a different perspective on an empty chair. To some, it is just another object placed in a corner of a room. To others, it is a silent witness—a keeper of dreams, sacrifices, victories, disappointments, and countless memories that refuse to fade.
The house remains the same. The family remains the same. The chair remains the same. Yet the emptiest thing in that room is still the chair... because the man who gave it meaning is no longer there.

Name: Harshitha Peddinty
Title: The Man in the Portrait
Content:
For Three thousand years, the portrait had been waiting.

No one knew who had painted it, there was no subtle sign of it. It showed just a young man inside dressed like a prince, his dark hair falling across his forehead, with an innocent face staring beyond the canvas. No one knew why every family from different backgrounds who owned the portrait eventually found a reason to give it away.

The frame was old and royal, carved from dark wood and almost to size of an average human being. He had been painted with remarkable precision.

And for three thousand years, he had been waiting for one woman to notice.
His name was Artemis Kazamir II, Prince of GloomHaven. Only son of King Alaric Kazamir I and Queen Ingrid Kazamir. A kingdom surrounded by mountains, green forests and beautiful landscapes. where the people believed that love and kindness were greatest amongst all.

He had never believed in love, and since childhood he was totally opposed to the definition of it. All he thought it was a beautiful lie because they were afraid of being alone.

Not until he met Cecilia, a common girl from the same kingdom. Who earned her living for working in a floral shop. They first met at the royal ball event and Artemis noticed her talking to her friends, completely unaffected by the world outside.

Something about her, captivated his heart and erased the past idealogy on love. When he found her alone sometime later, he approached her. At first, they spoke about ordinary things, their favorite books, food and places they have travelled so far. 

As days were progressed, they began speaking about the future. Cecilia’s beauty and intelligence eventually attracted the attention of a rival king, Alexander Ravenspire. King of neighbouring kingdom of Noxterra. He wanted Cecilia to become his queen. 

She refused him and his proposal. His pride slowly turned into anger.

War followed.

Artemis fought for his kingdom and for Cecilia.
 
He returned from battle alive. 

But the victory meant nothing when he discovered that Cecilia had fallen terribly ill.

The doctors and physicians tried everything they could. Nothing worked. Her illness was rare, and there was no cure.

Artemis married her and spent her final days beside her at his mansion. He refused to leave her.

On the night before her death, Cecilia took his hand.

“Don’t look at me like that, my love” she whispered.

“Like, what?”

“Like, I am already gone” she chuckled softly.

Artemis tried to smile, but failed. 

Cecilia looked at him for a long moment.

“If there is another life, Artemis… I will find you.” 

He shook his head.

“I want you in this life, the next life and whenever there is another. I want you to be my side, in every universe.”

She smiled faintly.

“Then I will find you in the next one. I promise you, my love.”

Those were the last words she ever spoke to him.

Cecilia died the following morning in his arms while slept. Artemis could not accept a life without her.

He travelled beyond his kingdom in search of anyone who might know a way to bring the dead back to life. Either in a good or a bad way. 

His prayers were finally answered. Someone told him about a sorceress who lived alone beyond the southern mountains. They said, she knew magic older than the kingdom. And has an ability to turn even a stone into a living soul.
Artemis went to her.

He trusted her and openly confessed his pain. She promised him she could bring back Cecilia to life. 

But she demanded something in return.

He did not know that the sorceress had already fallen in love with him. She understood his devotion to Cecilia, and understood that there would never be a place for anyone else.

Artemis agreed without asking what it was.

“Marry me” the sorceress said.

He had been prepared to give her money, jewels and even half of his wealth. 

But she rejected them all. All she wanted was him. Only him.

Artemis politely refused and tried to leave.

The sorceress stopped him.

Magic filled the room. The candles went out one by one. 

Artemis felt something wrap around his body. He fought against it. The world around him disappeared slowly.

The last word he screamed was Cecilia.

When he opened his eyes, he was no longer feeling the ground beneath his feet.
He was inside a portrait frame.

Where he had become a beautiful Renaissance painting.

“You wanted Cecilia back” The sorceress stood before the portrait.

Artemis stared at her.

“Then wait for her. Wait until the woman you truly love is born again, finds you and loves you once more.” She placed her hand against the large wooden frame.
Artemis struggled inside the canvas.
 
But no one from the outside could see him. To everyone else, he was only a motionless figure in a painting.

“Free me!” 

The sorceress smiled. 

“Anyone who tries to destroy this portrait will become a stone and will never turn to a human.” she whispered a series of mantras and left him there.

The portrait remained.

YEARS BECAME CENTURIES…

The kingdom, it’s people and the architecture disappeared. Slowly, the old world replaced by the modern era.

The portrait passed from one family to another, carried through houses, palaces, estates and an antique shops too. Artemis lived them all. He watched children grow old. Lovers fall in love. Family argues. People celebrate. Greive.

And every time a woman approached the frame, hope rose inside him. 

Every time, it was not Cecilia. 

A child.
A woman.
A man.
Even a dog, cat or a bird.

Until, in a crowded antique shop in London. A young woman stopped in front of his portrait in awe.

Her name was Aurora Beaufort. 

And for the first time in three thousand years, Artemis felt the curse weaken.
Aurora noticed that his eyes seem to be looking directly at her. Without thinking too much about it, she bought it and had it delivered to her home. She lived alone in a small home and worked as a pianist. Her parents had in a car accident when she was five.

The next day, when she returned from the work. She noticed something strange.
The portrait looked slightly different from the day before. It was a subtle change but something she couldn’t identify it. She reached out slowly and touched the glass. 

A phone call interrupted her.

From that day on, she developed a habit of standing against the frame and watching the frame in the bedroom for few seconds. She felt warmth beneath it, every time she touched the glass.

It was similar to touching a living skin.

One night, around 11:30 pm. Aurora returned home exhausted after teaching piano lessons. She changed into comfy clothes and threw herself onto to the bed.

She fell into a deep sleep. Then she heard something in the room.

Aurora slowly opened her eyes. 

The entire room was dark and quiet.

A tall figure stood in front of the portrait.

Her heart began to beat faster. She rubbed her eyes to confirm she was awake, then quickly reached for the lamp beside her bed and switched it on. 

She froze.

The man inside the painting was no longer inside. 

He was standing in front of her. Aurora stared at him.

For the first time in three thousand years, he spoke.

“Please… don’t be frightened”

Aurora couldn’t move. 

The man stood only a few feet away from her. Maintaining a respectful distance. 
He looked exactly like the man in the portrait – dark hair falling across his forehead, dressed in the clothes of another age. 

Yet his live presence felt little different in outside of the frame. Just like a living doll. He looked exhausted and still tried to maintain a smile.

“Who are you?” Aurora’s whispered.

The man looked at her for a long moment.

“Artemis.”

Aurora took a step backwards.

“How did you get here?”

“I didn’t”

“I came from the portrait you own” His eyes moved toward the portrait.

The canvas was still there, but the man who had been painted upon it was gone.

“This isn’t possible” 

“I know” He gave her a faint smile.

Aurora didn’t know whether to scream, run or call the police.

Artemis took one step forward. She stepped back.

“I have waited a very long time to hear someone say that.” 

Her back touched the bedroom window. He was standing in front of her. They were only a few feet apart. Their breath replaced the room silence.

Artemis noticed the open window and quietly walked past her. 

“It’s very cold. You forgot to close the windows. Either you’ll catch a cold or you will find a stranger barging in here.” He chuckled and closed it.

She didn’t mind his words, instead she asked the only question that had entered her mind.

“How long?”

Artemis expression changed.

“What?”

“The portrait?”

“Three thousand years.” He sighed a little.

Aurora looked at him. Not with a pity, but with a pain.

He told her everything. The portrait. The curse. Cecilia. The promise she had made before she died.

Aurora listened in silence.

When he finished. She asked “Do you think I’m her?”

“I don’t know.”

The answer surprised her.

“I’ve seen thousands of women come and go,” Artemis continued. “For centuries, I have been transitioned into different places. Every time, a woman approached the portrait, I wondered if it was her.”

“Why weren’t you able to come out earlier?” 

“I’m not sure. But I think this place and you are somehow connected to the curse.”

“Me?”

Artemis nodded.

“When you bought the portrait, something changed. For the first time in centuries, I could feel the boundary weakening.”

“What boundary?”

“The one between the painting and the real world.”

Aurora glanced at the empty frame behind him.

“So you’re saying, I released you?”

“Not completely”

Artemis looked down at his hands.

“Then why did you come out?”

He looked at her.

“I wanted to see you.”

Aurora didn’t know what to say.

“It’s been three thousand years, Mister. You are probably mistaking me for your beloved.”

Artemis remained silent.

“I’m not her,” Aurora continued. “I’m pretty sure you’ve forgotten what she even looked like by now.”

A faint smile appeared on his enigmatic face.

“Maybe” 

Aurora raised an eyebrow.

“You still remember her?’

His voice was quiet.

“Her voice... her kindness..” 

He paused.

“What happened?’ Aurora expression softened.

His eyes met hers.

“But when I saw you…”

Aurora waited.

“I didn’t see Cecilia.”

“Then what did you see?”

Artemis smiled sadly. “Someone I wanted to know.”

Aurora looked away. 

“I’m Aurora” She extended her hand.

He shook it. Then he immediately pulled his hand back.

“What happened? Are you alright? You look stressed”

“It’s nothing. It’s just… it’s been so years since I felt a human touch” He whispered.

Aurora expression softened.

“Then how are you going to find her? You don’t even know if she is here. She might not even be born yet”. Aurora continued. “You have no idea where she is, and have forgotten what she looks like.”

“I know.”

“Completely clueless”

A faint smile appeared on his face.

“Your life has become a maze without a map or guide.”

He looked at her for a moment.

“The most accurate description of my current life.” Aurora smiled.

“Then maybe you need a guide.”

“You?”

“Why not?”

Artemis raised an eyebrow.

“You don’t believe I came out of a painting.”

“I still don’t” She glanced at the empty frame.

Artemis laughed.

Aurora smiled.

Then Artemis’s smile disappeared. He suddenly looked down at his hands.

“What is it?” Aurora asked.

He didn’t answer. 

A strange shiver ran through his body.

“Artemis?”

He took a step backward.

“Don’t come near me”

The air around him began to tremble. Aurora watched him in confusion. Something pulled him backwards.

Aurora instinctively reached for him. “Artemis”

The force became stronger. His body was dragged toward the portrait. The distance between them grew. In an instant he was gone.

Aurora stood frozen. 

The young prince was there again. Inside the frame. But this time, his expression was different. He raised his hand against the canvas.

Aurora walked closer and placed her palm against his. 

The glass was cold. 
His hand was warm.

Good night, Aurora. The sound came from the frame.

Good night, Artemis. She whispered.

And for the first time, the portrait no longer looked like a painting to her. It looked like a prison which captivated a person and all his memories.

The next morning…

Aurora woke up to the sound of birds chirping outside of her bedroom window. She rubbed her eyes.

“Artemis?” She walked toward the window.

“Morning, Miss Aurora. Did you sleep well?” The same man which came out of the frame was standing there again.

“How did you come back again?” 

“Well, these birds called me...” He looked toward the birds with genuine wonder.

“Seriously? Are you sure about how things work?”

Artemis looked at her, confused.

“I’ve been trapped in a painting for centuries. I’m still figuring it out.”

“So you don’t know when you can be pulled in or come back again?”

“Believe me, this is my first experience.” He smiled painfully.

“Then, how will the curse break?

“I don’t know.”

“You don’t know?”

“I would remain trapped until the woman I loved returned to me.”

“And what if she never does?’

Artemis looked toward the portrait. “Then I suppose I stay there forever.”

“Then we will figure it out.” Aurora didn’t like the situation.

“We?” Artemis looked at her.

“Yes, We!” She replied him back.

“Miss Aurora, I don’t want you to do that for me”

“Why not?”

“Because you shouldn’t have to”

Aurora looked at him, confused.

“What about Cecilia? Don’t you want to find her?”

Artemis was quiet for a moment. 

“I strongly believe, she has already been born. May be that could be the reason why I am able to come out often.”

Aurora looked at him. He smiled gently.

Days slowly turned into weeks. Weeks into Months.

Artemis began appearing more often. Sometimes he would come out of the portrait in the morning and spent sometime watching Aurora work. Other times, he sat beside her while she read, speaking endlessly, and asking questions about every strange thing he saw.

He had no idea how a phone work, he thought television was a magical box that transported people into other worlds.

He loved pasta, cheese toast.
He hated black coffee. 
“Friends” The sitcom had become his favorite show. 

Aurora taught him to play the piano and within a few days, he excelled in it. She bought him the modern clothes for him, and he would casually perform a fashion walk around the house. Making her laugh. 

Aurora found all of it amusing.

Their conversations became longer.

She taught him about the world he had missed and in return, he told the stories about the world he lost.

Neither of them spoke about Cecilia anymore. And Artemis never initiated the topic of his past with Cecilia.

One afternoon, Aurora left the house to buy groceries. Artemis remained alone, he would have accompanied her, but he can’t without knowing when the magic can pull him back in the portrait. 

Slowly, he reached into the pocket of his coat and pulled out a small silver locket. 

He held it for a moment before opening it.

Inside was a tiny picture of a beautiful young woman.
Cecilia.

His fingers gently touched the picture. Three thousand years had passed. Yet he still remembered her face, every memory, every tiny detail.

With a loud sigh, he closed the locket and slipped it back into his pocket.
He never told Aurora about it and he never intended to.

When Aurora returned from the grocery store, she noticed something was wrong. 

“Artemis?” 

There was no response.

She placed the bags on the kitchen counter and walked into the living room.
Artemis was sitting on the sofa, stern face. 

He quickly pulled his sleeve down over his wrist.

“What happened?”

“Nothing.” he tried to sound normal.

“You’re hiding something” Aurora frowned.

He pulled his right sleeve back. Aurora froze.

Dark, thin lines had appeared across his wrist. They looked like a paint-strokes beneath his skin.

“What is that?” 

“I don’t know.” Artemis looked down at it.

Aurora reached for his hand. He pulled it away quickly.

“Don’t. I’m fine”

“No, you’re not”

He didn’t answer. Aurora looked at his face. He was becoming pale.

“The curse” Her expression changed.

“How long has this been happening?”

“A few days.” 

“A few days? And you didn’t care to tell me? Have we become strangers again?”

“I didn’t want you to worry”

She stared at him angrily. 

“You’re terrible at it.”

Both his hands were already beginning to lose their color. Artemis knew what it meant. The curse was finally turning him back into his original form. A man in the painting.

“Artemis? What is happening? Tell me what needs to be done to make you normal.” Aurora startled.

“The only option…” He stood.

“What is it?”

His face became calm and composed.
 
“Go back to my home.”

“Home? This is your home. Artemis. This is your only home.”

He looked down. Gathering courage together to do what he had to do.

“Artemis? We will figure it out something. There has to be something…” She tried to calm him.

Artemis looked at her. His left side of face has become glassy, tiny cracks spread across in between. Ready to crack more with a single touch.

“Your face…” 

He immediately turned toward the dressing mirror. 

“I should go.” He reached for her.

She held him back.

“Thank you for everything, Aurora.” He swallowed. “There is nothing I can give you back except being grateful for what you did to me. I hope you will find the gentleman you’ve dreamed of. All the best for your adventures, without me…” He chuckled weakly.

She listened to him.

“I knew, my chapter is always going to end like this. This is the last chapter of my life.”

“No, it isn’t” 

“You are a very pure hearted person, Aurora. Never change for anyone.” His voice softened.

“Take care.” He turned away.

 The other side of face was slowly becoming glass with tiny cracks spreading across the skin.

He started running to his prison, the empty portrait.

Aurora ran after him. To stop him from entering the portrait completely. He bumped into a small cupboard in the middle and continued to run again. It’s too late, he was a way ahead of her. Artemis stepped into the portrait. Every other time, when he stepped back into the portrait, they both have a hope on the returning. This time, it was different. 

He could never come back to real world, unless a blessing or magic has been given. She had to adjust herself to watch him again in the portrait only.
The curse has become too strong, shielded him from every way of not stepping back into real world.

Aurora spent her days, to forget the traumatic experience. But she couldn’t. 
It haunted her, in dreams. She felt guilty for Artemis. She began to believe it had all happened because of her.

Every day, she spent hours of watching and touching the portrait. There were no signs of movement, no words came from the frame. Warmth of his touch was gone, too. 

All she felt was a cold glass.

One day, she couldn’t stay inside the house anymore. For the past few days, she had barely stepped outside of the house.

Her mind was filled with questions she couldn’t answer. 

Artemis. The Portrait. The locket. Cecilia.

She walked without knowing where she was going. Until she reached a quiet garden. 

She sat beneath a large tree and closed her eyes weakly. All she could remember was him. The moments they had created in short time.

“I don’t understand” She whispered.

“Some things are not meant to be understood all at once” A gentle voice came from behind her.

Aurora turned.

A man stood a few steps away. There was something unusual about him. He looked almost unreal, as if he doesn’t belong here.

He smiled at her.

“You are carrying a story that began long before you were born.”

Aurora stared at him. “Have we met before?”

“Maybe, in the old times.” He answered.

“Who are you?”

He didn’t answer. He raised his right hand and gently placed it over her head.
“Calm yourself. You will find all the answers. Do not be afraid of anything that you are going to enter.”

A strange warmth passed through her. Aurora blinked.

She opened her eyes. The man was gone already.

“Excuse me, have you seen an old man. He was present right here. A large brown scarf and gloves.” She stood up and asked the other people.

“No miss. We haven’t seen any old man here. You might have be dreaming.” A man responded.

All familiarity was replaced by a strange feeling of uncertainty, anxious and discomfort. 

She raced back home.

She pushed the door open and immediately looked toward the portrait.

“Artemis”

No answer.

Her eyes searched the room, suddenly. Then something caught her attention.
A small silver object was lying near the corner of the cupboard. She walked toward it slowly.

The locket. She picked it up. There was a small dent on one side. Her hands trembled as she opened it. 

And then she froze at the sight of it.

Inside was a tiny picture of a young woman. A beautiful young woman with familiar eyes, lips, familiar features.

Her breath stopped for few seconds.

The woman looked exactly like her. Every detail. The woman in the locket wasn’t someone who looked like her. 

She was her.

Cecilia. 

The moment her fingers touched it—

A flash.
A royal mansion.
Maids were combing her long hair in a bedroom.

Another flash.
Artemis.
A garden.
Artemis holding her hand.

Another.
Her own voice. “I will find you again, my love”
Aurora dropped the locket.

“No…No…No…” Another memory struck her.

A cold room, her own body lying on the bed. The last conversation happened with Artemis on the night before she died.

She pressed the locket against her chest. Closed her eyes. 
“I remember everything.”

She ran toward the portrait. “Artemis!”

No response. It’s been few weeks since he spoke to her. 

“Why you didn’t tell me?”

Again, No response.

“You knew, but you still chose to walk away.” She leaned her head against the frame.

There were no signs of him moving. 

“You knew I was Cecilia.” Tears filled Aurora’s eyes.

Nothing.

She placed both hands against the frame.

“Please… look at me.”

He didn’t move.

“I remember everything now.” 

Silence.

“I remember your proposal, the lake, our palace and the war. I remember you.”
Her voice trembled.

“I remember how much I loved you back.” She pressed her palm against the canvas.

“But I am not here because I’m Cecilia. I’m here because I’m Aurora.”
The frame began to tremble.

“We are destined for each other, Artemis. I know that.” Cracks slowly appeared across the portrait.

“Cecilia loved you then, but now as Aurora. Born again to find you. I am choosing you now as Aurora Beaufort.”

The cracks spread across the entire frame. The pieces of the frame fell to the floor with a heavy sound.

“I choose you.”

The canvas began to glow.

Aurora pushed her hand against the painting.

“Not only in this lifetime. In every life, I choose you.” The painted hand of Artemis, slowly moved beneath hers.

Aurora gasped.

“Artemis…”

She pushed harder.

“I found you as Cecilia. Now I found and taking you back as Aurora.” With all her strength, she pulled him toward her.

A burst of light filled the room.

Artemis fell forward into her arms. 

Aurora caught him carefully.

For a moment, he remained completely still. 

He slowly opened his eyes, They were no paint strokes or glass-like cracks on his face. 

He looked like a normal person. Could move his fingers, walk, and talk.

“You’re back.” 

The dark marks disappeared from his skin completely. 

“I left you in the past, but it doesn’t mean that you will leave me now.” Aurora whispered.

For a few seconds, neither of them spoke.

Aurora held him tightly as she could, afraid that if she could let go, he would disappear again. Artemis slowly lifted his hand and touched her face.

“Aurora…”

She smiled through her tears.

“You knew everything, didn’t you?”

Artemis lowered his eyes.

“Yes”

“Then why didn’t you tell me?”

He was silent for a moment.

“Because I knew what Cecilia meant to me. I didn’t want that weight to become yours, I didn’t want you to become someone you weren’t. I want you to be you now are.”

Aurora looked at him through her tears, confused.

“You were her. But you were also never her. You have your own identity. A different life.”

He gently touched her face again.

“You had your own life, your own dreams. I didn’t want you to wake up one day and think you had to love me because of a promise made three thousand years ago.”

His voice trembled.

“I wanted to know you as Aurora. I did. All I wanted you to choose your life first.”

“You are selfish, Artemis.”

Artemis smiled quietly.

Aurora listened to him.

“I never wanted your past to make your decision and become present for you. Now I am alive all because of you. Because you decided that happen. Even if you chose to walk away from me, I still accept it.” His voice softened.

“Even after waiting for three thousand years?”

He reached for her hand.

“Because after waiting that long, I learned something.”

“To leave your own people?”

“Love is not forceful thing to do. It’s chosen. It should grow from the heart, Not from the mind.” He looked into her eyes.

Aurora held his hand tighter.

“And I chose you.” She whispered.

Artemis smiled and pulled her into his arms.

This time, there was no curse remained. No portrait. No boundaries. No years of waiting anymore. 

Only two people who had chosen each other.

Years later, Belle stood before a small audience at a book reading for her newly published novel.

“Where did you get the inspiration for this story?” A little boy raised his hand.
 
Belle smiled.

“Someone I love”

She looked toward the two elderly people sitting together in the front row. The old man held his wife’s hand. 

The audience applauded.

Beside them sat a young, handsome man. Belle’s husband.

Later, during the book signing, Belle opened a copy of her novel and signed it on the first page, which says.

“Because some stories are not finding about each other. They are about choosing each other.” She finished signing the book and closed it gently. 

Handed it back to boy with a smile.

After the event, Belle walked toward her family.

Her husband was waiting for her.

“You are wonderful,” he said.

“You think so?” Belle smiled.

“Yes, Because I know so.” He teased her.

Behind them, The same old couple who sat on the first row, Belle’s parents - Artemis and Aurora watched them, with quiet smiles.

“Love may bring two people together, but choosing each other is what makes them stay.”

THE END

Name: Richa Tiwari
Title: Dulhan ke mann ki baat
Content:
एक दुल्हन के मन की बात
आज आईने में खुद को दुल्हन बने देखा तो दिल ने धीरे से पूछा
“क्या सच में अब जाना होगा?”
ये वही घर था जहाँ मेरी हँसी बड़ी हुई, 
जहाँ माँ की यादें अब भी दीवारों में सांस लेती हैं।
जहाँ पापा की आवाज़ आज भी शाम के सन्नाटों में सुनाई देती है, 
और जहाँ हर कोने में मेरी अधूरी बचपन वाली ज़िदें पड़ी हैं।
आज उसी घर से मुझे विदा होना है।
लाल जोड़े में सजी हूँ,
 हाथों में मेहंदी भी है, 
माथे पर सिंदूर का सपना भी… फिर भी ना जाने क्यों दिल काँप रहा है।
नई ज़िंदगी का डर आँखों में चुपचाप उतर आया है।
क्या सच में कोई अजनबी घर मेरा अपना बन जाएगा?
क्या मैं वहाँ भी इतनी ही खुलकर हँस पाऊँगी?
क्या मेरी खामोशियाँ कोई समझ पाएगा?
या फिर मैं बस रिश्तों को निभाते-निभाते खुद को कहीं पीछे छोड़ दूँगी?
दुल्हन बनना सिर्फ सजना नहीं होता,
 ये धीरे-धीरे अपने ही हिस्सों को छोड़ना भी होता है।
आज जब सब मेरी मुस्कुराहटों की तारीफ़ कर रहे हैं, 
कोई नहीं देख पा रहा कि आँखों के अंदर एक छोटी सी लड़की डरी हुई बैठी है।
वो लड़की जो अभी भी चाहती है कि कोई आकर कह दे “मत जाओ… यहीं रह जाओ।”
लेकिन ज़िंदगी रोकती कहाँ है किसी को।
तो आज मैं अपनी यादें समेटकर, 
अपनी माँ की दुआओं को दिल से लगाकर, 
एक नए सफ़र की ओर बढ़ रही हूँ।
डर भी है… आँसू भी हैं… लेकिन कहीं ना कहीं एक छोटी सी उम्मीद भी है
कि शायद इस बार किस्मत मुझे टूटने नहीं देगी।
                                                                     ऋचा (Hymn)

Name: Harshad Pandit
Title: A Shunned Maverick!
Content:
A Shunned Maverick! 

His life, rules and tis’ own norms
In sinister minds, vengeful storms
Beguiling aura, guiding deceptive veils
Setting the tone for assiduous trails

Success to possess its glory and story
Manifests through envy, jealousy, and gory
Demeanour of a deceitful vile
Treachery the sword, bullet the guile

No invites to parties, picnics, to vibe
Denial of a jingo, an erstwhile jibe
Together they savaged, with elan
Notoriety, a trait of their clan

A maverick made to pay his price
Destiny, cruel fate, rolled it's dice
Eschewed by friends and at work
Repugnance of a hateful shirk

No time to cringe, no time to dirge
Fun-n-frolic, no more the urge
Forlorn, solitude comrades for life
Ready to face life's every strife

Maleficent stares ignored and thwarted
Unwanted paths not trudged, but parted
Nonconformist to remain all times
Spendthrift to save every dollar and dimes

Can ye dare to shake and swallow? 
In the dirt to make thee wallow
Care about thee, thine alter ego
Ensures maverick his heydays, morrow

Name: Jahnavi Muralidhar
Theme: Learning to love yourself after hating yourself
Title: An awkward first date (Me and myself).
Content:
Silence stretches between both of us as we sit together for a coffee date.
This silence is really loud, and, my thoughts seem a lot louder, this just feels awkward
I can't really cherish the moment when its with you, it feels different, a little uneasy
I've hated you for so long, I've sometimes worked against you, I've hurt you
I've personally run a blade across your tender skin, I've despised you inside and out
I want you to be someone else, I want you to behave differently! I want someone strong, confident, muscular, productive. I want someone who can lift me easily.
I want someone who takes care of themselves every single day.
I want someone who is happy.
And you don't even brush your teeth daily, and you don't even shower.
You're like a stick and so incredibly skinny.
You shout at your parents and friends and you hurt them sometimes.
But here I am, and here you are, so I guess we're willing to try again?

This feels really awkward and uncomfortable.
"We're so far apart." You tell me. "We're literally miles away. How do we meet at the same page, ever?"
"It's okay." I tell you. "We'll just take one step forward every day, just forward instead of back, and one day, we'll meet on the same page."
I hope my sincerity shines through in my actions, even if this doesn't feel amazing to you at first. Maybe its uncomfortable.
But I prepared this coffee date table for you and chose the cloth of your favourite colour. Maybe your thoughts are racing and you're not fully in the moment.
But its okay, even if its not exactly how I hoped it'd be.

I really want to take care of you.
I really want to cherish you and love you the hardest during your worst moments
You told me you're afraid of pain, well, in pain I want to look after you really well
Maybe it might hurt less, eventually, I'll keep trying
The first date is really awkward, it feels uncomfortable, and what are we even doing?
I awkwardly take sips of my coffee just to break the ice, and you keep staring away.
But at least we both managed to sit down, and try together.
And if we try enough times, maybe it wouldn't be awkward at all.
We're meant to be together in this lifetime and we have our whole lives ahead of us.
One day at a time, and I hope that eventually when I try, try and try again
One day it'll hit you, and one day we might laugh together at a joke
And one day we might even meet at the same page, the version of each other we both wanted to see
We're just going to try, and eventually, I'm going to be comfortable with you.
I know you already, I just feel like I don't love you. But one day, eventually
We'll meet each other at the same page.
We'll not feel awkward anymore.
The silence will still exist between you and me, but, it won't hurt.
One day.
But for today, let's just take one step forward.

I wish you were someone else, but, while you become that person
I'm still going to love you just the same.

Name: Babita Paul
Title: Growing Up
Content:
One fine morning,
It knocked my doors,
Unbothered and naive I stood;
Listening to the chatters of the neighbourhood.

I was rushed to bathe,
Declared impure,
Some blushed I was a "woman" now.

My mother stood as if some lightening struck,
My sister taught me the ways,
I was ordered to stay in my place,
Contaminated I was, is what she said,
I stood there unbothered and worried now.
I was told my fingertips must never wander there,
They drew borders long enough to ache for care,
My father learned to love from a distance,
For seven days of forbidden existence.
My classes were missed,
The heart brushed through the roof,
Waiting for someone to declare the silence,
I now stood bothered and bruised.
The secret laid brutally open,
The world had now taught me its ways,
As though time had now forgotten me,
I stood now caught between hope and fear.
Was this the end, I asked,
As if, some brutal truth remains unmasked,
The absence grew, but so did my resistance,
I stood now restless and undone.

Name: Trisha Vallamkonda Prathap
Title: The Amusing Irony
Content:
Just thinking of you
Makes my day,
My love is so true
That it'll never sway.

When you look at me
Like the most precious gem,
I make a silent plea:
I want this in every realm.

My heart melts at your smile,
My lips curve in your presence.
I know our bond isn't fragile;
I can fight the world in your defense.

You invade my dreams,
Covering your face.
Oh, how cruel this seems;
You make my heart race.

By the time I wake up,
Your voice that echoed in my ears—
Like a beautiful mashup—
Amazingly just disappears.

How are you there without being there?
How do I see you without seeing you?
I am fantasizing, I swear,
Yet I know everything I imagine is you.

It's an amusing irony:
I know you without knowing you.
It's just that one day destiny
Will make me meet you.

Name: Ayushman Gajendra
Title: The Last Person You Say Goodbye To
Content:
THE LAST PERSON YOU SAY GOODBYE TO
By: Ayushman Gajendra

“Some goodbyes teach us many things without words.”

Goodbye. The word itself feels heavier, doesn’t it? Ever wondered how it feels when your loved ones bid goodbye? Let’s meet Reyansh, a child who deserves every happiness in life, yet is deprived of the same.

One day, he was standing near the school gate when his eyes fell on children coming to school on their expensive gear cycles. He looked at his old cycle, then looked up at the sky and asked in a disappointed voice:

Reyansh: “Main hi mila tha aapko gareeb banane ke liye??”

Someone patted him on the shoulder. He turned around to find his classmate, Shreyas.

Shreyas: “Oye!! Class nahi jaana kya tujhe??”

Reyansh (coldly): “Hmm... Tu chal, main aaya......”

Shreyas noticed him looking at the gear cycles with a gloomy face and said:

Shreyas: “Jo bhi bol bhai, jo mazza pedal maarne mein hai, woh mazza gear cycles mein kahan....”

Reyansh: “Chal chal, late ho raha hai class ke liye....”

They entered the classroom, where a bunch of students were sitting with their gear cycles and considered themselves superior to others.

One of them taunted Reyansh.

Ravi (laughing): “Dekho bhai log, kaun aa gaya. Ab ye normal cycle wale bhi baithenge humare saath....”

Shreyas replied coldly:

Shreyas: “Kyu Ravi, normal cycle wale insaan nahi hote hai kya?? Kabhi chala kar dekho normal cycle, phir bolna......”

Ravi: “Haan, hote hain na... gareeb.....”

He started laughing with his friends, to which Reyansh replied:

Reyansh: “Haan bhai, sab teri tarah golden spoon ke saath paida nahi hue hain na.....”

Ravi (furiously): “Kya bola be tune???”

Reyansh: “Kam sunayi deta hai kya?? Aur haan, jab khud ke paison se koi cheez kharidega na, tab uski keemat malum padegi tereko......”

Ravi and his friends left furiously.

Shreyas: “Kya baat hai bhai..... Ekdum muh band kar diya uska....”

Reyansh: “Nahi bhai.... Bas reality check de raha tha usse.....”

Years passed, and their friendship grew stronger day by day.

Then came the day they least wanted—the farewell.

Reyansh hugged Shreyas and said:

Reyansh: “Bhai, pata nahi kab mulaqat hogi phir. Yaad toh rakhega na mujhe....”

Shreyas: “Pagal hai kya? Tu jahan bhi jaa, main hamesha yaad rakhunga tujhe....”

One day, after getting rejected from his dream job’s interview for the final time, Reyansh felt disappointed and went to a nearby tea stall to have a cup of tea and some cigarettes.

Meanwhile, a voice came from behind:

“Iski aadat kab se, Reyansh??”

Reyansh looked behind to find that the voice belonged to none other than his old school friend, Shreyas, who was serving chai there.

Reyansh: “Abe tu yahan??? Kaise bhai.....”

Shreyas: “Mera chhod, tu bata. Kya hua? Nahi hua interview clear??”

Reyansh: “Chai de bhai, aur ek sutta bhi....”

Shreyas: “Chai toh mil jaayegi, par sutta toh nahi milega tujhe.....”

Reyansh: “Sutta kyu nahi milega???”

Shreyas: “Bas mana kar diya toh maan le.......”

Reyansh: “Thik hai, par chai toh pila apne haath ki, jaise school mein banata tha.....”

Shreyas (smiling): “Tujhe yaad hai meri chai???”

Reyansh: “Bhool gaya? Humara deal tha ki agar kuch nahi hua toh chai ki tapri kholenge dono bhai.....”

Shreyas went and came back with two cups of tea. He was about to sit down when Reyansh said:

Reyansh: “Itne dino baad mila hai tu, aur phir bhi door baith raha hai mujhse..... Ruk, main bhi aaya neeche...”

Both had many fun moments together, and finally, when they were about to leave, Shreyas suddenly fell unconscious.

Reyansh: “Kya hua hai doctor isse? Ye achanak behosh kyu ho gaya???”

Doctor: “Inko Stage 3 lung cancer hai, aur kuch hi din bache hain inke paas.....”

Reyansh (teary-eyed): “Koi toh rasta hoga na isko sahi karne mein??”

Doctor: “I am sorry, but we can’t do much.....”

After some time, Shreyas regained consciousness.

Reyansh: “Kab se hai ye???”

Shreyas: “Kya???”

Reyansh (teary-eyed): “Ab toh sach bol de bhai......”

Shreyas: “Bhai, mujhe koi badi bimari hai kya?? Bata na....”

Reyansh: “Tujhe lung cancer hai, woh bhi 3rd stage......”

Shreyas (shocked): “Kya??? Majak mat kar yaar......”

Reyansh: “Sach bol raha hun bhai....”

Shreyas (gloomy): “Kitne din ka mehman hu main ab?? Kya kaha doctor ne???”

Reyansh (emotional): “Chup saale...... Main puri jaan laga dunga tujhe bachane mein.... Kuch nahi hoga tujhe....”

For the next few months, he used all his contacts and even arranged the best doctors for his treatment, but in vain.

He breathed his last in the middle of a surgery.

One day, Reyansh found a video of Shreyas. In it, he said:

Shreyas: “Hiii Reyansh, Shreyas this side. By the time this video reaches you, I would have been gone far away from you..... Ab pata chala tujhe, main uss din tujhe sutta pine se kyun rok raha tha.........”

Name: Dr.Pradeep Babu
Title: " वैकुंठ छोड़ आओ गिरधारी "
Content:
" वैकुंठ छोड़ आओ गिरधारी "
वैकुंठ छोड़ आओ गिरधारी,
कलियुग हाथ पसारे।
सूनी आँखें, भीगे आँचल,
तुमको आज पुकारे।
दोष किसी का, दंड किसी को—
कैसा यह व्यवहार हुआ?
निर्दोषों के हिस्से आखिर,
क्यों इतना अत्याचार हुआ।
कहीं सफर में बस जलती है,
चीखें नभ तक जातीं,
माँ की आँखों के आगे ही,
उसकी दुनिया ढह जाती।
माँ की गोदी सूनी होती,
पिता खड़ा मूरत बनकर,
अपने ही उस लाल को ढूंढे,
आँखों मे सागर भरकर।
किससे पूछें न्याय कहाँ है,
किसको व्यथा सुनाएँ?
आँसू बनकर शब्द सभी अब,
आँखो से बहते जाएँ।
हे मुरलीधर! अब मत देखो,
मौन खड़े उस पार कहीं,
एक बार फिर मुरली बजाओ,
दर्द सुनाई दे रहा है हर कहीं। 
आओ कान्हा, हाथ पकड़ लो,
टूटे मन को थामो तुम,
जिसके घर का दीप बुझा है,
उस घर उजियारा भर दो तुम।
पुत्र पिता को घर से निकाले,
कैसा यह व्यवहार हुआ,
जिसने उँगली थाम चलाया,
आज वही लाचार हुआ।
पति-पत्नी के पावन रिश्ते,
क्यों बनते अब भार यहाँ,
जहाँ प्रेम के फूल खिलें थे,
क्यों उठती दीवार वहाँ?
वैकुंठ छोड़ आओ गिरधारी,
अब मत देर लगाओ,
मुरली की मधुर तान सुनाकर,
मानव को मानवता का पाठ पढ़ाओ।
वैकुंठ छोड़ आओ गिरधारी,
कलियुग हाथ पसारे।
डा. प्रदीप बाबू
देहरादून (उत्तराखण्ड)

Name: Aruna Chaturvedi
Title: मेरी माँ की साड़ी
Content:
माँ की साड़ी केवल वस्त्र नहीं होती, वह बेटी के बचपन, संस्कार और अनंत प्रेम की सबसे सुंदर धरोहर होती है।"
माँ को इस दुनिया से गए पूरे आठ वर्ष हो चुके है, लेकिन कुछ रिश्ते समय के साथ समाप्त नहीं होते, वे स्मृतियों में और गहरे उतर जाते हैं। आज सुबह से ही  मन बहुत व्याकुल था। आज मेरी बेटी की सगाई थी। घर में चारों ओर खुशियों का वातावरण था, पर मेरे भीतर एक अजीब-सी कसक उठ रही थी। आज यदि माँ होतीं तो सबसे अधिक प्रसन्न वही होतीं। माँ, मेरी बेटी को दुलारतीं, उसकी नजर उतारतीं, और अपनी साड़ी के पल्लू से उसका माथा सहलाकर आशीर्वाद देतीं।हर तैयारी में उनकी सलाह होती, हर रस्म में उनका स्नेह और हर मुस्कान में उनका आशीर्वाद।शायद इसी कारण सुबह से मन बहुत भारी था और माँ की याद बार-बार आँसू बनकर आँखों में उतर रही थी।
इन्हीं विचारों में डूबी मैं अलमारी तक पहुँची। धीरे से सूटकेस खोला। सबसे नीचे सहेजकर रखी माँ की प्रिय साड़ी निकाली। वर्षों बाद जब उस साड़ी पर हाथ फेरा, तो लगा जैसे कपड़े को नहीं, माँ के स्नेहिल स्पर्श को छू रही हूँ। पलभर में स्मृतियों के बंद दरवाज़े खुल गए और आँखों से आँसू बह निकले।
याद आया... बचपन में जब रात को नींद नहीं आती थी, माँ अपनी साड़ी का पल्लू मेरे हाथ में थमा देती थीं। पता ही नहीं चलता था कि कब उसी पल्लू को थामे-थामे गहरी नींद में सो जाती। जैसे उस आँचल में दुनिया भर की शांति समाई हो।
थोड़ी बड़ी हुई तो माँ जहाँ-जहाँ जातीं, मैं उनकी साड़ी का पल्लू पकड़े पीछे-पीछे चल देती। वह पल्लू मेरे लिए किसी डोर से कम नहीं था। विश्वास था कि जब तक यह हाथ में है, दुनिया की कोई भी कठिनाई कोई मुसीबत  मेरा कुछ नहीं बिगाड़ सकती।
पिताजी कभी डाँटते तो मैं भागकर माँ की साड़ी के पीछे छिप जाती। सच ही तो है, बच्चे के लिए सबसे सुरक्षित स्थान माँ का आँचल ही होता है। माँ यदि पड़ोस तक भी चली जातीं, तो मैं दौड़ती हुई उनके पीछे पहुँच जाती। लोग हँसते हुए कहते, "देखो,बछिया आ गई।" माँ को उनका मजाक चुभता और  वो मुझे समझती "बेटा, थोड़ा अकेले रहना भी सीखो।" लेकिन मेरी दुनिया तो बस माँ थीं।
आज वही सारी यादें चलचित्र की तरह आँखों के सामने घूम रही थीं। फर्क बस इतना था कि आज माँ का पल्लू था, पर माँ नहीं थीं।

"माँ..." बेटी की आवाज़ ने मेरी तंद्रा तोड़ी।
वह मेरे पास आई। मेरी नम आँखें देखकर बोली, "क्या हुआ माँ? आज तो खुश होने का दिन है।"
मैं चुप रही। तभी उसकी नज़र माँ की साड़ी पर पड़ी। उसने साड़ी उठाई और मुस्कुराकर बोली, "माँ, क्या आज मैं नानी की यही साड़ी पहन लूँ? मेरी सगाई है... नानी का आशीर्वाद भी तो मेरे साथ रहेगा।"
उसकी बात सुनकर मेरी आँखें भर आईं। मैंने प्यार से कहा, "बेटा, यह सिर्फ साड़ी नहीं है, तीन पीढ़ियों का प्यार है और साड़ी उसकी ओर बढ़ा दी।
कुछ देर बाद जब वह साड़ी पहनकर मेरे सामने आई, तो लगा जैसे समय आठ वर्ष पीछे लौट आया हो। वही सहज मुस्कान, वही सादगी, वही ममता... एक पल को लगा, माँ स्वयं मेरे सामने खड़ी हैं।
मैंने बेटी को कसकर गले लगा लिया। तभी भीतर से एक आवाज़ आई—"तू माँ को कहाँ ढूँढ़ रही थी? वह कभी तुझसे दूर गई ही नहीं। वह तेरे संस्कारों में थी, तेरी स्मृतियों में थी और आज तेरी बेटी के रूप में फिर तेरे सामने खड़ी है।"
उस दिन समझ आया कि माँ की साड़ी कभी पुरानी नहीं होती। । वह पीढ़ियों को जोड़ने वाला वह धागा होती है, जिसमें त्याग, प्रेम, संघर्ष और अनगिनत आशीर्वाद बुने होते हैं।उसमें वर्षों बाद भी ममता की वही खुशबू बसती है। सच ही कहा गया है—माँ चली जाती है, पर उसकी साड़ी में लिपटा स्नेह कभी पुराना नहीं होता। हर बेटी के लिए माँ का आँचल ही उसका पहला घर, पहली पाठशाला और जीवन का सबसे सुरक्षित संसार होता है।"

अरुणा चतुर्वेदी

Name: Paramita Das
Theme: A letter from a mother to her daughter
Title: Amader Chhotobela, (Our Childhood)
Content:
আমার স্নেহের ঐশী, 
    আমার চিঠি পেয়ে নিশ্চয়ই অবাক হচ্ছ। মোবাইল ফোনে তোমার সাথে প্রতিদিন কথা হয়। দেখতেও পাই  তোমাকে। কিন্তু মোবাইল ফোনে অনেক কথা বিশেষত অনুভূতি সবটা প্রকাশ করা যায় না। তাই এই চিঠি লেখা তোমাকে। 
 তোমার স্বপ্ন পূরণ হয়েছে। ব্যাঙ্গালোরে বড় ফ্ল্যাট ভাড়া করে তুমি আর তোমার বন্ধু আছ একসাথে। অল্প বয়সেই অনেক রোজগার করছ। একটা ফ্ল্যাট বুক করে ফেলেছ  এত অল্প বয়সে শুনে ভাল লাগল। কিন্তু মাঝে মাঝে বল তোমার খুব ‘স্ট্রেস’ হচ্ছে, ‘হতাশ লাগছে’। তখন খুব চিন্তা হয় । দূর থেকে বুঝতে পারি না তোমার মন খারাপের কারণ। তোমরা আধুনিক হয়েছ, বেড়ে উঠছ। যুগের সাথে তাল মিলিয়ে চলছ। তোমরা ‘জেন জেড’ প্রজন্ম। আমাদের থেকে অনেক এগিয়ে অনেক দিক থেকে। কিন্তু তবুও খুব সহজে এত হতাশ হয়ে পড় কেন তোমরা ?বন্ধুর সাথে অমত হবে, অফিসের বস কোনদিন তোমার কাজের প্রশংসা করবেন, আবার কোনদিন করবেন না। কেউ তোমাকে পছন্দ করবে, আবার কেউ করবে না। এটাই তো স্বাভাবিক। কালকে আই ফোন কিনে কত খুশি ছিলে তুমি!! 
                       “মনেরে আজ কহ যে ভাল মন্দ যাহাই আসুক সত্যেরে লও সহজে”।
 কে বলেছেন? আমার চিরকালের প্রিয় বন্ধু, গুরুদেব রবি ঠাকুর। পড়ে দেখ কবিতাটা। ইন্টারনেটে পেয়ে যাবে। কবিতার নাম “বোঝাপড়া”। 
  আজকে আবার বুঝলাম প্রচন্ড মন খারাপ তোমার।  
  জানো, আমাদের সময় তো মোবাইল ফোন ছিল না কিন্তু মনে অনেক আনন্দ ছিল। আর আনন্দের উৎস ছিল বিভিন্ন ধরনের বই। বিশেষতঃ শুকতারা, আনন্দমেলা। ছোটবেলায় যখন প্রথম মানে বুঝে বাক্য পড়া শিখে গেছি, তখন শুকতারা আর আনন্দমেলার প্রতি আকর্ষণ তৈরি হল। সেই সময় সুকুমার রায়ের কিছু গল্প পড়ার অভ্যেস থাকলেও শুকতারায় বাঁটুল দি গ্রেটও পড়তাম। তখন আমাদের মতো সাধারণ চাকুরীজীবি প্রায় সব বাঙালির ঘরে ঘরে আনন্দমেলা আর শুকতারা ছোটদের জন্য আসত। মনে হয়, আমার সমসাময়িক অনেকেরই প্রথম পড়া কমিক্স বাঁটুল দি গ্রেট। বিশেষত আমরা যারা বাংলা মাধ্যম স্কুলে পড়তাম, এই দুই ম্যাগাজিন আমাদের ছোটবেলার সঙ্গে আষ্টেপৃষ্ঠে জড়িয়ে ছিল।
  তখন আমাদের মতো বাঙালিরা বিশাল ধনি ছিলেন না। আমরা যাঁরা পূর্ববঙ্গ ছেড়ে এসেছিলাম, আমাদের তখন প্রখর জীবনসংগ্রাম — তা মূলত আর্থিক। কোনোক্রমে মাথা গোঁজার ঠাঁই জোগাড় করে থাকা। কোনোক্রমে হলেও অন্তত তিনটে কামরার বাড়ি বা ফ্ল্যাট ভাড়া করতে হত। মা, বাবা, ভাই, বোন, দাদু, ঠাকুমা, পিসি, কাকু, কাকিমা নিয়ে বড় সংসার। উনুনে কাঠকয়লা দিয়ে রান্না হত। আনন্দের উৎস বলতে ছিল আকাশবাণীর নাটক। টিভি তখন আসেনি বাড়িতে। লোডশেডিং হত প্রতিদিন এবং অনেকক্ষণের জন্য। লোডশেডিংয়ে যতক্ষণ হ্যারিকেনে তেল থাকে, ততক্ষণ পড়াশোনা। তারপর লোডশেডিংয়ে ঘ্যানঘ্যান করতে করতে ঘুমিয়ে পড়া। তখন অভাব, অনটন ছিল ‘কিন্তু স্ট্রেস’, ‘ডিপ্রেশন’ হতাশা, কষ্ট এই কথাগুলি প্রতিদিন শুনতে হত না। জন্মদিনে কেক হত না। জন্মদিন উপলক্ষে সারাবছরে একদিন ক্যাডবেরি খেতাম। আমাদের সামনে কেউ চকোলেট আইসক্রিম খেলে মনে করতাম ওরা বড়লোক। তাই এটা ওরা খেতে পারে। আমরা ‘বড়লোক’না এটা শুধু জানতাম। কিন্তু এত সাধারণ জীবনযাত্রার মধ্যেও বাড়িতে প্রতিদিনকার স্টেটসম্যান পত্রিকার বাইরে শুকতারা, আনন্দমেলা আসত নিয়মিত। খরচ কমানোর জন্য এগুলি কখনও বন্ধ হত না। রেডিও ছাড়া আনন্দের উৎস ছিল এই কমিক্সগুলি। স্কুলে আমার সহপাঠীরা সবাই এই কমিক্স পড়তে ভালোবাসত। এই নিয়ে কখনও দ্বিমত হয়নি। অনেক সময় স্কুলে এই কমিক্সের বই নিয়ে যেতাম। হাঁদার দুষ্টু বুদ্ধি দেখে কেউ দুষ্টু হয়ে যেত না। বরং গল্পের শেষে দুষ্টু ছেলেরা শাস্তি পেত, সেটাই প্রভাবিত করত। ভালো কাজ করে বাঁটুল দি গ্রেট প্রশংসা পেত, তাই আমাদের সকলকে আনন্দও দিত। শুধু ঈশপের গল্পই কি নীতিবোধ শেখাত তখন? তা বোধহয় না। বাঁটুলের গল্পের মধ্যে দিয়েও দুষ্টের দমন, শিষ্টের পালন শেখা যেত।
   যদি মনখারাপ হত বা শুধু পড়াশোনা করে একঘেয়েমি আসত তবে বাঁটুল দি গ্রেট, হাঁদা ভোঁদা, নন্টে, ফন্টে, টিনটিন, গাবলু এসব পড়লেই মন ভালো হয়ে যেত। এত সাধারণ জীবনযাপনের মধ্যে এগুলি ছিল আমাদের আনন্দের উৎস। অনেক চাহিদা কিছু ছিল না। এগুলি পড়তে পড়তে একঘেয়েমি আসত না। নিত্যনতুন জিনিস লাগত না। তারপর কবে থেকে হাঁদা, ভোঁদার কমিক্স পড়া ছেড়ে দিয়েছি মনে পড়ে না। আর একটু বড় হবার পর, গোগল, সন্তু-কাকাবাবু, তারপর ফেলুদা আরও আরও অনেক লেখকের বই পড়তে লাগলাম। এইভাবে বই পড়ার যে অভ্যাস হল সেটা রয়ে গেল। আমাদের সময় তাই  ‘বোর’ লাগছে এই সব অনুভূতি হত না। এছাড়া গান শিখতে শিখতে গানকে ভালবেসে ফেললাম। 
 এখন তাই তুমি দূরে থাকলেও আমার বোর লাগে না। এখনও গল্প বই পড়ি। গান শুনি, মাঝে মাঝে দু কলি গাই নিজের মনে। মাঝে মাঝে লিখি বিভিন্ন বিষয় নিয়ে। এছাড়া আর ঘরের কাজ তো আছেই। বাইরে যে আত্মীয়রা ছিল আমরা তাঁদের চিঠি লিখতাম।
 তুমিও তো পড়াশোনায় ভাল ছিলে। মাঝে মাঝে মোবাইলকে বিশ্রামে রেখে বই পড়ার অভ্যাস গড়ে তোল। ই বুক হলেও পড়। গান শোন। আর মাঝে মাঝে আমাকে চিঠি লিখ, দেখবে অনেক না বলা অনুভূতি বেড়িয়ে আসবে। হতাশা, দুঃখ বেড়িয়ে আসবে। তখন আর ‘স্ট্রেস’ অনুভব করবে না। ইমেইল নয়। চিঠি লিখ।

Name: Aiman Musheer
Title: DISTANCE FROM ONESELF
Content:
Look at yourself,
then look a little deeper—
Did you see something?
Did you feel something?
Or did you simply let yourself
drift away from you?
Why did you not stop her,
the one who was once familiar to you,
the one who walked away
and stood at a distance,
as though quietly saying—
“I am still here.
Call me, and I will come.
Then why this distance between us?
Why did you push me away from myself?
Why did you leave me
with no choice but to become a stranger?”
Do you not remember
the person who once lived within you?
The one who understood your silences,
who could read your pain
before your tears ever spoke.
You did not lose her—
you simply stopped noticing her.
She is still there,
somewhere within you,
waiting for you to return.
After all,
can one truly ever be distant
from one’s own self?
It is only we
who become distant—
from the very soul
we carry within.

Name: Eric Paul
Title: निजी शिक्षक
Content:
मैं हूँ एक शिक्षक, पर सरकारी नहीं।
वेतन है कम, पर ज़िम्मेदारी वही।
जाने का समय तो तय है,
पर लौटना निश्चित नहीं।

उम्मीद से बढ़कर  है काम देना,
चाहे भूल जाओ साँस लेना।
घर पर आकर भी पीछा न छूटे,
नामुमकिन-सा है छुट्टी लेना।

छात्रों के संग न निजी नाता,
अभिभावक का फ़ोन सताता।
समय का न लिहाज़ रखता,
बेवक्त वो चैन चुराता।

कहने को तो इज़्ज़त है बड़ी,
पर घर की माँगें अधूरी पड़ी।
सबके जीवन में हरियाली लाऊँ ,
पर खुद की फ़सल सूखी पड़ी।

क़िस्त, किराया, बच्चों की पढ़ाई,
दस तारीख़ तक करते हैं चढ़ाई।
बहुत शर्माती है तनख़्वाह आने में,
उसकी देरी ने धड़कन बढ़ाई।

मुश्किलें मुझको सिखाती हिम्मत,
ईमान की न लगने दूँ क़ीमत।
पहचान बनाता हूँ मैं सबकी,
हाँ, मैं हूँ एक निजी शिक्षक।

Name: NITIN KUMAR SAIN
Title: बेतुकी ज़िंदगी
Content:
ज़िंदगी का सबसे बड़ा बेतुकापन शायद यही है—
हमें जीवन जीना पड़ता है,
जबकि जीवन किस तरह जिया जाएगा,
यह तय करने का अधिकार
हमें पूरी तरह कभी मिल ही नहीं पाता।

जीवन की परिस्थितियों में
कुछ भी, किसी भी क्षण बदल सकता है—
और आदमी फिर भी
आने वाले कल को
आज बनाई गई योजनाओं में
बाँधता रहता है।

नियति कोई आहट नहीं देती,
बस एक दिन
हमारी बनाई हुई सारी निश्चितताओं के बीच
कुछ ऐसा घटा देती है,
जिसकी हमने कभी कल्पना तक नहीं की थी।

और फिर जो आज था,
वह आज नहीं रहता—
उसके साथ बदल जाती हैं
कल को लेकर की गई वे सारी योजनाएँ,
जिनमें हमने आने वाले दिनों को
कितनी सावधानी से बाँध रखा था।

कुछ रास्ते,
जिन पर चलने का हमने मन बना लिया था,
अचानक रास्ते नहीं रहते;
कुछ मंज़िलें,
जिन्हें हमने अपने कल का नाम दे दिया था,
हमारे लिए रह ही नहीं जातीं।

फिर उसी बदले हुए आज के भीतर
हम एक नया कल सोचते हैं,
नई योजनाएं बनाते हैं,
नई निश्चितताओं का सहारा लेते हैं—
और शायद यही जीवन की विडंबना है
कि जिस वर्तमान की ज़मीन पर खड़े होकर
हम भविष्य बनाते हैं,
वही ज़मीन
किसी भी क्षण
हमारे पैरों के नीचे बदल सकती है।

फिर भी आदमी
कल की तरफ़ देखता रहता है,
उसे अपने हिसाब से गढ़ता रहता है,
उसके लिए रास्ते चुनता रहता है—
शायद इसलिए नहीं कि
उसे अपने भविष्य पर पूरा विश्वास है,
बल्कि इसलिए कि
बिना किसी निश्चित कल के
आज को जीते रहना
शायद इंसान के हिस्से आया
सबसे कठिन बेतुकापन है।

Name: Bijoyalaxmi  Mohapatra
Title: PRATIBHA’s LONGING
Content:
PRATIBHA’s LONGING

Pratibha was a regular housewife, living in Kharagpur, West Bengal. 

One day, Pratibha and her family went out for dinner at a local family restaurant. They were celebrating her elder daughter's academic success. The very next day, she puked, her legs were swollen, and she had to be admitted to the nearest hospital. Doctors diagnosed her with “Bilateral Hydronephrosis”. It meant her kidneys were failing and she needed medical treatment urgently. Their world came crumbling down. The daughters were yet to be settled, and her condition was worsening. Will she survive? What if she dies?

On the doctor's advice, her husband took her to CMC, Vellore. Vellore is a town in Tamil Nadu surrounded by hills. The temperature and climate are pleasant, ideal for patients suffering from dreaded diseases. Deciding to move to Vellore for treatment wasn’t easy for them. Her husband had to arrange money, seek leave from work, and above all muster the courage to take her to this alien town for treatment. They were scared and didn't know how to handle the whole process. Once they reached there, things fell into place. The doctor said it was curable, but the treatment would take 6-8 months.

She was admitted; many tests were done, and doctors inserted catheters to drain the fluid accumulated in her kidneys. The reason for kidney failure was still undiagnosed. They gave her medicines and monitored her Urea and Creatinine levels every day. Doctors advised that once the Urea and Creatinine levels were down, they would perform surgery. Slowly, Pratibha was becoming weaker day by day. She could no longer walk without support. After her surgery, her wound did not heal; it was still oozing blood. Her stomach swelled, and she vomited. Her intestine had collapsed. During the surgery, they found a tumor on her intestine that was damaging her kidney. The tumor was cut, and that led to the collapse. Within 15 days, they had to perform another surgery to rectify their mistake. Pratibha was not allowed to eat solid food. She could have only two spoons of water if she felt thirsty. She was given a formula intravenously instead of food. 

That night, Pratibha dreamt she was swimming in the pond in the backyard of her village home. She drank a lot of water. She saw the faces of her deceased parents, her brother, and her sisters. The next morning, she asked her husband, " Did anybody from my family call to enquire about my health? I miss them very much. Her husband and daughter were losing hope as they saw her suffer every day. They felt helpless.

By then, she had completed 6 months of hospitalization, and she felt weak, lonely, and demotivated. But a few families dealing with similar situations had bonded with them. There was a family from Bangladesh. Rahim Shaikh had accompanied his nephew for his Kidney treatment. His daughter had married him a few months ago, and he fell ill. His nephew was a well-built, handsome boy, but now he had to live with a urine bag attached for the rest of his life. He was very worried about his daughter's future. He often visited and talked to Pratibha’s husband. He said I had an elder sister who looked exactly like her. Fair complexion, 5 ft 2 inches. But she is no more. Your wife reminds me of her. He would visit them every day, talk to Pratibha, and ask about her health. At times sit quietly next to her bed and read a prayer in Urdu. 

There was another family where a 20-year-old girl, Susmita, underwent surgery on her limbs. A small tumor was removed. She and her mother often spoke to Pratibha and her caregiver daughter. They found solace and hope in each other's company. When Susmita recovered, her mother went to a famous temple in Vellore and offered prayers. On the day of her discharge, Susmita’s mother touched Pratibha's forehead with a flower from the temple and prayed for her early recovery. She said, " Once you go back, I will call you. We are sisters for life. We are more like family now. Do not forget me.” 

Soon, Pratibha recovered and returned to Kharagpur. They realized how amazing it was that Human suffering had bonded so many strangers together at the hospital. Pratibha said to her husband, " My brother ignored me when I was in pain. Instead, God sent me a brother from Bangladesh. God was kind enough to send me a sister from Kolkata. Now I have two families to go to.”

Name: A.R.Annal
Theme: Time and how we lose it and blame everything else while we remain at fault.
Title: Ticking clock
Content:
I Sat down quiet
Looking at the clock on the wall making the sound
Click.
Each minute too fast to catch like a
Blink.
Time is running away, I know
Yet I find myself trying to keep it locked away in a dismay.
You don't know the value,
You shouldn't waste it,
But how do I taste it?.

I Sat down quiet again
Looking at the ticking clock,
As if it held answers to all my faults
Deep down I knew it was all the fruit of my heart.
Everytime when I hesitated when I knew I need to start.
"Is time running away?"
"I don't know" i said as I continued running away from it.

Name: Pulak Patra(Asher Graves)
Title: De-evil's Pentagram: Cyclic Grief
Content:
Grief is a cyclic spell.
It loops.
It spares none.
It’s inevitable.
This poem follows through each stage of grief like a spell—
Untamed.
Unbound.

— The First Point —
Burdens are discreet, like shadows they creep,
Disguised as excuses, seeping in deep, shaking core beliefs.
Should I care about them? I don’t feel the need.
I am not in the deep!
I am not a mere sheep!
I am so close to the…
To the conclusion!
To the reconstitution!
Indeed.
I know what I’m talking about.
For I’m not weak.
I do not bleed.

— The Second Point —
Reenacting noir violence as something prophetic,
Proportional to the lethargy and lapse in memory.
Craving the caves as they
cave in melancholy.
Framing the phrase as they
phase in verbally.
Adding the daze as they
laze in physically.
Blaming the place but they
can’t pace gently.
Desperate to bridge the gap so they chose to race profusely.
Virtuous! Do I need to be?
What care should I’ve about them?
for I don’t feel the need!
They never did care for me anyway—
even when I was drowning in deep!!
But now when I am so close to the…

To the rejuvenation!
To the resuscitation!
Hitting rock bottom?
suddenly they care for me? 
Shite!
Indeed.
I know what they’re talkin’ about.
For I am not weak.
And I refuse to bleed.

— The Third Point —
Knowing the taste of fear they
made a note mentally.
Faster they ran to master it tactfully.
Dreaming how good it will feel in the end eventually.
Wisdom in hand, performing weird dance
tearing what little chance, they lost the hand!
for the house always wins regardless of the circumstance!
Misery loves company as the house loves common populace
Few serene hopes and you get them where you want!
Frustrated lads everywhere yet none questions house’s morals!
None brave enough to question their command.
Alas!
Beaming with delusion they fell prey to cult activity.
Worshiping day and night, swallowed by ritualistic vanity.
Failure in results added fuel to the aggressive analogy.
Looking for meaning brewed life into inhumanity.
Myth or not, this bizarre journey
will lead to a distorted ending.
But who’s sane enough to reject the voluntary heretic ascendency?
Forget transparency—lowered guards breeds corruptancy.
If I shall care enough, will I be granted a reprieve?
I can no longer swim this deep.
Almost there…
For the happiness.
For the redemption.
Away from the slip.
Tell me I’m not too late.
Tell me I’m doing great.
Tell me I’ll be okay.
Tell me I’ll win.
Tell me I won’t bleed.

— The Fourth Point —
Defence is irrelevant when you’re deemed unworthy;
Among these foolish creatures none have a slither of sanctity.
Only the demonic hymn echoes through the monastery.
Surviving Curates prayed for mercy.
The massive inflow of broken kin bought tears in the building.
The priest stays silent though, which enrages the victims.
They heckle at him and start grumbling.
Seeing the teary-eyed priest, they
Stopped for a moment.
Renegades demand necessities but caregivers chew on nothing.
And unlike several personas presently living.
These plausible gremlins do realise their wrongdoings.
But despise the inevitable homecoming
Yet are tied by its musing,
Alluring, amusing, sense of deluding
Delusion of a happy life.
 
Helpless and bound, the victims cry out for safety.
The last remanent of hope collapses under a misfit
The priest pondered:
Whatever should I even care for,
now nothing holds a meaning.
Am I drowning?
Am I swimming?
Am I breathing?
Am I dreaming?

I’m lost in the deep.
So close to the…
To the silence.
The oblivion of reckoning.
Wish I was strong enough to change a thing.
But I was weak from the beginning.
Thus, I bleed.

— The Fifth Point —
Eerily, the bewitching entity distorts it with ranting—
The entity, namely self-pity, flourishing,
Birthed by burdens, fed by the masses’ frolicking tendencies.
Exuberates an overwhelming aura, seemingly understanding.
Careful—this is the seed of self-loathing.
"Verily, must it be prompting?
Must it be coaxed with hoaxes, propelling redundancy?"
You think no one resisted this hypnotic screeching?
In this abominable world brave warriors took a standing.
Vexed and perplexed, anxiety stacked,
emotional wrecks, Reaper’s back,
falsehood’s flag, regrets that drag,
weaker to help.
Yes, I care.
Care, because I know what it brings.
Care, for we all swam through the Chanel of the deep.
Care, for I am so close…
To the end and the beginning.
Care, for now I know the meaning.
Care, for I know what I have become.
Neither weak
Nor strong.
Care, because I must bleed.
---Closing of the Circle---
Cause—
Burdens are discreet, like shadows they creep…

-Pulak Patra(Asher Graves)

Name: Sky
Title: Search of Light
Content:
Dark skies. Stars drifted far away from me. 

I rubbed my eyes and looked again. I found myself standing beneath them, so close to the heavens, as though only a flight of stairs separated me from the stars and the moon. 

The moon was huge– as huge as the night. Its pale whiteness wandered across the heavens and spilled over the distant lands. 

The distant lands, somewhere in those lands of others. I stood alone, alone in the green, green field. 

Short, well-kept grass pressed neath my naked feet. 

Yet no light ever reached my soul. 

Under that clear sky, my chest ached. My heart cried. There was no wound upon me, nothing that could explain the pain, yet it was unbearable. 

Still, I stood. 

Still. 

And I let the cold wind carry my soul away. 

Away, 

Somewhere far from this world. 

To a world filled with lights. With colors. With the things that could give meaning to my life. 

In search of things. I had wandered through the world of others in search of things. 

For any light. 

For any color. 

Anything at all. 

But I failed. Failed to fill my soul. 

The ache returned. It crawled back into my soul. 

I stood in the field, field green field.  

Nobody was there to held my cold hands. 

And share their warmth, some warmth with me. 

Yet my search had never stopped. 

My eyes, scrutinizing gaze of mine.  

Moved through the field to find something. 

Something that can take me away. 

My eyes found nothing. 

But my ears heard something. 

A gentle lapping. 

The whisper of a stream against the sleeping earth, singing a soft and distant song. 

Like a call of a whale. 

I turned toward it. 

And I let the song carry my feet. 

One step. 

Then another. 

Soon, my eyes found lights drifting upon the river. 

Something within my soul loosened. 

I ran toward them. 

As I neared the river, I slowed. 

The water lay before me like a mirror. 

My eyes softly moved through the river. 

There, they were. 

The stars. 

The stars I could never reach were resting within the river. 

Everything I had searched for was there– 

a canvas of the sky, painted in the darkest hours of moonlight. 

I stepped closer. 

My eyes lowered. 

And then I found myself standing within the river, surrounded by stars. 

All those lights. 

All those colors. 

Everything I had ever longed for. 

The water trembled. 

My reflection broke into a thousand pieces and merged with the lights I had spent so long searching for. 

I stepped back. 

My heart rose within my chest. 

Even beneath the coldness of the night, sweat gathered upon my skin. 

Everything I needed was there. 

Within the river. 

I gathered myself. 

Every fragment of strength that remained, I collected. 

Every last piece of courage, I gathered into my crying heart. 

The gentle wind brushed against me. 

For a moment, it felt as though it whispered that everything I had ever wanted would soon be mine. 

I stepped toward the river. 

My legs resisted. 

You know that resistance. 

The kind that comes when some part of you knows that everything is about to end –and believes that perhaps it will end for the better. 

The tears of the last cry.   

The sorrow of the last smile. 

The coldness that will vanish for something better. 

Yet, you know that resistance to not lose the ache,  

Cause it feels so familiar. 

Yet I made the choice.  

The last visit to a life that had grown too cold. 

And every bit of past asked me for a– 

A warm heart. 

A smiling face. 

Someone to make you feel alive again. 

Someone with whom you could share your laughter. 

Your joy. 

Every part of my soul, my blood, my skin— 

Everything within me wanted only one thing. 

To live. 

To live a life that meant something. 

Something good. 

But somewhere along the way, I had lost something precious within myself. 

The ability to feel. 

The joy. 

The wonder. 

The dreams that once belonged to me. 

They had all vanished, slowly, quietly, until I became nothing more than a body carrying the remains of a life, I no longer recognized. 

Everything I had ever counted on had become a disappointment. 

I stepped into the river. 

Because I had nowhere to go. 

The ground disappeared beneath my feet. 

And I fell. 

The water rushed around me, takes me within its shoulders. 

It hugged me with a coldness that almost felt warm. 

Its touch was strangely gentle. 

Almost heavenly. 

My legs had nothing to stand upon, yet I felt as though something carried me toward the sky. 

My hands had nothing to hold, yet I felt suspended in the air. 

My body sank into the depths. 

I opened my eyes. 

The lights were gone. 

No stars. 

No moonlight. 

Nothing remained; of the beautiful world I had seen above. 

Everything I had found within the river— 

vanished. 

Faded. 

Dissolved. 

Broken. 

Darkness. 

Perhaps this was the truth. 

Whatever I touched, I took its light away. 

Water rushed into my nose. 

Into my mouth. 

My body fought for a breath. 

My hands moved on their own. 

My legs thrashed like a frightened creature searching for land. 

Even though I had wanted an end— 

something within me refused it. 

My soul screamed for life. 

I moved my hands. 

Back and forth. 

Again. 

Again. 

But the shore was too far. 

I sank deeper into the river's arms. 

My final breaths escaped like bubbles, drifting upward without me. 

Like the stars. 

Like everything else I had ever lost. 

I sank into the abyss. 

I was like a bird without wings, falling through a world where nothing could carry me. 

My eyes slowly closed. 

Only if my life had not been meaningless. 

Only if there had been something more to hold on to. 

Perhaps I gave up too easily. 

Maybe I should have moved my hands harder. 

Maybe I should have screamed for help. 

Maybe— 

Maybe I should have tried my best. 

But it was too late for regrets. 

Wasn't it? 

I was falling into darkness. 

I was fading into darkness. 

Everything stopped. 

I was no longer falling. 

I was floating. 

Somewhere. 

Somewhere beyond the darkness. 

My eyes opened. 

I was deep beneath the river, far from the shore, far from the world I had belonged to. 

Yet I was surrounded by light. 

Stars twinkled around me. 

Everywhere. 

Colors moved through the darkness like living things. 

Warmth surrounded me. 

It was as though the sky itself had fallen beneath the river, and I had awakened among the stars. 

I reached out. 

My fingers brushed against one. 

It twinkled and drifted away, shy as a girl turning from a stranger. 

I swam after them. 

Not to hold them. 

Not to possess them. 

Only to admire their beauty. 

They moved around me, close enough to touch. 

Yet something inside me remained empty. 

The ache in my chest had disappeared. 

But the emptiness remained. 

A hollow place had been carved into my soul. 

So, I swam onward. 

I was no longer searching for the stars. 

I was searching for something that could feel mine. 

Then I heard it. 

A gentle wave. 

The whisper of a spirit in the depth, singing a soft and distant song. 

Like a call of a whale. 

A brightness far greater than the faint blue radiance surrounding me. 

Somewhere in the distant depths. 

I turned toward it. 

And there, within the blue darkness, I saw a whale. 

It moved through the water like a creature born from the heavens. 

Blue light surrounded its enormous body. 

Tiny sparks shimmered along its skin. 

I froze. 

I could only stare. 

I could only hear. 

Its calls, that make my heart beat again. 

The whale’s eyes were towards mine. 

And it was swimming toward me. 

There was no fear in its eyes. 

No anger. 

No sorrow. 

Only gentleness. 

Only love. 

I remained still and let its light reach mine. 

Let its beauty find mine. 

Let its soul find mine. 

It came closer than anything ever had. 

The whale moved its fins. 

Soft waves traveled through the water around its enormous body. 

Then it stopped beside me. 

Its light spread across my body. 

Across my face. 

Into my soul. 

And something within me warmed. 

A warmth I had forgotten for long. 

Slowly, I raised my hand. 

The whale's eye was enormous, shining like a pearl on the ocean. 

It moved its tail gently, closing the distance between us. 

I reached toward it. 

To feel. 

Not to possess its beauty. 

To feel it. 

For the first time in a long while, I found something. 

Something that’s not mine, not belong to me yet I find peace as it was. 

The whale lowered itself. 

Its head drifted away from me. 

For a moment, I thought it was leaving. 

Then it's back rose beneath my legs. 

It carried me. 

Its body became my ground. 

Gave me the support of a father, to stand over it.  

Gives me the warmth of a mother, when I clench to its back 

I clung to its back. 

My eyes grew heavy. 

The whale carried me upward. 

Toward the surface. 

Toward the shore. 

The stars slowly disappeared behind us. 

Yet I no longer needed them. 

I had found something else to hold on to. 

The divine whale carried me somewhere. 

Somewhere, maybe somewhere we call afterlife... 

My eyes were closed. 

Its gentle call echoed through the water like a song. 

A song of gentleness. 

A song of care. 

The very things I had spent my life searching for in others. 

Before I surrendered to sleep, I understood something. 

I had found something I should have known earlier. 

Somewhere within the depths of the river. 

I had found something; it was too late... 

It was time for me to sleep. 

Closed eyes, the body was floating somewhere upon the surface of a river. 

The body had traveled somewhere far, far from its world. 

The river waves pushed it. From shore to shore, bank to bank. From one place to another, like a boat with no man, no soul. 

The night was empty. No stars. No moon. 

The whale was gone. 

There was only the body. 

It drifted onward until the river finally carried it toward its end. 

Slowly, the waves pushed the body toward the edge. 

Then, as though the river itself had decided where it belonged, it carried the body onto the land. 

Nights passed. Days dissolved. 

The mud dried. 

Wild grass grew around the body. 

I opened my eyes. 

I opened my eyes and looked back at the river. 

Under the moonlight, it was empty. 

The miracle had vanished. Whether I had woken from a dream or from something else—I didn't know. 

For a moment, I wondered if it had ever existed, and even I... 

I stood. 

Then I turned my back toward the river. 

Toward the lights I had once believed were everything. 

And I walked. 

Into the grass. 

The field was no longer the neat green meadow I had entered. 

The grass had grown wild now, rising almost to my hips. 

The path ahead was dark. 

Uncertain. 

I could not see where it ended. 

But I kept walking. 

Because I had learned something in the darkness. 

A path did not have to be visible for me to take the next step. 

I walked toward the middle of the field. 

And there— 

stood a home. 

My home. 

Its roof was dark beneath the moon. 

Its walls were scarcely touched by the pallid light. 

Beside it stood an old tree, its naked branches spread against the sky, each limb like the crooked hand of some forgotten watcher. 

Everything was quiet. 

Utterly quiet. 

I walked toward the house. 

Then I heard it. 

Laughter. 

Soft at first. 

Then another voice. 

Then another. 

Warm sounds spilled through the walls, breaking the silence that had followed me for so long. 

I stopped. 

My eyes rested upon the house. 

And for the first time, I smiled. 

I had spent so long wandering through the world of others, searching for light. 

I had searched the heavens. 

I had searched the river. 

I had searched the stars. 

But somewhere in the depths of that memory, when I had been on the back of the whale—the divine whale—I understood something. 

Perhaps the light I had been seeking was never meant to be found in the world of others. 

Perhaps I had carried a little of it all along. 

Fireflies emerged from the wild grass. 

One. 

Then another. 

Then dozens. 

Tiny lights flickered around me. 

I walked through the grass, making my own path toward home. 

The fireflies followed. 

Or perhaps they only seemed to. 

Either way, they lit the darkness before my feet. 

And behind the walls of my home— 

There was laughter. 

There was warmth. 

There was life. 

And for the first time in a long while, 

I walked toward it. 

And nothing was disappearing.

Name: Sakshi Singh
Title: The biggest lie I ever told
Content:
The biggest lie I ever told was that I wasn’t waiting for you.
Because the truth is… I still stop for a second whenever someone looks like you.
You left long ago,
but my heart never received the goodbye.
I learned to smile in front of everyone,
yet every night I silently grieve the life
we were supposed to have.
The cruelest part isn’t that you chose to leave
it’s that you left me with memories
that refuse to.
So yes
The lie is that I don’t wait for you anymore.
The truth is,
I’ve only accepted that you’ll never come back,
not that I’ve stopped hoping.
It’s the one that survives,
even after the person is gone.
